GURUVANIKAL · January 2002 · Volume 4
Malayalam source paragraphs GV4:P0001 to GV4:P0023
English line for line; each paragraph carries its Malayalam source number.

[GV4:P0001] Guruvani

[GV4:P0002] January 2002

[GV4:P0003] The path that we are currently implementing in Santhigiri is given by God. This is not something that has come in the past or will come in the future. We are only entitled to fulfill our duty of completing this path. There are many here who have come seeing me without even knowing me. I have not introduced myself by displaying miracles or performing magic tricks before you. If you do not understand this with your life, or rather your consciousness, I will not be able to do anything; this is the absolute truth.

[GV4:P0004] God has given us, that is, the human race, only what is absolutely necessary. What is our need? Only what is required for this Guru concept of ours. Everything else must depart from the world. Or, if there is anything that does not depart, it must be assimilated and worked out in alignment with this ideology. This is how it should be implemented. Our prayers and intentions must reach the end of the aeons. Billions of generations have come and gone in a traditional manner. The absurdities contained within them must completely end, and whatever needs to be absorbed into our Guru lineage must be sustained, shaped as God, and fulfilled according to God's will. Therefore, we should not create unnecessary noise in this.

[GV4:P0005] We must clearly understand what the formless and the formed entities are, and what the color of the form is. Suppose the color of the form is given a conceptualization in the Trimurti system. That conceptualization will only reach up to that point. In order to extend the concept to further distances beyond that, the position of Brahma in the Trimurti system lies in total confusion. It has been transformed into one with four Vedas and thus taken through various such platforms. It is not possible to study beyond this.

[GV4:P0006] Question: Even though he has been made into the master of the four Vedas, Brahma still stands as one of the Trimurtis, doesn't he?

[GV4:P0007] Guru: Yes. As the four-faced one. But that face does not exist. Instead, merely a figure has been drawn and kept.

[GV4:P0008] Question: Then what about saying that Brahma is the authority over all four Vedas, having been given the four Vedas?

[GV4:P0009] Guru: They have merely concocted all that. It is just like the concept of Ravana's ten heads. The one who drew it brought it into sound form. What can those who drew this and those who repeat it do about its temporal significance or karmic significance? Because he is four-faced, there is no duality. Everything is an illusion. It implies the absence of two, doesn't it? As long as there is no duality, what can humans do? So this is a lie. If there is something called non-duality, duality must also certainly exist.

[GV4:P0010] What all does duality apply to? The present situation is that it has been included only within the sequences of sound forms. It is the artists who studied colors and played within the sixty-four arts that have brought about these circumstances. And then, everyone has tried to demonstrate it through logic. For example, there is no use in competitively arguing that such and such a preceptor has said it this way or that way. What have they done for the preceptor or for those who competitively argue? What do they have to offer other than the beauty of colors and the beauty of pictures? They can neither see it nor show it. This is just like the prancing of a good bovine. If one merely stands carefully and enjoys this bovine, which shows its ferocity and fluffs up its fur before taking a sudden leap, will that become the karma of the preceptor? Anyone can spout rationalism. How much of it can we actually grasp—this is a subject beyond our comprehension.

[GV4:P0011] As long as one does not know the course of karma that stands as the formless-and-formed, there is no point in offering any justification for it. The blunder that has occurred here stems from drifting away from the karma of the conceptual forms of the god and goddess. When it is said that the deity is both formless and formed, how can this formless position and formed position be discovered? The realm of our knowledge and experience has been convoluted in such a way that it cannot be understood even if seen. What we hold is a muddled education which assumes that everything is achieved with two or four visions of the Lord. What this education does is present the Lord and the Lord's Lord according to a vocabulary of sounds, giving them a form, and then sacrificing them to 'Swaha'. Everything is the Lord's illusion!

[GV4:P0012] To give shape to a sound pattern, the color of the plane from which that sound originates must be shaped. As that color is shaped, the diversity of hues must be formed. It is when this color is shaped that the absorptive dharma becomes complete. Instead of accomplishing such monumental tasks, our knowledge revels in merely speaking about the karma of some Treta Yuga, claiming it is complete, and standing in the position of that Yuga's perfection. This is the aspect that the people are unable to comprehend. If such a profound subject is tossed around like a ball in this manner, what can anyone do?

[GV4:P0013] Here, the loss of an entire Yuga occurs. If one Yuga is lost, nothing from the next Yuga can be grasped.

[GV4:P0014] Question: Can't it be corrected?

[GV4:P0015] Guru: Who will correct it?

[GV4:P0016] Question: Can't it be corrected by coming as a divine mandate?

[GV4:P0017] Guru: When it comes as a divine mandate, a complication also arises along with it. We have an understanding about interstellar spheres, don't we? There is the Earth, the changes in the solar system, and the specific karma brought about by time. This remains within the atmosphere itself. It is just that this nature of karma differs for different spheres.

[GV4:P0018] The nature of changing times stands formless. We must see what the karma that merges into the formless is. This is what is called Varna Dharma. We must know whether this color merges or not. If it merges, we must know with what and at which stage it will be merged. Will it do to merely chant 'Swaha' instead of that?

[GV4:P0019] Here, both men and women have vision. They see and perform all the things mentioned above. This is our subject. These children are seeing where the form ends, what all types of formed and formless entities exist in the world, in which color they all merge and stand as dharma, whose dharma it is, and what its extent is. These formless-forms and color-dharmas are all contained within a single form. Everything is just that. This is a Yoga.

[GV4:P0020] Speaking of Yoga, there are so many yogas mentioned by physicians. There are so many yogas mentioned by Yogis. To put it another way, 'Arimedadi Oil' is a yoga. Thus, every oil is a yoga. Every ghee is a yoga. Every decoction is a yoga. By combining which of these yogas can a special medicine be given for nerve pulsation? For that, the nerve blockage must be accurately determined. That nerve will subsist only in the measure of that life force. It will not stand otherwise. In the part called the nerve, it is maintained by being connected through veins and brought to dissolution through hair follicles. In this state, the rules of Yoga and the rules of doctrine have intermingled and gone awry, standing in a condition where nothing can be retrieved. The formless-form and the color-dharma have played out in this manner and become totally convoluted. The performer of karma who comes by divine mandate must be one who can rectify this.

[GV4:P0021] Missions always exist, do they not? They are present in all eras. There are missions spanning a century, and those that transcend it, allowing one to attain liberation by witnessing the rise and fall of this world. Therefore, simply concluding the mission of a century by asserting that both the manifest and the unmanifest are one and the same will not suffice. For instance, although doctors from various disciplines speak from within their respective systems, the core matter remains the same. However, none of them can control the trajectory of life. This is not something that doctors, or even thinkers or theoreticians, can accomplish. After doing everything possible, they can only step aside saying that they have done all that is humanly possible and that one should now pray to God. As for Vedantins, merely contriving various explanations does not mean they can define what 'Varna Dharma' is, or what the unmanifest and the manifest are. What is the 'Varna' of the deity or Guru spoken of in this manner? What is their 'Dharma'? This is where the aforementioned problem lies. Another aspect is that wherever one is ensnared by a demon, they remain stuck there. Similarly, wherever their disciple reaches a deity, they remain there. What a disciple must understand is in which of the manifest and unmanifest forms the Guru or the deity is absorbed. It is insufficient to merely state that they are absorbed in everything. Where the Guru is absorbed, how the Guru and oneself are unified, what the light of the Guru is, where all the light of the Guru exists, how many manifest and unmanifest forms are within it, and how many 'Varna Dharmas' exist—all these must be declared by the disciple upon seeing them. There are no other justifications for this.

[GV4:P0022] Among the nine planets, we observe three spheres. The rest are seen through the telescopic nature of physics. Seeing these spheres in this manner does not mean we have traveled to all of them. In reality, it is the unmanifest and manifest nature inherent in the planetary bodies that transports us to each sphere. Where does the Guru stand in that unmanifest form; where do they stand in the manifest form? Where does this Guru stand in the tri-guna karma of Tamasic, Rajasic, and Sattvic qualities—this constitutes the state of the Guru. This state must be realized by the disciple themselves. Offering other rationalizations for this will not suffice.

[GV4:P0023] Guruvani

GURUVANIKAL · May 2002 · Volume 4
Malayalam source paragraphs GV4:P0024 to GV4:P0044
English line for line; each paragraph carries its Malayalam source number.

[GV4:P0024] May 2002

[GV4:P0025] To bring even the smallest matters to perfection, one must traverse through numerous sorrows. Our ancient history is an acquaintance with such an experience. When we say 'ours', it is not just mine or yours, nor is it merely that of our ancestors. We are trapped in a lack of functional capacity, having completely missed the knowledge that has been evolving over millions of years. Numerous Gurus and prophets have come and gone over time in an attempt to rectify this. However, there was a lack of knowledge and experience to understand or impart this. This is the predicament that has afflicted us.

[GV4:P0026] There are many people who say that we have made some mistake. But if asked what this mistake is, they do not know how to answer. Where did the mistake occur, and how did it happen—this is what remains unknown. The truth is that neither our ancestors, who were theoreticians of karma, nor the preceptors and prophets who came to clear ideological confusions, were able to identify where the mistake occurred. As far as these preceptors are concerned, and consequently for us as well, this remains a completely unfamiliar action. We have drifted away in this ignorance. Therefore, we were unable to embrace Dharma. Dharma must be adopted with humility. Instead of doing so, we have not practiced humility beyond mere lip service. This lack of humility is experienced in various forms. One is caste. Another is religion and class. How did these castes, religions, and classes originate, and when did they emerge? How did the circumstances arise for them to constantly change in this manner?

[GV4:P0027] Theoreticians belonging to the Trimurti tradition posited ten incarnations. Apart from those, there have been many other incarnations. Now, incarnations are appearing countless in number. If incarnations appear in such immeasurable numbers, which one will we accept? That is one problem. Then, there are some who are characterized as followers of prophetic religions and guru-centric religions. But what is the greatness of time? What is the belief appropriate for the times? We lack the knowledge to understand this, elucidate it from those lineages, and move forward. This error did not occur just today or yesterday. We must investigate at least from the time of Lord Krishna to understand and act upon this predicament. Through Kamsa, we can understand that the divine will had a prior preparation for the arrival of Lord Krishna. Since the arrival of Krishna to this day, we have never been ready to respect and understand that history or to take up any aspect of that hardship and work selflessly. Following Lord Krishna, numerous Gurus have appeared all over the world.

[GV4:P0028] Science has today provided us with the knowledge that, similar to our concept of this globe, there are countless planetary bodies in this space. It is a limitation that once a piece of knowledge is discovered, it stagnates at the point of that knowledge. We do not contemplate how it occurred while standing upon the acquired knowledge. Now, each of you who has studied English considers Ptolemy to be one of the greatest thinkers. His disciples have also followed the very same path. However, the tendency to stagnate at the point of discovered knowledge can be observed here as well.

[GV4:P0029] We cannot succeed by incorporating an estimation of two thousand, four thousand, or five thousand years into the life of a great soul. Even mentioning four or five million years will not suffice. We must account for at least a Chaturyuga as a minimum. A Chaturyuga encompasses a span of over 4.3 million years. That itself is categorized into various Dharmas. However, we know nothing about it. If we proceed with the calculations formulated by the English or the Trimurti tradition, we will have nothing to convey to the coming generations.

[GV4:P0030] To grasp the magnitude of this error, we need to observe the emergence of many thousands of great souls. It is reported that two thousand four hundred and forty-four Gurus have arrived since the commencement of this Kali Yuga itself. If this many people have come within a mere five thousand years, how many millions must have appeared within this Chaturyuga? This remains a massive question mark for us. Only if we confront this question somewhere and seize some opportunity can we manage it.

[GV4:P0031] The only ones we can take as a foundation are the great souls. Among these great souls themselves, we must know whose history and records will provide a favorable environment for our inquiry. First, we must acquire an understanding of the Gurus who have evolved within the Trimurti tradition up to this day, as well as the trajectory of karma that has been born, nurtured, and perished within that lineage. However, there is a fundamental obstacle to accepting this. That obstacle is what the Trimurti tradition says about Swayambhuva Manu. We must understand that Swayambhuva Manu, true to his name, was self-created or originated in a self-born karmic process. But he has been arbitrarily linked as the son of Brahma. This is where the previously mentioned limitation arises. There is no method anywhere that details what must be done to eliminate this limitation.

[GV4:P0032] Our ancestors speak about Lord Rama. Or they speak of the history that has occurred within this Chaturyuga. But let us take a glimpse into the final days of all these great souls. This will cause us pain. God has given us the opportunity to witness the boundaries of the lives of numerous great souls. For this opportunity to reach you, it must stem from a center of faith. When we say a center of faith, it must be a place that recognizes what the Trimurti tradition and the Manu tradition are. The path to discover and rectify this is to begin from wherever the Guru lineage, the Manu lineage, or the Deva lineage extends and culminates. Instead, tying it to the Trimurti is the mistake that has befallen all the great souls.

[GV4:P0033] To explain how this initial mistake occurred, much would have to be said. It is not necessary here. We only need to know from that fact about Sree Krishna which we failed to understand. Sree Krishna was born in the Yadava clan. What is the karma that determined that this great man, who worked for the people, would be born at a specific occasion before his birth? What did it ultimately become even after he was born? We have never thought about this. Why? We have not even considered that it happened that way. Until today, the only action that has taken place is reducing everything to Vedanta through constant repetition, lingering on the phonetic sweetness of the letters, and ultimately tearing it apart through interpretation. This is what has been preserved as Vedanta. We cannot prove the truth from this Vedanta.

[GV4:P0034] Some speak citing Ramarajya as a model. In what manner have we perceived that great man who suffered so much, bringing him to the forefront? There is no one to clearly explain Rama's stance to us. If we consider all the people who have come since Sri Rama until today as a whole, we will understand that they are not the ones to be adopted in the dharma of this era.

[GV4:P0035] What currently exists is the twenty-eighth Chaturyuga of Vaivasvata Manu. Where did things go wrong in the meantime? Until today, efforts have been made to rectify what went wrong. Where the error occurred is exactly what writers and thinkers have failed to find despite their search. What is thus unattainable is beyond thought. How can that which is beyond thought be attained?

[GV4:P0036] If one envisions the solar system by standing in the karma of a visionary, the subsequent knowledge is whether the solar system is subject to the Manvantaras or something else. It is this knowledge that should rectify you. Such knowledge cannot be instantly transferred to us. It can only be imparted very gradually. For this, God should not be reduced to a mere sleight of hand. We must come forward to reclaim and observe the eras in which dharma could be practiced through life, and having seen them, rectify the mistakes within them and put them into practice. To undertake this, one must observe the course of karma that exists in four states: gross, subtle, causal, and effect. Then, one must also observe when dharma should emerge. Since it is a dharma of the time, the dharma of Kali must be examined specifically. One must observe what Kali is about, in whom the dharma to be undertaken according to the familiarity of Kali is vested, and how far that person has reached, or where they stand. The person implementing the Yuga Dharma must know all of this.

[GV4:P0037] What guidance should that person provide for us? Regardless of whether one is a demon, a deva, a sage, or an ascetic, they must advise on what error has occurred in the course of dharma up to this day, and what must be done to correct that error. There is no point in advising anything else. Whatever is said about the theory of Yoga, the theory of Karma, or the theory of Knowledge, none of it is something an individual can easily step into. Then what is that karma? It is observing the course of karma that has passed, grasping that karma, and correcting it. That karma is worthy enough for even your children to be accepted as a contribution to the world. There is no point in saying here that I should be exempted, that I am a liberationist, a rationalist, a scholar, a mute, or someone devoid of any knowledge, or an ignoramus. All these merely fall within the realm of your verbal rhetoric. No one should try to win by saying such things.

[GV4:P0038] We must remember the tragic predicament we have fallen into here. By talking about rationalism and liberationism, we are deviating from the course of dharma and from the thought of what all harmonizes within dharma. When this happens, there will be a deficiency in the amount of knowledge required to understand each era. Then, the karma written and preserved by scientists and Vedantins will occupy that space. This is an obstacle on the path to truth.

[GV4:P0039] Truth is none of these; it exists within each of us. The fire of the five elements is within us. There is fire in everything in the world. In the realm of knowledge where the five elements are blended, the growth of the life force is at a standstill. One must know what has happened to it and in which knot the life force is entangled. Knowing this is the hallmark of a visionary.

[GV4:P0040] How will this knot be untied? If the visionary is to untie that knot and give it to us, we must have the knowledge that we will receive everything through that visionary. What has happened in the past is foresightedness; if one waits idly thinking that everything will be obtained from it, it will not come. Such people will suffer the tragic fate of a life force devoid of vitality. This is not what I am telling you. In the course of karma where you grow as male and female, the karma of birth and death lingers in everything, even in a single atom. What is the karma that has operated and settled within this atom? Who must you become to reclaim this dharma? What should be the lineage of Gurus that has attained this abundance of merit, and what should the Guru be? You must see and realize this for yourselves. It cannot happen except through such a path of knowledge. This should not happen just in one or two children, not in one caste or religion, and not in any single species of living beings. This subject is about discovering the achieved realization of the course of life moving through all living beings. Through that achieved realization, where do we stand now? This should not be said by a person who has become deserving or qualified by seeing and experiencing it. You and your children are the ones who must say it after seeing it. Why would you say so? A vigilant nature has been given to me, which must be activated by comparing it with your past times, as well as the present and future times. Knowing what this waking state, dream state, and deep sleep state are, one must also observe what all yields in deep sleep. My birth and death have thus come into the course of karma, known, done, and caused to be done in this manner. This truth is not to be spoken to those who say truth does not exist, nor to those who say it does.

[GV4:P0041] In the course of dharma where the Earth, on which truth stands as the foundation, and similarly the eight planets stand together, how has this truth operated and settled? It is the Guru's obligation to show this. Only a disciple seen by a Guru should explain it to you. Others should not explain it. You must understand that this is the experiential aspect of truth. This is not a dharma mixed with intellect in the foolishness of stringing together fragments of Vedanta. It is not about the ignorance of the scholar or the scholarship of the ignorant.

[GV4:P0042] What is your capability as householders—who are to take up the responsibility of the future times having seen the three periods of time—to show how we can uphold dharma, and how will you take it up? Otherwise, this is not meant for an ascetic. Let the ascetic take it or not take it. There is nothing much to say about that. If the ascetic wants it, he will take it. Otherwise, he will discard it and leave. Let him do whatever. You need this. You and your children. Every one of you who is alive needs this.

[GV4:P0043] The path of the Guru is to know the predicament and the destiny of that soul, which repeatedly manifests with the good and the bad clinging to the righteous course of bygone times. I am speaking to you about such a path of the Guru. No one other than Sree Krishna has spoken about this path. Jesus speaks about this most beautifully. Vivekananda also speaks well about it. How will that become good through us? Vivekananda's conclusion is that the Devas convened a meeting in Devaloka against this. So what if they convened a meeting? Will this not disappear only if the Guru is someone who stays in Devaloka? If it is a Guru who resides in Devaloka, it will disappear. This is what has happened until today. This is being told to you now by placing such a condition before you. By growing through this condition, you must get any child you see. Otherwise, there is no salvation for you. I am not merely reciting this to you; rather, I am placing such a karma before you. Understand whether it is the truth or untruth by observing it, and learn to perform karma by fulfilling it. Also, see how charity and merit will reach us. Let us reflect on who we are in that humble karma where the merit of that charity has reached fortune. Each one should become a person for that. This is what I have to tell you.

[GV4:P0044] Guruvani

GURUVANIKAL · June 2002 · Volume 4
Malayalam source paragraphs GV4:P0045 to GV4:P0066
English line for line; each paragraph carries its Malayalam source number.

[GV4:P0045] June 2002

[GV4:P0046] To what shall we surrender and pray? We have passed down certain knowledge that came and went millions of years ago. At the same time, prophetic traditions, as well as Sikh, Buddhist, and Jain traditions, have emerged in such a way that it is impossible to know whether what has been passed down is right or wrong. All of these have been spoken in various languages in different parts of India. However, most people in India possess the experience of having worked steadfastly within the Trimurti tradition. Among these, they have also lived according to the doctrines brought by people of other religions. When each of these doctrines presents its own perspective, we may also feel that there is truth in it.

[GV4:P0047] We must understand one thing. How will the karma performed in the Treta Yuga or Dwapara Yuga be useful in the Kali Yuga? If there is a transitional nature today that is shifting towards the Satya Yuga, how can this karma be adapted for the Satya Yuga? India has more experience with this transitional nature of epochs. Although it exists to some extent in other lands, they articulate it in a different manner. There are doctrines in Western and Arabian countries that are propounded in various ways. However, none of these should be taken as exemplary in the Kali Yuga. Why? The Prophet's doctrine is one whose time has not yet ended. It can be carried forward for another ninety years. Yet, within this period, conflicts and quarrels capable of disintegrating it are taking place within it.

[GV4:P0048] Similarly, in the case of Hinduism, the knowledge of a transmission that has been passed down for many years is invoking a God who has been divided for caste and religion in various ways. We possess the ignorance of thinking that by speaking thus of caste and religion, only the God who fits within them is supreme. To remove this ignorance, many great souls came independently even in this Kali Yuga. The prophetic religions that came in the Kali Yuga arrived in such a manner. But we cannot recognize any of this. Therefore, we have proceeded with the attitude that everything is acceptable and good. However, we cannot fault any of this. This is because we have seen karmas that were performed appropriately in their respective times and yielded results.

[GV4:P0049] Are these results deserving of the liberation of our soul? Even if we agree that everything else is correct, all of these have the shortcoming that none of them is a karma entitled to grant liberation. Should we not then develop an independent mindset that claims the right to the liberation of the soul and allows each of us to become a part of the merit-acquiring karma?

[GV4:P0050] We are those who live here for a short time without knowing anything at all and then depart. In the meantime, people manifest in various ways—as those who live as fathers, mothers, children, wives, and husbands, as those who live by embracing asceticism, or, if none of these, as those who live desiring the worship of God. But we are merely unable to know what flaws have occurred in all of this. These karmas are as old as we are, making it impossible to know them.

[GV4:P0051] It has been more than five thousand years since Kali Yuga began. We, who cannot even study the history of these five thousand years, will never be able to study all the Yugadharmas that occurred previously and adopt a model of Yugadharma. Therefore, let us just know what we need to know concerning our lives. If we move on to other matters, we will have to learn a lot of stories and historical wealth. Even after knowing all this, the things necessary for our present existence are not going to yield from them. Or, even if they do yield, we will also bend in accordance with how we try to believe, love, and put it into practice in the coming times. Other than this, we are not going to get any opportunity from such matters to specifically say, know, or think anything about the destruction that is going to befall our lineage.

[GV4:P0052] People might tell us about the great merits they achieved in times past. Whatever that may be, we must be convinced that there is a great blunder before us. Who are we in the karma spoken of by the many thousands of Gurus and more than twenty-five prophets who have come and gone? How will we theorize all these? How much have we been able to accomplish in the same measure as the karma they performed in their times? If we did accomplish it, what did we transform it into? To what extent were we able to merge into it?

[GV4:P0053] If we can ponder this slowly and adopt it over time, the first thing we must understand is that we have a flaw. What is this flaw? In what era did it occur? How did it come about? We stand having been born in an era where these things can be clearly known, and with the karmic capacity to find a solution for it. Having understood this, can it be taken up as a karma; will that dharma be attained through that experience; can this dharma be undertaken in a way that is free from karmic blemish? This is what you should think about. Otherwise, if you go about listening to, thinking about, and saying many things, you will have no foundation in anything. You do not know how to retrieve and preserve anything. Nor do you know what karma is to be preserved the most.

[GV4:P0054] What needs to be preserved the most is our character in life. What has mostly accumulated in life are entanglements. We must see that those entanglements are karmic attributes clinging to our soul. Within that karmic attribute itself, this karma can be prepared and contained. If that karmic attribute is made to repent, what are the good things that can come to us? You should at least have an idea to know this much. Only then will you feel that this is worth taking up. And that too, without rejecting anything.

[GV4:P0055] The guidance that has reached the karmic path of the human world up to this day must have surely reached the extent of the karmic attribute of this entanglement. If there is no doubt about it, one only needs to look at what that aspect is. That is the Shaiva, Shakta, and Vaishnava traditions. For the Shakta, that is supreme; for the Shaiva, that is supreme; for the Vaishnava, that is supreme. Besides, there are thousands of its branches. In this special dharma that we have been practicing, seeing, knowing, and speaking of in these traditions, how much merit-acquiring karma have we been able to perform? It has been lost in such a way that our families, our countrymen, let alone the Vedic religion or any notable prophetic religion, are unable to perform this dharma. If asked how this loss occurred, they will only evade the question.

[GV4:P0056] We can only live in accordance with the dharma and karma of the parents we got. Otherwise, what else can we do but get caught in some karma that the land and its people characterize as good or bad, and take on and foster that karmic blemish. We have a history of karmic blemishes that cannot be exhausted no matter how much is said. But that is not our resolve, is it?

[GV4:P0057] What is it that we require? What constitutes the realm that falls within the divine ordinance? How can we assume this responsibility? The human world requires a disposition that comprehends this. We cannot progress by exhaustively studying the system of the Trinity and the Manu system that prevailed for numerous epochs prior to it. There is only one core subject for this. If one fails to comprehend it, it remains a subject prone to the gravest errors. In what manner have the great souls of the past demonstrated this? One might have heard of deeds encompassing certain extraordinary mystical powers. The common populace cannot achieve anything by merely relying on these mystical abilities. For example, suppose an individual ascended to heaven in their physical body. What do we gain from such an occurrence? Would we derive any tangible benefit by merely recounting this narrative and offering our reverence?

[GV4:P0058] This is what we must comprehend: during our lifetime, we must discern the virtues and vices of bygone eras. We must understand the reasons why these virtues and vices have become a burden upon us. To realize this, we must trace our steps backward. Having been born absorbed in the karmic legacy that our ancestors revered and worshipped, we cannot arbitrarily discard it or abruptly transform it into something entirely different. However, we can deduce one fundamental truth. The Divine cannot manifest in a paradigm that assigns a separate deity to each caste. Do men and women have distinct gods?

[GV4:P0059] We remain ignorant of how the karmic force, which has purportedly manifested as distinct deities for men, women, and various castes, is sustained. Consequently, our entire understanding is restricted to a lineage that chased miracles and exhibited extraordinary mystical powers. We have not comprehended these mystical powers as a systematic discipline of knowledge. Instead, we have misconstrued them as a distinct form of spiritual wisdom. If an individual resides somewhere and offers solace to a few people, society immediately questions whether he is a mystic. We have erroneously equated the term mystic with an enlightened being. We remain completely unaware of the fundamental truth that a mystic is not necessarily an enlightened being.

[GV4:P0060] What is the karmic course that astonishes us by performing Jinn worship and displaying the frenzy of various devotional spectacles, or the karmic course of a Brahmarakshas yearning to merge with Brahman? There is a story told regarding this Brahmarakshas. A Yaksha summoned gods like Agni, Vayu, and Varuna and placed a blade of grass before them. But these gods could not stir or move it. Agni could not burn it, nor could Vayu blow it away. What can we understand about this blade of grass? We evaluate this miracle from within the confines of a karmic potential that has been subjected to the passage of time in mythology. What is the meaning in saying, "I do not respect this"? There is a fact that this was once revered. Do we disrespect it because it does not exist, or because we have too much knowledge, or because we lack knowledge? Therefore, we must comprehend a matter in accordance with our knowledge. Otherwise, you will face great ruin. Let this be understood first.

[GV4:P0061] What constitutes your knowledge? "Yesterday, I went to such-and-such places. Today as well, I went. Now I am returning." Expressed differently, "I went, came back exhausted, lay down, and slept well." How does one know that he slept? Sleeping is a transformation of the life force. The individual himself knows the state of sleeping well. However, what is the cause? We require the karmic capacity to recover and understand what the cause is. If what is seen in the waking state appears in the dream state, and what is seen in the dream state appears in deep sleep, there is a mechanism that grants liberation to the deep sleep state. The term deep sleep is generally understood as a state of sleeping without knowing anything. However, that is not the case. There is a dimension where one sees without physical eyes during deep sleep. So, which is this eye that sees? It is that which perceives within the core of the mind. That is the karmic course we cultivate. How will that dharma reach us?

[GV4:P0062] In the nature of this mind's eye, the karmic course of billions of years is being dragged before us. That was never done by me. It was not done by my ancestors. Then who did this? What we observe here is a karma that remained hidden behind some flawed action. If you do not completely understand this, you will find it difficult to grasp. What you assume is that if you invoke God, you must become wealthy tomorrow. Or you must become the greatest ruler. Or you must attain happiness by roaming freely and living as you please without any illness. Which of these is good? All are indeed good. But you must understand one thing. We possess a certain familiarity that our ancestors believed, knew, and communicated. We must realize where this will lead us. How does this manifest before us in the waking, dream, and deep sleep states? We have been made an instrument for this.

[GV4:P0063] We are gradually observing and comprehending what ripens in the waking, dream, and deep sleep states one by one. What is this waking, dream, and deep sleep? In the waking state, the eyes may be closed, or they may be open. Whether the eyes are closed or open, there is a nature of seeing. Even while sleeping, that special attribute does not leave us. Furthermore, one perceives while remaining in a silent, motionless state where the nature of space and time is indiscernible. This is another facet of deep sleep. It is difficult to comprehend how this comes to us. If one begins to count its seeds, another problem arises. Did the seed come first or the mango? What answer can be given to this? By standing on a sense of dharma that rationalizes certain things which can be dismissed through logic by asking such questions, who can we become? We will become no one.

[GV4:P0064] If you accept a title such as Guru, Deva, Rishi, or Sanyasi, you must understand one thing. What did we gain from the actions of about twenty-five prophets of the past? Similarly, what will you gain by hearing, knowing, and reading about sages who have come and gone across epochs, and about a Guru who emerged as the controller of miraculous deeds by displaying numerous mystic powers and miracles? That is not it; what you need is a center of faith that grasps these past occurrences. What will you observe in this karma that stands capable, having seen and grasped the actions of various epochs? This is what must be seen in the waking, dream, and deep sleep states. When it thus occurs and is experienced in the waking, dream, and deep sleep states, one must be able to recognize what it is. There are some individuals here who are capable of knowing this. So, what should we do? We must attain the karmic capability to grasp the cause, through which we became eligible to attain it. That cause, which guides us to retrieve both the good and the bad, can only instruct us on the capability to attain this path. That must be instructed in accordance with each individual's knowledge. Otherwise, one might be bewildered, assuming that one's own actions are entirely perfect, and love may manifest as a reflection of ego, resulting in nothing being accomplished. The love of God is not this. It is a karmic course that traverses thousands of paths that we have crossed, walked, known, and acted upon. It cannot be acquired merely by hearing, knowing, or speaking about it. It only guides you by explaining that what you see and hear is precisely this, in accordance with your understanding. Before a Guru who imparts such teachings, everything—all the enlightened beings, yogis, gurus, and prophets from all the traditions that have existed hitherto—must assemble. You should only accept such a person as your Guru. Otherwise, you will commit a grave error. You will fall to the ground like someone who loses their grip. How should you perform your karma by incorporating life, having understood at least this much? You will not incur any harm merely because you did not contemplate on God. However, you will not receive its benefits either.

[GV4:P0065] What is meant by faith in God? The ancestral curse of many predecessors, who waited for prosperity and wealth by making vows and offerings, building numerous pavilions, and constructing grand temples, remains within us. How can this curse be removed? You need not wander aimlessly for any of this. No matter where you wander, it will not work. What you need is a Guru who is capable of liberating everything that you and your ancestors have previously worshipped. Whether one is a prophet, or someone who has demonstrated brilliance by recounting various legendary riches while standing in the path of the prophets, or someone who has advanced far in mystical practices and attained the power of levitation, all of them must come before this Guru for the sake of their lives. Unless you surrender and pray to such a Guru, you will not gain any special benefit.

[GV4:P0066] Guruvani

GURUVANIKAL · July 2002 · Volume 4
Malayalam source paragraphs GV4:P0067 to GV4:P0670

[GV4:P0067] July 2002

[GV4:P0068] We have an outdated worshipping habit of getting things done by offering something insignificant to God. This is not the way; we should worship God to seek His grace. What should be done to attain God's grace? We have a duty towards God. We must understand it and perform it with a sense of duty. Because we have not done so, we have been committing errors in our worship of God for a long time.

[GV4:P0069] There is discord between husband and wife. As they continue to quarrel into their old age, their children will also follow suit. This is what I have observed to this day. Only in a few homes is this lack of culture absent. You have never entrusted your children with the knowledge of what is not being done for you here at the ashram. You have not entrusted them with it until today. I do not know what will be done tomorrow.

[GV4:P0070] God does not need your vows and offerings. Are we supposed to offer vows and offerings just to find a righteous path? If you wish to offer something, you may do so. Why? When such a custom has emerged in society, you can do so to learn some kind of lesson from it. That can be done in a temple or an ashram. However, that is not the matter I am discussing with you regarding the worship of God. There is a state of ignorance that our ancestors have perpetuated to this day. By uttering certain words in the very nature of that ignorance and trying to triumph through those words, you are holding on to certain karmic flaws.

[GV4:P0071] Wherever you go in the hilly regions, people speak in grandiose terms and act as if they possess great culture. However, not even a trace of culture can be found in them. By constantly exhibiting their culture, they have become like Westerners showing off their culture. What is that culture? It is only an external culture. It is not internal. They have decided that internal culture is unnecessary. This has infiltrated every home and its inner core.

[GV4:P0072] Since the practice of making vows and offerings has been going on for a long time, it has evolved within the temple system and grown to a large scale. In order to resolve the complications caused by this, God has imparted a certain knowledge to us over various periods. It was given through numerous great souls. Yet, we still have not understood that knowledge today.

[GV4:P0073] Christians are the community that habitually preaches the greatest sacrifice. But is there sacrifice among Christians now? The meaning of sacrifice is to practice living truthfully. Are Christians living truthfully now? Christians stand like compasses pointing towards the West. Other than the culture of the home remaining among some poor people, it does not exist in a single household that has enough to eat, drink, and wear. Why? It is the Hindus who have shifted towards that today. They have also adopted the practice of vows and offerings similar to that of the Hindus. They are even prepared to commit any kind of violence in the name of God.

[GV4:P0074] Muslims claim that they govern according to laws determined by God. Is the divine law that one can commit any kind of plunder? If this is the situation within the Islamic religion, which emerged only a short time ago, Hindus possess a history that has undergone immense changes over time. Hindus embraced oracular deities and became devoid of culture. When their authority waned, they attempted to appear great by displaying foolishness. Similarly, there is caste, and castes within castes. Those who belonged to a higher caste began to live by flaunting its greatness. Those who were not considered great began to live like Westerners. Because of this, humanity has drifted away from its true nature. As human nature drifted away, a realization that both men and women need freedom has spread.

[GV4:P0075] The sense of freedom is good. But what is freedom? It is assumed that freedom is men and women properly arguing and justifying their stances. That is not freedom. What shortcomings have we experienced in the past? The women in the house must know this. What was the situation amidst those shortcomings? How did it happen? Teach them this first. Due to those shortcomings, we have received a misguided life. When the uncultured Western culture began to spread, it became even worse.

[GV4:P0076] Aside from presenting models of sacrifice, there is no actual sacrifice among Christians. Who has become Christians? Those who lived as the most downtrodden among the Hindus. When they acquire money and capability, they will not stay grounded. They will only behave without any manners. Today, Christians and Muslims in Kerala have become wealthy. However, their culture is completely different. They speak eloquently with sweet words, but they will not translate it into action. This is a path towards danger.

[GV4:P0077] God has given you the most suitable opportunity. But you will not take it. I will only speak and behave truthfully with you. What do you do? You squander it. What can I do? What kind of freedom have you envisioned? It is an inferiority complex born from having lived in servitude. This is one kind of freedom. Another is the freedom of an arrogant life. Yet another is the freedom derived from fighting over caste and religion. Is this the freedom of humanity?

[GV4:P0078] Have you felt this idea to be true? If so, you are the ones who must put it into practice. It is for you to implement that I have done this. People assume that this is how freedom should be sought. This freedom is not freedom. It is a freedom that drags our children into error.

[GV4:P0079] The greatest ignorance lies in the hands of the educated. In uneducated children, flaws are seen much less. Wherever wealth, capability, and education have risen, arrogance has also risen. The culture of Mayyanad, the culture of Kottayam, and looking more broadly, Ernakulam, Kochi, and then a different culture in Kozhikode. Thus, how many types of cultures exist in Kerala itself! If you are imparting such a cultureless knowledge, what have you decided to give to your children? I am asking those who come and reside here. The reason you Hindus, Christians, Muslims, and people from Brahmins to Chandalas come and stay here is because I have love and obligation towards you, and you towards me. I have taught you after having done something myself. But that is not what you have perceived. You live here as if carrying a resentment that is the greatest accumulation of an undignified life. You must not bring your old resentment in here and express it. If you express it, your children will be lost. Then I will not be able to do anything. Why do you commit such perversity here? I am telling you this after addressing the flaw that has come down through your lineage, and altering even the freedom of worship to a different path so that the culture of your home may change. But you are unable to think, understand, or obey it.

[GV4:P0080] I have eradicated the tradition that you have been worshipping. I have not done this by looking at whether it is Hindu, Christian, Muslim, or Buddhist. The core of that old culture has been uprooted from your tradition. Have I ever considered whether you are a Brahmin or a Chandala? What I am asking is whether you have ever thought that at least one child who has lived here to date should grow up in this new culture. The experience I have received from everyone who worked near me, and from their entire families, is pain. If that is not the case, you must say so.

[GV4:P0081] Why have I done this for you? If you did not need it, then why did you make me do it? Is anyone among you prepared to live according to that standard and show it to me? Are you living here to corrupt this concept given by God and ruin yourselves?

[GV4:P0082] After taking hold of all your old baseness and doing the work to liberate you from it, the first thing you are told is that you must abandon the principles of caste and class (Jati-Varna Dharmas). You must tell me if you have abandoned them. If you had abandoned them, this is not how you would be behaving here. Is it not a culture forcibly imposed from somewhere that you are holding onto as your asset? Is this why you are being nurtured with such great effort? Have I done things for you while preserving my own self-interest? Please tell me; I want to know this from you yourselves.

[GV4:P0083] You should not assume that I am speaking only about the matter of caste. I categorically state that not a single one of you has been careful in any matter. What is the purpose of sugarcoating these pleasant words to me? For what reason did you come here, believe in this, and reside here? That is what you must tell me. If anyone has acted with genuine affection towards this concept, towards me, and towards the institution, tell me that. Other than living engrossed in the act of feigning prosperity and friendship wherever you look to create a non-existent wealth, what have you done for this? If you do not wish to instill your culture in your children, you must move away from here. Otherwise, you will only leave after destroying this and turning it into a culture of division.

[GV4:P0084] You are performing actions with your focus on some distant goal. Whom are you trying to appease; are you showing this baseness to appease God? If you exhibit this anymore, I will not stand with you. Those who remain within and those associated with this should act only after understanding that. I am saying this to you with absolute certainty. You only need to believe in this, live here, and associate with this if you have the resolve to live truthfully. You do not need to say anything for me to hear. You just need to live and show me. I do not need to hear you say anything. I will not believe it.

[GV4:P0085] You have become the Shudra class. Any mistake that arises from you is not intentional. When you act, it will only happen that way. How many among you came having perceived this before seeing me physically! You can increase your spiritual merit only if you handle this with the understanding that it is a manifestation of divine will. Otherwise, neither doctrines nor miraculous feats are being preached here. What will you gain if I perform miracles?

[GV4:P0086] Someone performed a miracle. Someone portrayed themselves as a great person. Because of that, what inner peace do we attain? You are witnessing this directly. You are directly experiencing spiritual merit. There are so many people who have known me for a very long time. Because they lacked familial fortune, they went astray. What is meant by familial fortune? Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra. It has been understood that this is the era where the class standing in the fourth quarter possesses authority, hasn't it? What authority? The Shudra class holds the authority for the knowledge of Brahman. When speaking of the Shudra class, there is a Brahmin and a Shudra in each of our homes. This is the rationale. But this is not what has been conveyed to us. Instead, Varnasrama Dharma was celebrated, and we were hidden under that class and reduced to a caste. This has grown to such an extent that no one can do anything about it. Today, if we take India as a whole, there are one hundred and eighty-four castes. Let each person reflect upon where we have reached.
