[GV4:P0244] Ashram: The Place That Gives the Knowledge of Experience

[GV4:P0245] We hold an understanding of the ashram as it existed in the Treta Yuga or beyond. However, that is not how one should perceive the ashram. The nature of the ashram must evolve according to the Yugadharma (the duty of the age). Until today, we have had no knowledge regarding this matter. No one has clearly informed us about it, nor have we known it.

[GV4:P0246] The purpose of the ashram is to create an opportunity to perform the karma destined for each yuga in a manner that benefits the land, the nation, and the world. The ashram is not merely meant for sanyasa (renunciation). This does not mean sanyasa is absent. It is there; there can be sanyasis and brahmacharis. There can also be vanaprastha sanyasa. It can also serve the purpose of fulfilling the faith of those who do not fall into any of these categories.

[GV4:P0247] What should we understand by terms like brahmacharya, vanaprastha, and sanyasa? We have ancestral Gurus who were born in different yugas and otherwise. If we consider a single yuga itself, they functioned in five different ways. A Yugadharma is accomplished based on the information provided by Gurus possessing five distinct natures. Among these five Gurus, there is a Guru who appears at the beginning of the yuga and another who appears at the end. The great soul who emerges at the intersection of the end of one yuga and the onset of another will be the one arriving as the Yugadhikari (Authority of the Yuga) during that period. The notion that an ashram is simply a place to sit around, chant, and breathe one's last without knowing any of this is incorrect. Those who harbor such erroneous knowledge are not the ones who should come to the ashram.

[GV4:P0248] The vasanas (latent tendencies) that have been worshipped and perpetuated across multiple lifetimes must be severed. Only the great soul who arrives at this yugasandhi (junction of ages) can prescribe the karma necessary to sever these vasanas. All the events that transpired in the first three yugas of a chaturyuga (cycle of four ages) must also manifest in Kali, the dharma of the fourth yuga.

[GV4:P0249] What is it that we need to comprehend in detail about the Kali Yuga? We have heard that Kali is evil. Such statements were made because matters were explained by highlighting individual flaws. Among the yugadharmas, Kalidharma is the most superior. The dharma of Kali is to evaluate the good and bad deeds performed thus far, to discern if there is any divine will beyond that, and to determine our course of action in accordance with that divine will—evaluating the virtues and vices of all these aspects.

[GV4:P0250] Many great souls may emerge in Kali. Numerous great souls may have appeared in the preceding yugas as well. Beyond all this, the dharma of Kali entails recognizing the mistakes committed through one's own life and the lives of ancestral great souls, and understanding how to establish the system of worship and other requisite karmas in alignment with the Yugadharma. The ashram is not a place to behave basely, as misconceived by some who lack this knowledge, nor is it a place to retreat to and squander one's life when rejected by family and society. Such individuals will not adhere to the ashram, its discipline, or its teachings. They will lack the capability to function in that manner. Such people will only propagate evil among others and will never perform good deeds. Whether male or female, for every single virtue they possess, they will harbor ten vices; for a thousand virtues, they will sow ten thousand seeds of destruction.

[GV4:P0251] For a long time, God has desired to reveal that this is not the dharma of Kali, or to seek the absolution of this world's sins. Who are we within the dharma dictated by that desire? Kali is the era equipped with the facility to process the numerous experiences embedded in the karmas associated with our many lifetimes, allowing us to realize the essence of our soul. The ashram is the arena designed to put such a dharma of Kali into practice. The ashram is not a venue meant for adhering to the dharmas of the Treta Yuga and Dvapara Yuga.

[GV4:P0252] It is during our period of education that the most optimal method is desired. Because an individual has numerous tasks to accomplish, certain events have transpired in their life, specific occurrences have taken place in the lives of their ancestors, and from all of these, a destined karma has emerged. The period of education is the phase granted to rectify those mistakes and to render service by understanding what can be optimally prepared not only for the family but also for the land and the nation. However, what develops within us is the karmic capacity envisioned by the ancestors, devas, and rishis, which has assimilated the good and bad deeds of our forefathers. This is the most significant issue afflicting us. It is not the karmic trajectory or vasana of today or yesterday that burdens us. Regarding service, all of this can be executed consciously, knowingly, or unknowingly. What is implied here is—there is no role here for the scholar's literal interpretations, the layman's foolish interpretations, or the individuals who seek such things.

[GV4:P0253] What all has been enacted in the Treta Yuga and Dvapara Yuga; how many Satya Yugas, Treta Yugas, and Dvapara Yugas have thus elapsed; and how much karma has been resolved through these yugas. The karma into which we are currently born and raised is the absolute accumulation of the preceding yugadharmas. What is the utility of pursuing education without the requisite knowledge to comprehend all this? Today, college education and the education beyond it are mere facets of a culture forcefully imposed from elsewhere.

[GV4:P0254] It is indeed beneficial to adopt an ashram-like nature and its corresponding mindset. However, the karmic accumulation of the Kali Yuga cannot necessarily be comprehended through that alone. The Kali Yuga is a truth to which the scholar and the layman, the knowledgeable and the ignorant, and individuals of any caste, religion, or class hold an equal claim without any prejudice. But instead of preparing to operationalize it, our family members and local community dismiss it with contempt, relying on obsolete knowledge they have merely heard. They do not even pause to consider what enhancement this contempt will bring to our lives.

[GV4:P0255] I am conveying certain matters to you based on what has been revealed to us here (at Santhigiri) through divine visions. This has been iterated many times in the past. Yet, I have not been able to convince myself thus far that anyone has truly paid heed to it. Having established this space as an ashram, undertaking only what is strictly essential for life, and dedicating the entirety of the remaining time towards fulfilling the dharma of Kali, we are currently in the process of learning from the most fundamental aspects onwards. Among those engaged in such learning, there are also individuals who find themselves incapable of fulfilling it.

[GV4:P0256] We do not see here an inheritance that our predecessors have diligently cultivated and handed down to us with complete love and respect regarding any aspect of karma. It is not merely the duty of a Brahmana or a Kshatriya; they are also unaware that Kali is the era where the Vaisya and the Sudra must advance in karma by joining hands together. Therefore, they will not change their mercantile nature either. Today, humans have a tendency to manipulate any situation to justify immoral actions. However, that is not what we should desire. By examining the paths through which the humans, deities, and sages of the present and the past eras acquired knowledge, our focus today should be on what needs to be done to acquire knowledge now, how long our health will permit it, how we should live until old age, how we have been advised to act practically, and how much of that advice we have been able to assimilate. Instead, what can we achieve by fabricating, modifying, and arbitrarily renaming old customs? We are born in an era where nothing can be achieved through such fabrications. However, this is an era where everything is attainable.

[GV4:P0257] Today, what is predominantly seen are ashramas functioning according to the dharma of bygone eras. They continue the rituals based on those traditions. We must have the knowledge of the virtues in them. Otherwise, we will face the misfortune of standing bewildered even before our own children. The widespread rituals of today heavily incorporate the aspects of mantra, tantra, and yantra strictly according to the Vedic religion. However, they hold no place in the dharma of the Kali era.

[GV4:P0258] One must reside in an ashrama to attain the fruitful realization of undertaking and performing the duties of a grihasthashrami (householder), an aspiring seeker of knowledge, and an aspirant of wealth. However, without a purpose, it will not lead to purity of intention. Nor will it bear any result. If one resides in an ashrama without knowing any of this, with a mind wandering and becoming corrupt, they gain nothing but the unloading and distribution of the accumulated impurities of countless past lives. Many venture here to gain familiarity with this old habit. The logic they use for this is the phrase, 'The great sages praise what they see day by day.'

[GV4:P0259] The great sages praised what they saw day by day. However, this is not what the great sages truly saw. This is merely a literal interpretation. One should not look at this karmic progression that has been exaggerated through mere wordplay. Then what? Concerning ourselves, one must ask: Why was I born? Why did I grow? Why should I continue to live? Many things have intruded into my life, which has been caught in the cycle of birth, death, rebirth, and death. I have accepted this karma (the body) to eliminate this from myself. How many of us possess the ability to reflect upon this?

[GV4:P0260] There are also those who act by only seeing right and wrong. It is referred to as four generations. That is not merely a calculation of human generations. It implies four generations corresponding to a yuga. That will subsequently align with the calculation of the Chatur Yugas (four eras). This is an experience. Just because an experience occurred, it does not mean it is understood. The experience must have primarily occurred at the beginning. This is not something that resides in the scientific consciousness of either the scholar or the ignorant. If one habituates oneself to actions driven by foolishness, it will result in karmic flaws. What is being described is the path of knowledge that serves as experiential evidence.

[GV4:P0261] There might be experiences of the Treta Yuga and the Dwapara Yuga. One might have passed through the Satya Yuga as well. In the Satya Yuga, one only speaks and acts truthfully. Therefore, the action is truthful. The action in the Kali Yuga is also the same. But the karma of the Kali Yuga is not like that of the Satya Yuga. One must cultivate a determination to inquire how dharma is sustained when karmas are exhausted without rejecting the dharmas that came and went in other yugas, what is required for it, and what is not. Past gurus have worked tirelessly for this. However, we have strayed from all those paths. No one knows what our present requirement is. The brahmachari, the householder, and the sanyasi do not know. This is because we have not received that knowledge from the temples and the ashramas.

This is elucidated in terms of the Trinity (*Trimurti*) forms and their lineages. We do refer to him as *Nanmukhan* (the four-faced one)—representing the face of wisdom.

[GV4:P0323] The doctrine of *Nanmukhan* essentially denotes the authority of Kali Yuga. The other yugas are Satya Yuga, Treta Yuga, and Dvapara Yuga. Among Brahma, Vishnu, and Maheshwara, it is said concerning Brahma that the fourth face is absent. That is, the face of true wisdom is missing. It was plucked off. Because he did not know the meaning of the *Omkara*, the fourth face was severed.

[GV4:P0324] This is the very subject I wish to convey to you. Some among you are doing commendable work. I am pleased about that. However, I am also aware that this effort is inadequate. Even prior to Sree Krishna's advent, knowledge of that arrival was disseminated. We were unable to retain Sree Krishna here. Although there are accounts of various wars, we drove Sree Krishna away to the extent that He had no opportunity to remain in India. He was driven away by the monarchs of that era themselves. There is a history to that. It is said that having been forced to flee, He reached another shore and constructed Dwaraka there. That city was subsequently submerged in the ocean. Evidence of this can still be observed today.

[GV4:P0340] The epochs are in a state of continuous transition. The masses lack the profound wisdom required to adapt in tandem with this epochal shift. [GV4:P0341] As far as we are concerned, we possess the certainty of direct experience. Your sole contemplation should be on how to act while remaining absorbed in that ultimate dissolution of whatever is perceived. These great souls were those who performed austerities, bathing in the snow-fed, flowing Ganges at four in the morning, chanting with intense spiritual agony. From the exalted position where that sacrifice devolved into mantras and tantras and was solidified through penance, one must descend by operating solely with the karmic capacity of an ordinary human being. Only through such a descent will true order be established.

[GV4:P0342] The word of the discoverer is logic. There must be someone to actualize that word with utmost sincerity. This is because it has been corrupted through action (*karma*). Rectifying this is no easy endeavor. If the action is not executed with absolute tranquility, it will inevitably go astray. This is a subject that eludes the grasp of any scientist.

[GV4:P0343] As stated earlier, our primary asset is our experience. The inception will be arduous. The difficulty will fluctuate in proportion to the degree of sincerity. Even during prayer, the initial experience is often one of distress. There may even be times when one feels an aversion to praying. Then, interest resurfaces, followed by another phase of dullness. That is its nature. Just as one does not desire to consume the exact same food every day, a yearning for variation in prayer will also arise. The perversions carried over from one's own past lives are the root cause of this. No religious adherents speak of this, because their depth extends only up to the status of the deities. The Quran discusses liberation to a certain extent, but it is not exhaustive. This is because no religion possesses a prehistory and antiquity that spans the duration of the epochs. The Bible recounts merely six thousand years of history. These are insufficient to penetrate the profound secrets of human existence and the ultimate reality of karmic forms. The realm of absolute knowledge is located far, far beyond all of these. In that realm, there are no artificial fabrications. There is no tuft, no purdah, and no other external masquerades.

[GV4:P0346] Life Devoid of Self-Discipline

[GV4:P0347] Every household of ours possesses a certain shrewdness. The land itself possesses that shrewdness. However, each of these forms of shrewdness has its own inherent flaws. In southern Travancore, there are certain ruffians. The lineage in the households of these ruffians invariably stands on the side of a particular kind of ignorance. A specific type of ignorance, characterized by boastful arrogance, has developed among everyone. They may have acquired wealth, employment, and capabilities, but adverse consequences will inevitably manifest during their children's generation. Similarly, we are mindlessly participating in a race driven by the karmic momentum of unchecked scientific advancement. That race is profoundly misguided.

[GV4:P0392] What I convey to you stems from my personal experience. I have not appropriated the logic, scriptures (*shruti*), or rationalizations of any external authority. By virtue of being born a Hindu, I operated under the assumption that the Hindu paradigm was superior. There was indeed an extended period during which I harbored this belief. In our formative years, our mothers instill in us the notion, "Children, God is a wrathful entity that punishes with death." Consequently, even if God is not a punisher, can one evade the ingrained fear of Him? As we mature further, God is perceived as an entity that orchestrates trials and surveillance. Advancing still further, God is reduced to the residue of frenzied oracles—trembling, dancing, chanting, and exhibiting possessed behavior. Subsequently, after cultivating faith, devotion, and reverence over a prolonged period, a realization dawns that this entity is not worthy of being revered as God. At that juncture, embracing rationalism and alternative ideologies, an individual showcases intellectual prowess within the confines of those arguments. Ultimately, the individual finds himself entirely lost within them. In this manner, men and women perpetuate diverse spectacles across various strata. There exist myriad such inexplicable karmic trajectories. These are the very phenomena you categorize using diverse nomenclatures—*Karmi*, *Yogi*, *Jnani*, *Bhakta*, Fakir, Saint, and Apostle. Irrespective of our caste, religion, or class, we are fundamentally incapable of transcending this overarching paradigm.

[GV4:P0421] Knowledge in the States of Waking, Dreaming, and Deep Sleep
