There, one must see what one's Guru stands as. If we are to be able to get close to this Guru, we need an acquaintance to see what that karma was, where the snow that caused Sri Krishna's Dwarka to sink became rain, and then turned into water.

[GV4:P0445] Where was this snow in ancient times! It was here even without anyone creating it. This is the magnificence of nature. The real story regarding Sri Krishna is that this snow, which was so hard that it could only be broken by shooting it, melted into water drops, mixed with whatever there was to mix, raised the water level, and submerged everything. A Guru is needed to know in detail about such a great soul. If one ever says anything denying the Guru, everything will be lost. How foolish is it to say that one will only think and act logically. How can a person, who is in the unfortunate state of not even knowing who his own father is, logically decipher these matters that are beyond thought and vast as the sky? There is a very ancient ignorance within us regarding this logical reasoning. The Guru is the one who points out this ignorance and eliminates it.

[GV4:P0446] You have no experience of being taught such matters at the time of your birth. Instead, what have we been taught? That a mere vision of God is sufficient for everything. We stand upon this foundation of ignorance. Even if God were to manifest not once, but a thousand times, there is nothing to be gained. For any true realization to occur, one must reach a state where the soul is offered as an oblation to the soul itself. The one who enables such a transformation is the Atmaguru!

[GV4:P0447] If one wishes to tell another, "I slept well yesterday," it must be an experience they have personally had. What can be done if one claims not to possess that experience? It is "I" who states that I slept. Therefore, the concept of "I" is present there. That perceived "I" is the Dharma—not separate from oneself—existing in a state of cessation, possessing an imperishable nature, and residing in the action of the form of sound. You must reclaim this discernment. Just as the sound we produce and hear eventually dissolves into the atmosphere, nature captures an imprint of the actions we perform both individually and collectively. Similarly, the truths—both good and bad—worshipped and propagated by our ancestors remain intertwined within this nature. The life force clinging to my body is merely the residue of countless lifetimes that have manifested, vanished, and acted consciously and unconsciously over an immense expanse of time. We can attain this knowledge solely through a Guru. Whether one encounters a deity or a demon, my Guru will be present there. Toddy, rice gruel water, and milk may share the same color; the differences lie only marginally in their form and essence. One must learn to distinguish these subtleties. This comprehension is impossible without a Guru. Thus, a Guru must be someone who has traversed through all that is good and all that is evil. No matter what absurdity is witnessed, one must be able to perceive their Guru amidst it. In this manner, we are shown the paths that the Guru has traversed. Ultimately, one must observe what they transform into when themselves, the Guru, and the perceived objects all dissolve and merge into one.

[GV4:P0448] By revealing a formless essence within nature—where all demonic forces are subsumed—one must perceive the entity that endures as the ultimate truth in this formless state as the Guru. This is precisely why it is stated that a Guru is essential. Does the Guru reside exclusively within the good? No. The Guru is present in both the good and the evil. Otherwise, who would absorb your impurities? One must perceive within themselves a formless power manifesting as a form, remaining unblemished and without losing mental equanimity, realizing and imparting the knowledge that it is in no way evil. That is to say, the Guru is fundamentally formless, yet simultaneously possesses a form.

[GV4:P0449] Jagrat (the waking state) and Swapna (the dream state). Whatever is perceived in the waking state is subsequently experienced in the dream state and in Sushupti (deep sleep). It is Turiya (the fourth state of consciousness) and Turiyatita (the state beyond the fourth) that reveal the intricacies of the variations in forms and names. The Guru represents the absolute totality of action that elucidates and differentiates these five distinct states of consciousness.

[GV4:P0450] What was the nature of the deity during the era of the deities, and what was the role of the sage (Rishi) then? Who are these sages diverging into the four paths of the ritualist (Karmi), the mystic (Yogi), the seeker of knowledge (Jnani), and the devotee (Bhakta)? What is the relationship between such a sage and one's Guru? How are the attributes of bygone sages and deities reflected in my Guru? The Guru is the embodied knowledge that discerns and elucidates the authentic essence of all deities spanning the Shaiva, Shakta, and Vaishnava traditions, the true forms of Ghatotkacha hurling serpents with a thousand hands, and Goddess Durga—and transcending all these, reveals the manifold virtues of a soul devoid of gender distinctions. All of these profound realities must culminate in our direct experience.

[GV4:P0451] Here, this profound experience does not belong to the offspring brought from my household; rather, it belongs to your children, husbands, and wives. It is subsequently transmitted to their descendants, eventually attaining a state of permanence. Thus, it is the love rooted in faith in the Guru that is being instilled within you. The formless essence that pervades and empowers all manifested forms within nature belongs to the Guru. It is nature itself that reveals this reality. This Guru is the one who characterises and demonstrates to us the nature of that eternal power from bygone eras. Guided by that vision, we continue to progress forward.

[GV4:P0452] What constitutes the evolutionary transformation of our life force? Through what all has it intricately woven its way? This must be perceived through the soul. True knowledge is the wisdom reflected synergistically by the life force and the soul residing within this physical body. The life force and the soul exist within you. How does one recognize this? If the trajectory of action required to reclaim this realization is absent within us, we will be left utterly bewildered. Our faith constitutes the resolute firmness required to actualize this experience. At times, my Guru may appear virtuous; at other times, he may seem like an unparalleled scoundrel. Yet, he remains my Guru. I shall acknowledge all of these facets. This is the ultimate steadfastness of faith. One cannot simply take a Guru somewhere to be cleansed, purified, and rectified. What scientist, what proponent of liberation can ever assert that such love, such a profoundly deep connection, does not exist?

[GV4:P0453] Direct experience is the most profound bond; it is the ultimate love. It is beyond comparison. The experiences encountered in the Jagrat (waking), Swapna (dream), and Sushupti (deep sleep) states constitute the exclusive domain of the Guru. No one else will be able to comprehend them. Therefore, such matters should be disclosed only to the Guru. One will witness the good, the evil, and the absurd. The Guru serves as the sole medium to question why one has been led into the ignorance of such absurdities. The philosophy underpinning our faith is the spiritual oblation (Atmanivedana) that unifies one's life force and vital breath (Prana) as one, after traversing through all these dualities sequentially. It is certainly not Vedanta. The assertion that the Katha Upanishad dictates one thing or another Upanishad dictates something else—none of this constitutes the true philosophy of our existence. The Upanishads are merely the documented personal experiences of various individuals. Can interpreting and expounding upon them ever constitute true spiritual realization?

[GV4:P0454] The witness to the Jagrat (waking), Swapna (dream), and Sushupti (deep sleep) states. The Guru represents the ultimate culmination of action (Karmapoorthi)—encompassing all that we have worshipped or neglected to worship with this witness as our focal point, the good we have acknowledged or remained ignorant of, the circumstances arising through special destiny, and the spiritual heritage nurtured collectively by the Guru, oneself, and one's lineage.

[GV4:P0455] Guruvani

[GV4:P0456] Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Samarpana Edition 2002

[GV4:P0457] What the Believers Must Know

[GV4:P0458] I have never performed any magic tricks before you. I have not exhibited any special mystical powers (Siddhis). Whatever is pleasing to God, that must transpire. The exact will of God has been revealed to us. Several among you have also been convinced that this is the absolute truth. However, how do you conduct yourselves with one another? You are individuals who constantly quarrel among yourselves, as if bereft of the capacity to utter a single kind word. When one arrives at the threshold of a virtue that, through the sheer majesty of a benevolent word, could be transmitted to the younger generation, the community, the household, and the nation—what inevitably accompanies you is strife. The conflict escalates to its fullest extent and then dissolves into sheer nothingness.

[GV4:P0459] If those residing in the Ashram fail to comprehend the spiritual ethos of the Ashram, then for what purpose am I toiling? If, having arrived as believers, you do not assimilate the intrinsic nature of the Ashram through seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, and tasting, not only will you remain ignorant of this path, but you will also ultimately tear apart and discard the fragments of knowledge you have gathered from various sources, thereby straying entirely from the path of faith. Have you not witnessed countless individuals abandoning this place in such a manner?

[GV4:P0460] What is attainable here can only be acquired through sheer endurance. When one examines the reasons behind your quarrels, it becomes evident that there is absolutely no valid justification for them. You do not even practice the foundational virtue of forgiveness. You will only comprehend the heights to which patience can elevate you if you actively practice it. As far as Sannyasa (renunciation) is concerned, there is scarcely a need to speak of patience. Honor and dishonor are treated as equals (Manapamaname thulyam). That is to say, before the ideals of Sannyasa, both honor and disgrace hold no significance. Relinquishing both, whatever one receives in the contemplation of the Divine, that alone must be accepted. Beyond this, there is no alternative justification to be sought. You engage in various antics under the misguided assumption that life merely consists of the superficial displays inherent to materialistic existence.

[GV4:P0461] There is a sect known as the Lingayats. They are individuals who do not wear clothing. I have read in newspapers that they occasionally enter the parliament and cause disruptions. They number in the thousands. When they arrive, it becomes impossible for others to remain in that vicinity. Thus, how many varied followers of spiritual paths exist in India alone! However, one should not presume that adopting these paths will lead to the ultimate truth. To lead one to the truth, an individual who has intimately experienced the truth must arrive. For this, forests, mountains, women, or men do not constitute an obstacle, as it is a matter of profound fortune. Even if one were to wander the entire globe in pursuit of the truth, it is not guaranteed to be discovered. Conversely, even if it is in your immediate proximity, you may remain oblivious to it. If individuals residing in the ashram fail to comprehend the ashram's environment, what else can possibly be said to such individuals?

[GV4:P0462] There is an adage that to determine the purity of gold, one must bring it to a touchstone; bringing it to a grinding stone will not reveal its true value. This implies that you must engage intimately and act to rectify your own flaws. One must utilize their knowledge to repair the defective aspects of their being. If one lacks the knowledge to preserve seeds without them spoiling, three-quarters of those seeds will invariably perish. Similarly, you are individuals who have squandered your lives without prudent preservation. You fail to comprehend even the accomplishments achieved within your own home in the broader context of your household, society, and the nation.

[GV4:P0463] Many among you had proven to be rightful heirs to this fortune (experience) even before encountering me. It has also been demonstrated to each of you what the necessity of this experience entails. Despite comprehending this, you refrain from embracing it. Even though God has provided an opportunity to profoundly understand the knowledge bestowed upon you, the requisite action to honor it does not manifest within you. Why do I insist that this must be imparted to your children? It is not solely for your benefit, but to ensure that this society receives whatever it is destined to gain from you.

[GV4:P0464] You possess love and faith. I acknowledge that. Your affection and trust towards me have no boundaries. Even if boundaries were set, the Divine would eradicate them. Although you may lack purity of soul, you harbor the thought that nothing contrary to this ideal you believe in should emanate from my side. Those who stood with me continue to leave, one by one. Those who depart stand aside and claim they bear no enmity towards the Swami. When asked why they leave, they attribute it to the actions of others. Do you come to the ashram merely to observe others? These others are individuals with their own rights, wrongs, and flaws, much like yourselves. Consequently, they will act and cause actions in accordance with that nature. You must recognize that it is partly your responsibility to prevent such alienation from occurring. Blaming others is not the appropriate recourse. They might have acted according to their level of understanding. I am not suggesting that you should undertake the task of reforming them. However, if you comprehend the situation, there is no harm in gently and affectionately advising them against such actions. Do not inflict pain by using substandard words. I articulate this because there exists within you a tendency that does not hesitate to hurt others.

[GV4:P0465] Can anyone—whether those who stood close to me or those who later departed citing various reasons—utter a single word claiming that this is not the truth? I am not referring to those who have had a brief association with me. If those with less familiarity display displeasure, they cannot be faulted. If those who possess an association spanning twenty or thirty years are unable to assimilate this in profound accordance with their tenure and affection, and if those who witness it with their own eyes and harbor immense personal devotion cannot sustain it within their own homes, what is the point of blaming others?

[GV4:P0466] Knowledge exists, but there is an absence of true understanding where it is required. This is the essence of a Shudra state of mind. If you are educated, you will tend to evaluate things from the standpoint of your acquired learning. If, instead of demonstrating humility, you exhibit the arrogance of a learned person, you will be unable to internalize this experience. Is the subject matter here something that can be guided by a salvationist, a rationalist, an atheist, a wealthy individual, a scholar, or a Vedantic philosopher?

[GV4:P0467] It is easy to speak of truth, compassion, and empathy. However, do we possess the action required to unify these virtues? The essence of this truth is being demonstrated to you as your rightful inheritance. Yet, you fail to recognize it. Our knowledge is entirely directed towards claiming ownership over children, wife, husband, wealth, and education. I have never instructed you to abandon or refrain from acquiring any of these. I have never asked you to forsake your home, nor abandon men or women. What I am stating is this: you diminish yourselves concerning the profound knowledge residing deep within your minds. I have imparted this very understanding to the experienced children who stand beside me. This is a subject attained through immense struggle. However, I have reiterated to you a hundred times that I have not struggled for it presently. I have done nothing for it in the present time. It is exceedingly ancient. It was Buddha who calculated and stated that he attained numerous lifetimes where that state of philosophical vision was sustained—five hundred incarnations where the state of vision endured. An argumentative nature that denies all this may be considered acceptable; however, the truth remains that such individuals are incapable of achieving anything significant. If each of you were to contemplate in this manner, the nobility inherent in that knowledge would enter your minds, and you would begin to externally manifest what true nobility is. That is the experience you have received.

[GV4:P0468] I possess no mystical powers, nor do I engage in speaking in tongues. Nevertheless, I possess the ability to articulate the actions occurring within each of your homes. These are actions that remain incomprehensible to others, even if they were to see, hear, or learn of them. Having understood it in this manner, and recognizing that this is the highest of Dharmas and that no greater Dharma is yet to emerge, you can embrace it with the utmost courage. The predicament faced by those who departed from here is entirely due to their failure to comprehend this reality.

[GV4:P0469] We must transform the actions residing within our minds. How can you, who have solely learned to berate and criticize others, accept this? Is this not akin to the egoistic grasp of politicians? Scholars, on the other hand, will enumerate the names of numerous books and merely unearth their deepest roots to present to you. Entangled in such individual traps, we remain ignorant of how to properly honor this. Why do I articulate my experience to you in such exhaustive detail, akin to an open book? It is with the intention that if even one or two among the many who happen to encounter these words comprehend it, they might honor it, disseminate it to the public, and internalize that action as their own. That action is not for me. Yet, in another sense, it indeed is for me. Whatever you do will ultimately reach me. For when the authority of a Dharma has been established, I must not declare that it does not belong to me.

[GV4:P0470] It is the Divine that has granted you the opportunity to accomplish this. It was by understanding Buddha in this manner that Emperor Ashoka renounced everything and set forth for this cause. He sacrificed both of his children for the sake of the ideology. Why did he undertake all these actions? Being an emperor and possessing a refined culture of that magnitude, he comprehended it. He demonstrated to us the requisite qualification on how to strive, sacrifice, and propagate it. What destiny awaits us, who are incapable of even contemplating such matters? If you are to uproot the inherited flaws deeply entrenched within you, and should you attain this, you must be prepared to contemplate solely upon it, cultivate it, and handle it in accordance with true knowledge. I convey this to you after having introduced the illumination that the subject of experience has offered thus far. It would be immensely beneficial if you cultivate at least a habit of contemplating how to assimilate this truth. However, one thing remains certain: even if you become acquainted with this knowledge, you will be unable to embrace it if you fail to preserve the truth.

[GV4:P0471] Sacrifice possesses an inherent glory. It is not intended to display greatness. Whoever receives this in their hands must honor it. This is the greatest of fortunes. It is so because it is the path of liberation that rectifies the errors accumulated over numerous *yugas* (epochs).

[GV4:P0472] What am I essentially telling you? By analyzing a vast period beyond *yugas*, I am highlighting the true aspects of the lives of the Gurus who appeared solely in this *Kaliyuga* and presenting them to you. If the children growing up before you make an error in even a single word contrary to this ideal, it must be corrected immediately. Otherwise, it would signify a lack of humility towards the truth. Furthermore, this ideal will depart from your household. If you are blessed with the fortune to receive the fullness of God, you must undertake that *karma* at any cost. This is neither for renunciation nor for acquiring dominance. Emperor Ashoka did not embrace this to attain dominance, did he? His intention was to bring benevolence to his kingdom through his and his children's *karma*. He was a man who had acquired sufficient wealth. Even after Ashoka demonstrated such immense glory of sacrifice, what could the subsequent subjects or vassal kings achieve here?

[GV4:P0473] You must be able to contemplate this at such a profound level. This can be accomplished only if there is love for God. If there is a conviction that the *karma* within us, which causes us to flourish and perish, rests upon that glory of God, then executing this becomes our necessity.

[GV4:P0474] Guru Vani

[GV4:P0475] Santhigiri Janmadina Poojitha Commemorative Edition 2002

[GV4:P0476] The Truth Realized Through Experience

[GV4:P0477] The path of prophetic vision is profound. The prophetic vision of a *yuga* is fulfilled through five Gurus. The influence of each Guru intermingles with the others. The fifth Guru is one who arrives to reveal the characteristics of the forthcoming *yuga* as well. However, the influence of the fourth individual will also be blended into the influence of this fifth individual. That influence will persist until the person of the next *yuga* assumes it. A mistake that can occur during such an assumption is that if the fifth individual, upon observing the truth of the past, makes an error while evaluating the stance of that truth in their own era, everything thereafter will be entirely flawed. Since the *yuga* is changing, there is a possibility of making mistakes. This is how Sathyathranan erred. That mistake was repeated by numerous Gurus who came subsequently. If inexperienced thinkers write about this, a perspective blending the Western mode of thought and Eastern prophetic vision will result.

[GV4:P0478] Among the four *yugas*, *Kaliyuga* has the shortest duration. The chronology determines that *Kaliyuga* itself lasts for four hundred and thirty-two thousand years. *Dwapara* is twice the duration of *Kali*. When *Kali* is added to *Dwapara*, it becomes *Treta Yuga*. When *Kali* is added to *Treta Yuga*, it forms *Krita Yuga*, also known as *Satya Yuga*.

[GV4:P0479] In a *yuga*, a visionary who perceives all this, along with individuals resembling prophets, sages, or Gurus functioning under them, will emerge and operate. When referring to a visionary who observes all this, Sri Krishna can be cited as an example. Before Sri Krishna's birth, royal status was bestowed upon the Yadava clan. Kamsa's downfall was his inability to fully comprehend its significance. However, Kamsa cannot be entirely blamed either. He failed to understand the manifested form that was declared in accordance with the *Yuga Dharma*.

[GV4:P0480] This manifested form is referred to as *Rupapadam*. One can only proceed by relying on the feet of that form. It is the lesser Gurus arriving in that period's influence who completely attain this *Rupapadam*. The divine voice (*ashareeri*) that Kamsa heard was formed as a command from the divine will (*Brahmasankalpa*) to proclaim Sri Krishna's birth prior to it. One can only function by prophetically envisioning and imbibing the Gurus who manifested in the past and brought forth *karma*. Regardless of how great a poet or philosopher one is, numerous doubts will arise. At such times, one can only rely on the *Rupapadam* of the visionary.

[GV4:P0481] The reverence required to reflect upon the reason for delivering a divine voice prior to the visionary's birth, and the quality generated by that reverence, cannot be determined by certain Gurus. For the Guru appearing at the beginning of a *yuga* and those coming intermittently, starting and operating from those divine feet necessitates examining the doctrines of those who came before them.

[GV4:P0482] Sri Krishna is the Guru born between the end of *Dwapara* and the beginning of *Kali*. Gurus appearing under the influence of two thousand, three thousand, five thousand, or ten thousand years associated with these divine feet have nothing to retain or offer here. In this state, it became impossible to comprehend who a visionary is. How much can even the primal Guru who originated a religious doctrine declare? At most, only up to a realization. Realization implies the manifested *dharma*. The form and nature of this manifested *dharma* is not displayed as the form and nature of the immediately preceding *yuga*, but as the form and nature of the *Yuga Dharma*. It commences as one. Sri Krishna arrived by unifying numerous doctrines together. The Gurus coming under him are supposed to elaborate and demonstrate those events.

[GV4:P0483] The temporal determination of each *manvantara* will vary. However, it is not sufficient to merely observe the change in time. One must also examine whether there is an error in the determination of *karma*. Our understanding is that the seventh Manu, Vaivasvata Manu, has also completely executed the determination of *karma*. Similarly, five Gurus appeared for each *yuga* and repeatedly fulfilled all the *Yuga Dharmas*. Documenting and executing the prophetic vision to be expounded in the respective *yugas* is also the very same *karma*. In the *Yuga Dharma*, this *karma* also stands distinct with an image. It is from this that any error occurring anywhere in a *manvantara* can be identified.

[GV4:P0484] For such an identification, seven Gurus will emerge under each of the aforementioned five Gurus.

[GV4:P0485] Sri Krishna came in the capacity of a visionary for numerous such Gurus. Due to the inability to determine *karma* and error in this context, the poet's mode of exposition diverts into another direction. The incident of Sri Krishna opening his mouth to reveal the universe represents this divergently expounded *karma*. It is said that he opened his mouth and showed it to Devaki and Yashoda. Is that the truth of the event?

[GV4:P0486] The history of seven children being beaten to death caused countless emotions of sorrow to flow together for Devaki and Vasudeva. From the time of Sri Krishna's inception, great souls had provided visions to the mother and father, explaining why the eighth child was being born and what all he would accomplish, thus resolving their doubts. The corresponding conviction and courage continued to instill within them. Otherwise, how could a mother and father wait in such a manner and partake in sorrow?

[GV4:P0487] These matters are not to come from the hands of scholars. Nor do they belong in the hands of the great sages who repeatedly appeared under the deities. The gurus who have come and gone from the time of Sree Krishna to the present day belong to periods ranging from two thousand, three thousand, five thousand, to ten thousand years. We see stories of many gurus who appeared in India itself making immense efforts to acquire spiritual powers (siddhis). Writing down stories based on the imaginative conceptions of gods and goddesses, calling them eternal (Sanatana) and so on, disrupts the Yugadharma (the dharma of the epoch). The trinity of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva belongs to the imagination of forest dwellers fabricated in this manner. Those referred to as Adam and Eve also belong to the category of prophets. All of this is stated based on the culture of each land at that time. How much faltering has occurred within these two thousand years to the Christian laws that speak of the old and the new! Can we recognize the life of Christ and the return of Moses today? What is the return? Even after whipping and driving the people who were completely lost in polytheism and bringing them to this side of the Red Sea, the calf's head still remains under their arms!

[GV4:P0488] Gita Govindam and the concept of Meera are examples of the imaginative excellence of poetic assemblies. Both the intellectuals and the unintelligent here hang onto the imaginative splendor of these poetic concepts. Through alphabetical interpretations ranging from the Shabdataravali to the Amarakosha, which purifies vowels and consonants, even Sree Rama is being showcased. The entire population of the world is hanging onto the part that says 'Amara Nirjara Deva'. This chain of hypocrisy has spread and climbed even among the authors of the Vedas and epics, and the authors of the Upanishads. It must be assumed that even the prophets have not been able to recognize this hypocrisy. There is no point in forgetting the truth that we cannot comprehend the blunders that may befall us by getting caught in the path of action, which is praised by combining terms like avatar, guru, and prophet. The blunder that occurred when Sree Krishna was praised in this manner is proof of this. The exact same situation has occurred in the case of Moses as well. It is by adding a bit more imagination that things are said about Jesus: when it was said, 'Let the rock split and move apart', it moved. How should we view the ignorance of the disciples who could not obey the instruction to pray until three in the morning, and the question at the final stage of that life, 'Father, why have you forsaken me?' In what way and by what kind of person should the determination of faith of the Sikh gurus and the divine law residing in the atomic concept of the Jains be corrected?

[GV4:P0489] Mine is the path of an unlettered scholarship, where the answers to these cannot be found through the mere knowledge of alphabets. This is the error I had to face.

[GV4:P0490] It was the time I was performing poojas at Aluva Advaita Ashram. Then, there were some thoughtful people who would come there, enjoy the beauty of nature, sit in the courtyard on the northern side of the ashram, talk about many things as if passing the day, be lost in thought, and spend time writing poetry according to their intellect. I too have often gotten involved in that path of action. Many of them were studying at Aluva UC College at that time. I also had an acquaintance where I stayed away from the knowledge and thoughtfulness of these young men, while at the same time understanding many of their characteristics and enjoying their company. One among them was Narendran, who later became a High Court Judge. The rest of them I recognized during my ashram life. Among them was Chandrabhanu and some others. At that time, there was an Ayurvedic clinic on the way from Palayam to Chempazhanthy through the church cemetery. They used to gather there. The special nature of their good imagination has filled my mind with love. This sweet feeling is still in my mind. One of them later became a sanyasi. When I built a hut in Varkala, I called this sanyasi as if it were a thought. Then his response was like this: 'Whatever is built for Karunakaran is not enough. He has to build his own' . Later, when a hut was built in Pothencode, this person happened to come there too. Before coming to Pothencode, I had asked him an experiential question. To that, he asked me a counter-question brimming with humor: 'Karunakaran has a lot of questions, right?' But after that, I got the proof for this question of mine from a rogue soldier named Pattalam Ramakrishnan. He is the one who revealed the things about Sree Krishna, the eternal celibate Hanuman, and the Brahmarakshas that came to disrupt Vasishta's yagam during Sree Rama's time. Isn't this enough proof that a scholar dressed as a sanyasi does not even have as much knowledge as an experienced devil? Let that be.

[GV4:P0491] The narrative has been constructed to claim that Sri Rama descended into the Sarayu river and attained *jalasamadhi* (spiritual salvation in water). Does this imply that *samadhi* cannot be attained on land? Why was such a fabricated tale recorded? Similarly, Ramatirtha is also said to have attained *jalasamadhi*! If one asks for what purpose, there is no response. If it is argued that they simply renounced this life, then what becomes of the *karma* they accrued through their existence and the power of their penance? These great figures did not merely renounce life; rather, they were led astray. When they realized and were convinced that their path had gone astray, they were confounded—what have I been doing all this while? I need this no longer. The truth is that they simply abandoned it. This is what the Prophet meant when he asked: "What have you done to me, who trusted only in you?" It is for this exact reason that Jesus lamented, "Father, have you too forsaken me?" Did these great souls utter these words without reason?

[GV4:P0492] The souls existing as *Brahmarakshasas* do not enter *Brahmaloka*. They are the ones who performed severe penance, as if standing on the point of a needle. Why does God give birth to a great soul? It is not merely for his own spiritual attainment. Rather, it is to simultaneously fulfill his inherent *dharma*. In contrast, what does Vedanta proclaim? That everything is *maya* (illusion), the *maya* of the Lord. Consequently, the masses were rendered incapable of understanding anything. This is not *maya*; it is reality itself. What one must understand is how to deal with this reality.

[GV4:P0493] The established system of worship remains subordinate to the deities who manifested during the *Treta Yuga* and *Dvapara Yuga*. During those epochs, human beings were incapable of independent action. In the *Kali Yuga*, man is born with agency. It was in such a context that Sri Krishna appeared. Thus, Krishna, who manifested as the primordial Guru (*Adi Guru*), has been depicted merely as a philanderer. It is for this precise reason that the *Gita Govinda* was composed. We merely translate and interpret its meanings. I have not formally studied any of these commentaries. However, I know for a certainty that this is not the truth.

[GV4:P0494] Due to the failure to truly comprehend Sri Krishna, this nation was plunged into ruin. How many Gurus emerged after Sri Krishna! The Buddha, Mahavira, and Guru Nanak appeared. The *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam* (twelve clans born of the Pariah woman) and the eighteen *Siddhas* manifested. Did all these figures appear merely for the sake of singing praises? Yet, we failed to obey even a single one of them. What was the underlying cause of Sri Narayana Guru's sorrow during his final days? His grief stemmed from the fact that there was not a single disciple capable of taking up this mantle. There was no one left to perceive this as the ultimate truth. I am not stating this merely to inform others. I am compelled to articulate the truth that I have witnessed.

[GV4:P0495] Furthermore, having categorically divided traditions into the *Trimurti* system and the *Manu* system, we have been instructed by portraying Manu as the son of Brahma. Is this indeed the truth? Manu is *Swayambhu* (self-manifested). It is the self-manifested Manu who has been inaccurately depicted as Brahma's son. This is mere intellectual gymnastics with words. This is the profound fallacy that has befallen us. No one has been able to transcend this error. Gurus who emerge with the spiritual influence of two thousand, five thousand, or ten thousand years are powerless to rectify this misconception. Divine sanction is absolutely necessary to correct this. What must we do to attain this divine sanction? One must manifest in accordance with the *Yuga Dharma* (the law of the epoch). Having thus manifested, one can only depart after elevating *Dharma* to its rightful state.

[GV4:P0496] I have not acquired formal academic learning. Had I been formally educated, I would not possess the capacity to definitively state what the truth is. However, I can now declare that this is the absolute truth. Once it is affirmed as the truth, one must perceive the profound secret underlying that truth. It is the disciple's duty to perceive this. When Sri Narayana Guru lamented that there was no child left to inherit his legacy, it signified that there was no disciple capable of perceiving the inner secret of the truth. Instead, what do people claim? That he exhibited miraculous powers (*siddhis*), alongside propagating various Vedantic mysteries. Where do we currently stand? If we continue along this trajectory, what shall become of the profound knowledge inherent in our tradition? Rather than rejecting traditional wisdom, one must attain a profound realization of reality and translate it into direct experience. No alternative path will lead to our salvation.

[GV4:P0497] Where do we stand within the framework of *karma* that the *Trimurti* system has conveniently defined as creation, preservation, and destruction? We must cultivate the capacity to comprehend this. To achieve this understanding, we must reach that specific state of realization. Having observed this, one must discern whether it is the *Manu* lineage, the Guru lineage, or the *Rishi* lineage that is truly qualified to perceive it. Subsequently, one must investigate why the *Rishi* lineage failed to attain it, and why the lineage of Prophets was unable to advance further. Unless spiritual liberation is granted to those *Rishis*, Prophets, and Gurus who remain stagnated, incapable of progressing further, no individual can transcend to that ultimate state.

[GV4:P0498] We have established a practice of worshipping everyone. However, apart from merely offering worship, it is impossible to ascertain the specific spiritual plane (*mandala*) in which these deities exist. It is precisely from the plane where they reside that we fail to ascend. Consequently, we fail to derive any spiritual merit from the astrological sign (*rashi*) in which we are born. Unless this condition is liberated, no true benevolence can be attained. This profound act of liberation constitutes the true essence of *Guru Pooja*.

[GV4:P0499] Therefore, one must cultivate a profound understanding of the Guru. Having realized this, one must inquire: what is the true nature of the Guru, and what elements converge within this Guru? Everything referred to as a *Brahmarakshasa*, a *Trimurti*, or a Prophet must ultimately merge within this Guru. That is the true essence of a Guru. It is futile to underestimate anyone. Everyone has contributed to the utmost of their capabilities. Do you genuinely believe that these great souls departed without realizing the exact spiritual state they had attained? They departed with full awareness. Yet, they find themselves unable to progress further. Your intellectual pursuit must be directed toward formulating a *karma* that enables them to advance. That should constitute your paramount sense of duty. If you choose to conceal yourself behind the veil of ignorance propagated by individuals uttering '*Swaha*' or preaching *Advaita*, you will remain incapable of fulfilling your fundamental duty. Let no one harbor the illusion that spiritual attainment is possible without first loving and spiritually liberating our ancestors. That is simply an impossibility.

[GV4:P0500] I am not propounding any complex Vedantic calculations. Rather, I am elucidating the fundamental principles necessary to safeguard the masses within the realm of true knowledge. Instead of protecting the people, are we not merely thrusting them into a bottomless abyss while blindly reciting *suktas* and endlessly reiterating literal, pedantic interpretations? That is not what is required of us. One must comprehend the absolute nature of truth. If we proceed in any other manner, it will constitute a grievous injustice perpetrated against humanity. The Divine will never condone such actions. The assertions of the Vedantins hold no truth. If one fails to discern the underlying reason why these great souls manifested only to endure such profound sorrow, then spiritual inquiry is ultimately futile. This constituted the core of my spiritual investigation. The Divine assisted me in discovering that precise cause. Furthermore, there exists a specific *karma* designed for their liberation. That very *karma* is the *Guru Pooja* performed at Santhigiri.

[GV4:P0501] Guruvani

[GV4:P0502] Santhigiri Janmadina Poojitha Samarpana Pathippu 2002

[GV4:P0503] Darshanasathyam

[GV4:P0504] There exists a profound *karma* structured both in microscopic (atomic) and macroscopic (infinite) forms across the nine celestial spheres. Yogis chart their spiritual trajectory by situating this within the six *chakras* (*aadharas*) and relying upon that precise calculation. As one progresses in this manner, is it not imperative to recognize the entity that exists in the state of formlessness transcending the *Sapta Bhoomikas* (seven spiritual planes)? This profound reality remains imperceptible to the yogis. Until one transcends the realm of the *Navagrahas* (nine planetary spheres), the divine can only be perceived as an indistinct form. For the vision to attain absolute clarity, one's spiritual sight must penetrate the *mandalas* located beyond the *Navagrahas*. To transcend the *Navagrahas*, one must first cross the *Surya Mandala* (the solar plane). All other *mandalas* are positioned such that they envelop the sun. In order to transcend the *Surya Mandala*, the guidance of a Guru is indispensable. This is the ultimate reality. It is also the eternal law. We must actively seek to comprehend the Guru who has attained and established himself in the form of this sublime *mandala*. It is mandated that the presiding deity (*murti*) must be established within this devoted service to the Guru. Subsequently, one must rigorously investigate the specific epoch (*Yuga*) for which that Guru has manifested.

[GV4:P0505] The *Treta Yuga* embodies a distinct truth. The *Dvapara Yuga* equally possesses its own unique truth. What, then, is the fundamental truth of this *Kali Yuga*? What is the merit in claiming that one will remain unaffected by the impurities of *Kali* while actively residing within this epoch? One must realize that it is strictly due to our immense spiritual fortune that we have obtained birth during the *Kali Yuga*. However, the presence of a Guru is absolutely essential to reveal the specific *karma* that serves as the root cause of this great fortune. This intrinsic *dharma* is the absolute truth. Can the truth ever be repudiated? That fundamental reality must be articulated meticulously in accordance with the specific calculations of each *mandala*. That constitutes our ultimate triumph.

[GV4:P0506] Just as this earth has a sky, all other planets and stars have their respective skies. Without knowing about these skies and having a clear understanding of the stars, one cannot go beyond them. When the Prophet (Nabi) saw these nine planets (Navagrahas), he realized that the entire harvest of this flock resides in the moon. Therefore, he placed the moon in the position of karma. But no one else understood this. It was upon seeing this that the Prophet made his pleading prayer: "Oh Father, what have you shown before me, who had believed that there is nothing other than You!" The five daily prayers are a commemoration of this pleading prayer. But no one knows why he is pleading like this—"Why did you send me to this earth inhabited by these lowly people, and what should I do?" According to the laws of the body, this pain is inevitable for anyone, even for any great soul. Those who deny this are merely groping in the dark. The Prophet saw this in the ninth mandala. It was after witnessing the reality ripened therein that this pleading prayer was made. In that state, he sat in that burial ground for three months. And there he attained Samadhi.

[GV4:P0507] It is only after I saw this that I understood this reality. When I became bewildered by the visions obtained from the state of the Devas, I could not comprehend the reasons for it. It took me nine years of searching for the cause of this bewilderment to make it clear to myself.

[GV4:P0508] As far as a Yogi is concerned, he progresses by rejecting everything, saying "Not this, not this" (*Neti Neti*). How can they discard this karma that persists in this Manvantara calculation? For him, there is no karma. Fine, agreed. But who are the karmis (doers of action) associated with him? Do they not need the path of a Guru? If one says that it is not applicable to him, who will uphold this law of nature?

[GV4:P0509] Having been born in the Kali Yuga, we cannot perform the karma of the Treta Yuga. There is no other logic than to understand what its karma is and perform it. Kali is equally applicable to everyone—human, Deva, Rishi, Jnani, Karmi, Bhakta, and Yogi. Only a Guru can provide guidance by recognizing what exists and instructing one to act accordingly. Stating any other logic will not be correct. It is because there was no one among us to understand this and behave accordingly that numerous arguments emerged.

[GV4:P0510] It is indeed true that Islam says God has no form. The formless is a stream of light. Light does have a form. There are hundred, two hundred, or five hundred-watt bulbs, as well as zero-watt bulbs. All of these emit light. If there is light, it has a form too. The only difference is that there are variations in that form. Therefore, what is needed first is to believe that light has variations in form. When this is the truth, who can say that this truth does not exist?

[GV4:P0511] It is when one believes thus that the existence of evil spirits (Pishachas) is perceived. In what all states does a Pishacha exist? The Pishacha exists even up to the state of Brahmarakshas. This Brahmarakshas is referred to as 'Mahan' (great one). Brahmarakshas means one who has progressed aiming solely at Brahman. Where will this end up? They have progressed by rejecting everything, saying "it does not exist, it does not exist," without performing karma. What is the use of someone ascending there while denying the entities in God's conception? Because they are not permitted to ascend there, these forces remain in the middle realms. In the middle of this atmosphere, they stand like absolute aggressors.

[GV4:P0512] I once asked Swami Jagadeeswarananda about this. He is the one who taught the *Brahmasutra* to Swami Agamananda. He had passed the Shastri examination. He had also enrolled and studied in the Vedanta class in Kashi. He spent twenty-one years there studying and teaching. During the time he was teaching the *Brahmasutra* to Agamananda, I was living in the southernmost room of the magazine office near the Samadhi. At that time, I had a habit of waking up late in the night. Jagadeeswarananda used to notice this. I did not know that he was noticing it. I would get up, walk a little along the road, and reach near where they were staying. At one end of the courtyard there, a woven palm leaf was placed. I would go and sit on it for some time. Then I would go to sleep. One day he came and sat next to me, saying, "You rogue." He sat next to me and talked for a while, saying, "Wasn't I watching where you went?" Then I asked him about the clarity and obscurity of light—neither clear, yet not obscure. It has a form. Therefore, it cannot be said to be obscure. But it has no form. I used to see such things. Then he said, "Oh child, you should not ask me about matters of vision. I only have the knowledge that Dr. Sivananda told me such a thing exists."

[GV4:P0513] Rishikesh Sivananda and he had studied together. Rishikesh Sivananda later went to Kashi and lived there in a hut for twelve years. He also used to chant the *Hare Rama* stotram. Through that, he received three or four visions. He mentioned this matter. This Sivananda was a doctorate holder. But he went to Rishikesh saying that this paper was not even fit for scooping bran. While living there, he got a boil on his leg. He could neither walk nor sit. He even suffered the fate of having to crawl on the road. If a poor man lies there, who will pay attention? Then Jagadeeswarananda saw him, hired a horse carriage, and took him to the hospital. He mentioned this matter during their conversation then. He only knows about this from what he had heard him say. He told me that otherwise, he had not even seen the light of a lit incense stick. He knows that this exists. The scriptures say so. But there is no such familiarity among us. There is absolutely no knowledge about the paths suitable for the soul's spiritual merit (Atmasukrutham). It is because even the Sanyasis lack that knowledge that our homes have become ruined. Even families living with some traditional knowledge do not know how to carry forward devotion. There are many ancestors who ended up getting stuck after worshipping Brahmarakshas, Yogi, Karmi, etc. This is the blunder that has befallen all households. This evil spirit has taught them ignorance. When the children in that house grow up, they will become ignorant. I have the experience of interacting with thousands of such families. It was upon seeing the subtle form of this ignorance that these great men cried out in such panic.

[GV4:P0514] There is karma shared here as Deva, Devi, Jnani, Rishi, and Sanyasi. Who can deny this by saying it does not exist? Even in the Rishi tradition, there are those who have reached up to the state of Brahmarakshas. We know that Narada was a Rishi. Which world did this Narada reach and stand in? What is the sense of pride of that world? They lived and demonstrated it before departing.

[GV4:P0515] Saying that what our ancestors worshipped does not exist does not make it non-existent. This certainly exists. What should we do with this? We must take this and surrender it to a Guru or to God. There is no other logic for this. There are Jivatmas in this who have been stuck for epochs. These are karmas that have come after the Treta Yuga and Dwapara Yuga. When the time of Sri Krishna arrived, its base was in Krishna. Krishna became its authority. But we could not revere and accept Krishna. What did we do there? We bothered to interpret and complete the meaning of Vedanta. But that is not what Krishna did. That is why Krishna said, "Arjuna, you are not killing anyone, nor are you causing anyone to be killed."

[GV4:P0516] Guruvani

[GV4:P0517] Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Samarpanappathippu 2002

[GV4:P0518] The Experience of Santhigiri

[GV4:P0519] About five hundred of the people who have been visiting our ashram are experienced. Once they arrive here, they must see me. Otherwise, they will be deeply distressed. When they are unable to see me for many days in such a manner, they will experience certain psychological deficiencies. That is the greatest wrong that can be done to them. Therefore, you must not use rules to stop them. Their experience might be small. But for them, it is significant. This fact must be known to those who stand here and to others. You cannot understand what their specific matter is just by looking at them. They also cannot understand the reason why you are stopping them. It is enough for them to just see me. Their pain will vanish. Otherwise, they will face insurmountable difficulties. After a while, it might even turn into a psychological problem. Hence, if someone feels that they absolutely must see me, you must allow them to do so.

[GV4:P0520] Looking at the nature of some people, one might even wonder if they have any love or faith. No one can understand that. There are many such individuals. This does not mean that they have attained great spiritual states. Some people cause me distress the moment they leave their homes. That does not mean I should not see them. I may be experiencing distress due to the deficiency of their soul or their inherent tendencies. Nevertheless, it must be endured. You must be very careful not to cause them any pain. Similarly, we must be very attentive when serving them food. All of this is a matter related to devotion. If these things are not handled in their proper manner, it will generate a sinful power.

[GV4:P0521] Even those who have been at the ashram for ten or twenty years lack the knowledge of how to handle matters here. For some, whether male or female, these are things that must essentially be done for them. You must consider this as the right of their soul. For some others, even if such things are not done, they have no trouble at all. They will acquire everything by seeing, hearing, knowing, and experiencing. For a soul, all this is necessary until a certain stage is crossed. Some have a lack of ability to understand on their own.

[GV4:P0522] Some people may behave half-crazed. We must never lose our temper with them. We should call them, seat them, advise them on good things, and then send them away. Otherwise, they will suffer from a psychological lack of growth. Even if I say a word to them in jest, that is enough to satisfy them. Out of a hundred people, maybe two will have such problems. Those who stand near me must know many such things.

[GV4:P0523] Here, you must not consider caste or religion. Those are very troubling matters. If some souls happen to leave in sorrow, it will bring certain detriments not only to you but also to the ashram. We must never obstruct the right of a soul. You may feel that they are completely worthless. But you do not know the right of their soul, do you? Whatever the cost, you must impart peace to them before letting them go. Have you not seen me speaking for them on certain occasions, no matter how physically unwell I am? It will not be right if you rigidly adhere to the rules.

[GV4:P0524] Another thing is that some people will feel mentally suffocated, unable to stay here even for two days. Those who stand here must know that matter as well. You must also communicate this among yourselves and understand. Have you not seen me calling some people privately and speaking to them, no matter how lacking in knowledge they are? On some days, at least a thousand such people will come. Can I deal with all of them alone? If, in those situations, you show them the rules instead of showing love and patience, what can I do? You must show affection to everyone. You must not behave toward them like a peon in a government office.

[GV4:P0525] During the time I was wandering, there were many such experiences. No one has ever stopped me. But at the time when I wish to see, I must see certain people. Otherwise, there will be distress. This desire of the mind is a very serious matter. If the circumstances are not right, you may stop them. But you must speak good words to them peacefully. We can see the Guru, you can see and then go, please calm down a little ... When the opportunity arises, you must allow them to see me. They cannot tell you the matter that they have to tell me privately, can they? They can only leave after saying it. Otherwise, they will face great distress. Out of a thousand people, about three hundred people have matters for which they need to see me. About four or five people must see me right then. If they do not see me then, they will experience indescribable distress. If we do not understand and handle this properly, it will become contrary to the will of God. God has such a determination, hasn't He? The goodness that we strive to achieve should not go in vain.

[GV4:P0526] There are some families who come and stay here for days. Such people are not like those who are fine even if they don't get to see (me). They absolutely must see. That is a necessity of their soul. Therefore, we must show compassion to their soul. Do not withhold that compassion. Regarding some people, you might assume, since they see (me) every day, why do they have such great agonies. Do not assume so. It is an issue of their minds becoming corrupted. Similarly, there are some who stay here rendering service. Whenever they feel like seeing, they must see and say certain things. Otherwise, they wouldn't feel like coming here for several days. If they go, those standing there won't allow them to see, then why should they go there—in that sense, they won't come later. Then, it might develop into a small resentment and that resentment will continue. Even if those standing here cannot be careful about this, those who come should have this understanding. Not everyone may have this understanding and love. Therefore, we must act according to the situation, speak in good language, and remove the rigidity of their minds. No matter how difficult it is, you must show that. You should not keep them away by citing other procedures.

[GV4:P0527] When some people come, you might feel that when they were given an opportunity, they stood aloof, and now they have barged in. But that is how they are. They will come when they feel like it, do things when they feel like it, and leave when they feel like it. Even if they cannot see me, they have a desire to receive some *Prasadam* (offering). They must be allowed to leave only after being given the *Prasadam*. If you do not do so, a lapse will occur on account of that. If that lapse happens, no matter how great the things you do, your compassion will be lost. This will cause harm to your life.

[GV4:P0528] I am entrusting you with the work of removing the stains from the souls of others, which I have established—that you should do things in such and such a manner. After entrusting you with that duty (*Karma*), I am not asking you to observe any severe vows or austerities. Without such severe observances, would anyone normally agree to let you surrender all your flaws? Can any individual take upon themselves the flaws of even a single person? What is being done here? You have found a place to unload thousands or crores of burdens. What is the secret of this? As long as you do not understand this, there is no point in my saying any of this.

[GV4:P0529] I am not teaching anything to anyone in a structured manner. When they gain experience, I will take some time and speak to such people. Everyone realizes for themselves the old tendencies of the soul, the course of *Dharma*, and what errors have occurred in that *Dharma*. Like the saying *Jagrat, Swapna, Sushuptinam Sakshi Poorti* (perfect witness to the waking, dream, and deep sleep states), the Guru, standing as a witness, transforms your *Karma*. After that, you ascend to the different states of *Turiya* and *Turiyatita*. For that, you only need to depend on the Guru. You do not need to look up to any deity, sage, or spirit. All these will appear before you even without you calling them. What you elders do not get, your children will get. There is a saying for this here: If given to elders, they will ruin it. As for children, as they grow, this experiential aspect will grow in their flesh, blood, and marrow, and it will also grow in their intellect. Along with that, love, humility, and respect will also grow. Instead, what do the elders say? "I have seen and known a lot in life; I am superior to others." On top of that, they will read the *Bhagavata* and explain its meaning. Likewise, they will talk about the *Puranas* as well.

[GV4:P0530] I am not talking about any of these. I am talking about the *Karma* that is the cause of these *Puranas* and *Itihasas*. That *Karma* is the *Gurupooja* that I have done for you. By performing that *Karma* and removing the base elements in each course of *Karma*, the great ones are maintained as great ones. They are elevated slightly from where they stood. Just as you were born and came here, through the Guru, you will be saved by the recurring special feature of the *Dharma* across future lifetimes. There is no distinction of male or female, young or old for this. Everyone who has the innate fortune for it will receive it. Thus, by the seventh generation, you will become a pure human lineage. You need not show any vanity, boastfulness, or justification in this. This is something to be achieved even at the risk of your life. There is no meaning in saying that you spent time or money for this purpose. That talk is ignorance; it is empty prattle.

[GV4:P0531] This knowledge must first arise in the wealthy. Only if there are wealthy people can any good be done for the land. The *Karma* combining knowledge, humility, respect, and fortune will come only through him. When a certain *Karma* proves useful, if the machine that deceives man can perform some aspects of maturing a human being, what cannot be achieved if you walk the path through that truth! By wandering around Kashi, Rameswaram, Vrindavan, Ayodhya, and going to Rishikesh and Badrinath, you will not grasp even one aspect of this truth. You are not going to gain this virtue by wandering around using your status and spending money. Haven't you seen the ministers and great leaders here going to see the Lord? They can go and see the Lord anywhere, anytime, right? For some other leaders, they don't have to go anywhere to see. They can see directly from where they sit. If there is socialism, they can see quite a bit more. I am not speaking for them. It is for you. If politicians are beaten with thorns, their skin peels, and blood flows, it is good for them. They can flaunt themselves as martyrs, right? It is always good for him. Whether he dies or not, it is a virtue. Aren't you swallowing all this foolishness and attaining absolute freedom? Falling into this complete trickery called absolute freedom, dying and rotting without liberation from *Tantras*, *Mantras*, or any kind of liberation at all—what else is special about it?

[GV4:P0532] Didn't I tell you earlier, pour out all your sinful energies, let them all be exhausted. For that, I will not say that you must observe any celibacy (*Brahmacharya*) or vow. But I will say that you must live without forsaking *Dharma*. When you realize what that *Dharma* is, celibacy will naturally become a safeguard for it. No one needs to tell you to do so. When you understand for yourself what you need through that discipline, it will happen on its own. Then you will not go wrong anywhere.

[GV4:P0533] What is celibacy (*Brahmacharya*)? When you finish performing *Gurupooja*, this god, goddess, sage, ascetic, and everything else come, bow down before the Guru, and attain liberation. At least one child in the house performing *Gurupooja* will see this. It is not enough if you do *Gurupooja* alone. It will not be effective if the rest of the family stays away. At the very least, the father, mother, and children in the house should see this as the truth. Once the *Gurupooja* is done, you should not invite any other calamities. If you say that the grandmother and grandfather were accustomed to it, so I cannot help but be accustomed to it too, then nothing can be done. What is this habit? That it is enough to call out "Narayana" at the time of death. Another one is that, when angry, there is no satisfaction unless some wicked things are spoken. There is a sense of pleasure in uttering twisted words that somehow destroy a person and bring disrespect to the Guru. This is a kind of trickery. How many such families do we have! All this is the remnant of ignorance imparted by foolishness. This has completely destroyed our *Dharma*.

[GV4:P0534] By performing Guru Pooja, the path to the spiritual merit (atma sukrutham) of gods, goddesses, sages, and ascetics is cleared. That is why one is able to see all those forces directly. I am not saying that spiritual merit has been achieved, but the path to it has been cleared. The dharma that can be directly experienced is realized here. What use is it to you if I perform some kind of impersonation instead of this? What has actually happened here? The baseness that resided in your life has been completely destroyed. How many crores of rupees would it cost to achieve this?

[GV4:P0535] What is the experience in a home where Guru Pooja is performed? How do the past Gurus stand, how do the sages and the wise stand, and how does it radiate light into the ages to come? This is the familiarity that the children in your home acquire to witness this. By standing as a witness in all three states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, the Guru extracts both your good and bad. Giving the good to your life, he accepts the bad and destroys it. Thus, you become purified in the karmic aspect known as the purity of the vessel. That Karma Yoga is what is being given to you.

[GV4:P0536] Oh Godٹ. Oh Guruٹ. Just this one call. You do not need to do anything more than this for it. Your karma is reaching the destiny of your home, land, and country. Having ten children as mentioned earlier is enough to achieve this Karma Yoga. Then what did you get as the guardians of these children? The merit of being able to donate your children for the land and the country. With that, your lineage prospers. But if you cannot preserve such a great karma, there will be destruction of that magnitude. God gave you the opportunity to take up God's karma and to become its owners. Do not hoard it, quarrel over it, and trample it down. Not even a single word in this regard should be trampled down. You do not have the authority to trample it down even with a single glance. You should work entirely for goodness and preserve this for the spiritual merit of the children across multiple births. That merit is a karma that becomes the Guru, becomes God, and helps in attaining salvation across births.

[GV4:P0537] What are you placing and offering in the place of God? A venomous snake. This is your tradition. Life must be transformed into different states. Then, standing as a human, standing as a god, standing as a sage, and transforming this tradition, our Guru Pooja is the theory of evolution of a soul waiting for the spiritual merit across births. Will God be in your hands no matter how many crores you spend? If so, God should be in the hands of those who spend thirty and fifty crores to build temples.

[GV4:P0538] I am not telling you any of this. Giving a share of what you eat, a share of what you drink, showing decency in everything you do, and behaving with mutual respect towards each other, just one call "Oh God" is enough. You should call nothing else but "Oh God, Oh Guru". Because that call is not mine, it becomes yours. Because God has given you and me the opportunity to be born and made you my contemporaries. There should be no stubbornness among yourselves, and no lack of humility. "He is my brother, she is my sister, if they suffer a shortcoming, it is my shortcoming too, and taking it upon myself is my dharma." I am asking from you children who will put this into practice and show it. You do not need to do anything else for me. Instead, if you raise your children, husband, and wife according to your desires, get hurt, and fall into the core of sorrow, I will not be able to do anything. I am giving you the karmic ability to voluntarily withdraw from that sorrow.

[GV4:P0539] What should you think about? When your children grow up near you, what all should you give them to raise them? You who live by blaming your husband, blaming your wife, and blaming your children must understand one truth—all this is your predestined karma.

[GV4:P0540] I have not spoken Vedanta to you. I have only told you the truth from my experience to the best of my knowledge. You must take it completely. This is my requirement. This is not a careless asceticism. It is an asceticism that has come through sacrifices over multiple births. No one will get this without making sacrifices. I am giving you the proof of that sacrifice. If you want, you can take this and believe it. I am not asking if you have the knowledge for it or not. I am not asking your caste or religion. I am not teaching that you will benefit if you stay separated from your wife or husband. I am not saying to leave her if she is no good. Look after them as much as possible, if there is no other way, then let go.

[GV4:P0541] The Malayarayars have a specific tradition when they go to meet the king. They retain the bottom-most node of a bamboo stalk and knock off all the others. The topmost portion is sealed with wax. They fill this bamboo with honey and delicacies made of flattened rice, bring it before the king, toss all these items backward, and then fall forward to offer their obeisance. The obeisance is performed with hands placed behind the back. What was the consequence of their custom being such? The devil, blessed by the frenzied dancing of these Kappiris (spirits), stands there. It is this devil that makes them don such costumes. The *Theyyam* dance and similar practices have evolved through continuous refinements of this custom. This represents our primitive method of invoking the divine. We must critically reflect upon what we stand to gain from such practices.

[GV4:P0542] Do not raise children by merely providing them with education and wealth, thereby making them useless to society. They must be given what is ordained by their destiny. You must formulate the destined karma, the karma that they are meant to assimilate through their lives. This is the karma for you to unite with me. Apart from this, you should not assume that you can achieve anything else by living in this world. It is your accomplishment to be able to cultivate such a karma and a corresponding faith. Ultimately, that will translate into the world's accomplishment. This constitutes the secret of *Guru Puja*. It is the light serving as the foundation of this karma that the children here perceive being revered by gods, goddesses, sages, ancestors, ascetics, and even the *Trimurtis*, including Maha Vishnu. And then they declare, "Children ٹ, do not let this go astray; for their salvation depends entirely on keeping this flawless."

[GV4:P0543] This is what you must take as evidence, rather than attributing this to any kind of mystical power of mine. If I stretch out my hand, nothing will appear from thin air. I do not possess the magical knowledge to stretch out my hand and produce gold. I only possess what God has bestowed upon me. I share that with you. By sharing this and putting you through difficulties, I pray that you attain the fruits of your past life's struggles. Thus, when the contemplation of the soul becomes firmly established in you, you must realize what spiritual merit (*Atmasukrutham*) is—this is my desire.

[GV4:P0544] What is meant by this difficulty? Did I not say earlier, "Let everything of mine be yours, both the bad and the good." When such a dedication occurs, certain afflictions will befall the body and mind. Can you at least conceptualize this? You will not attain this from any other place. They will simply tell you to worship anyone you please. Or else, they will instruct you to worship by including this or that specific item.

[GV4:P0545] Here, by performing the *Guru Puja*, we are revealing to your children the karmic potential that encompasses everything from spirits and ghosts residing in Vaishnava, Shaiva, and Shaktheya concepts, up to deities, sages, and ascetics. It is not I who am demonstrating this. It is an agency of God. God is manifesting in my form. Having assumed such a form, the divine appears before you in accordance with your conception.

[GV4:P0546] Have you not heard of Uddhava? History states that Uddhava looked exactly like Sri Krishna. When Uddhava developed a doubt, Krishna told him, "Then go to a house where I am not present." Wherever he went, Krishna was there. Uddhava was no ordinary person, after all. He was well-versed in philosophy and Vedanta. His doubt was why Krishna was manifesting before these women (the Gopis). It was to understand this that Uddhava went to them. When Uddhava arrived, it was Krishna whom they saw. They asked, "Why did you take the trouble to come here? Had you called, we would have come to you." Upon comprehending this experience, Uddhava was terrified. These women were masters of their own minds. For many lifetimes, they had been *Brahmavadinis*. *Brahmavadinis* are those who perceive the ultimate form within Brahman and expound upon it. They are beings who have taken billions of births. The vision is granted to such evolved souls. How can ordinary people understand this? These Gopi women, being *Brahmavadinis*, were perceiving the form of Krishna within Brahman. How have you understood such a Sri Krishna?

[GV4:P0547] What you are witnessing is the vision of Krishna coming and bowing down to the Guru who has carried forward that tradition without letting it be lost. You must not assume that it is me whom Krishna is bowing to. Brahman has assumed my form and stands before you. That is what is being revered.

[GV4:P0548] There is a story in the *Bhagavata*. A Yaksha took a blade of grass and threw it into the assembly of Devendra. Then he called the Devas one by one. First, Agni (the god of fire) was called. He could not burn that blade of grass. Then Varuna was summoned, but he failed. Vayu also failed. No one could even move this blade of grass. Then Devendra declared that the one who had come as the Yaksha was Brahman. The Devas were unable to perceive the true nature of Brahman. The soul capable of seeing this was bestowed with the title of Devendra. That is, he was granted the position as the Indra of the Devas. However, even such a Devendra acted foolishly. That is why he incurred the curse of Sage Gautama.

[GV4:P0549] If we live recognizing the truth in history, how can you realize the truth without properly cultivating the ability, competence, love, and corresponding reverence to grasp it? All of this is evident. But even the soul that experienced this direct realization has no liberation. That is what Devendra's experience proves. So, what is the inherent spiritual competence required to transcend into the state of liberation? This is what we must actualize through our lives.

[GV4:P0550] This experience rests in your hands as clearly as a gooseberry, or like yielding gold. You must manifest this in your lives. It depends entirely on your unity and your way of life. Forgetting caste, religion, and class, you must unite as one, and the merit of that karma must reflect in your ancestral lineage (*pitrutvam*). Then, transforming into deities and sages, they must be born as children in your homes. The *Guru Puja* performed here serves as the guiding light for this karma.

[GV4:P0551] What is your comprehension today, what is your requirement, and what is your absolute necessity? What is the truth that emanates from it? It is to comprehend this that you ought to come here. One need not become an ascetic to acquire this from here and impart it to one's children. In the disposition of men and women born as human beings, the female householder (*Grihadharmini*) who adheres to the duties of household life (*Grihadharma*) must be exceptionally competent. The obligation to render her husband worthy also resides with her. It is such a woman who is elevated to the stature of a *Brahmavadini*. In the householder's stage of life (*Grihasthashrama*), one should not anticipate miracles; rather, it is an earnest endeavor to perceive the light of truth. In that endeavor, the husband, wife, and children immerse themselves together. It is for that specific undertaking that you are instructed to surrender everything here. Merely surrendering everything is insufficient; one must also pray fervently.

[GV4:P0552] What is the nature of prayer? It is not merely chanting while sitting with folded hands. Whatever task you perform, you should pray. Prayer must permeate every action. It should reach all virtuous actions as well as base actions. The Guru will elevate this prayer from all those actions. That is why it is said: word is truth, truth is Guru, and Guru is God. You must experience that divine presence. To experience this most subtle of subtle truths, one must transcend the states of wakefulness (*Jagrat*), dream (*Swapna*), and deep sleep (*Sushupti*) and ascend higher. This is a truth that no one has ever articulated before. By witnessing, hearing, and knowing this, make your life blessed. Through that, you will acquire the capability and competence to rectify the errors committed by your father, mother, or ancestors. That must be attained from God. That is our immense fortune.
