[GV4:P0555] What Those Living in the Lineage of the Guru Must Heed

[GV4:P0556] We possess a culture that has led a severely degraded manner of living. Because knowledge is highly constricted, there is an arrogance within all of us that authority is the benchmark of knowledge. The ego of 'I' exists in all human beings. There are even those who harbor resentment for being criticized. They lack the wisdom to realize that being corrected is beneficial. Ignorance is more prevalent among women. Irrespective of age, shortcomings exist among both the lowest and the highest strata. The majority of girls live without ever contemplating where they were born, why they were born, or how they were raised. They possess an inclination to merely dress up and wander about, completely unwilling to do any work or get any work done. Each individual is far removed from their respective duties. This condition has arisen because every household possesses a lineage of living in ignorance for an extended period. It is a tradition of living a sedentary life, consuming without ever engaging in labor. Each one of us is the progeny of this depravity. Caste-based conflicts can be observed everywhere. Aside from engaging in such struggles, no one knows how to contemplate the proper upbringing of girls.

[GV4:P0557] If this practice is to change, an appropriate administration must emerge. For that to happen, one must pray with an aching heart, beseeching the eradication of the ignorance that has infiltrated this human society. Pray also that this land does not deteriorate due to our overflowing passions. Pray that all the absurdities witnessed in this world be reduced to ashes and perish. The foremost thing you must do is to implore God, asking for a way to remove these deficiencies from our progeny, and for the mindset and action required to achieve it. You will undoubtedly experience transformation.

[GV4:P0558] You possess a lack of administrative experience. The deficiencies of those who perished by committing treachery in governance can only be rectified through divine grace. Maintaining strict discipline in prayer will yield immense results. You are individuals who are incapable of loving one another by speaking kind words. No matter how much improvement occurs, a sense of deficiency remains deep within. One must pray for deceptive thoughts to depart from the world entirely.

[GV4:P0559] What great souls proclaim does not materialize immediately. Believing the words of Jesus that heaven would arrive, one had to wait for 1500 years. Work must be executed swiftly. Otherwise, impurity will adulterate the action. While performing an action, it must be done with noble intentions. When those who have acted in such a manner are reborn, they will possess 10 hands (extraordinary capability). Yet, they will not exhibit corresponding arrogance.

[GV4:P0560] An opportunity similar to what Moses received was bestowed upon India in the exact same measure. However, a submissive nature of worship, incapable of seizing that opportunity, had already been prevailing here. According to Hindu scriptures, there were four eras (*Chaturyugas*). Preceptors (*Acharyas*) existed as authorities for each *Chaturyuga*. Prior to the commencement of the *Kali Yuga*, Sri Krishna arrived and rejected all the rituals that had existed until then. Yet, all the actions of Sri Krishna became submerged in myths. Krishna was tethered among gods and goddesses. That should never have happened. Krishna declared that one should forsake everything that existed until then and worship him alone. Moses was not as pure a soul to that extent. When Moses was born, the people were slaves of the Pharaoh. The Pharaoh knew beforehand that Moses would be born among these downtrodden people. Therefore, he continually executed all the newborn male children. The background of Sri Krishna's birth was also exactly like this, was it not? When the Pharaoh killed all the male children, Moses' parents somehow raised their son in hiding and prayed fervently. Then, they set him afloat in the water. The king's daughter and her maids saw him, realized he was a slave child, and entrusted him back to his own mother. She raised him until the age of 4 and then handed him back to the palace. During none of these instances was Moses imparted with spiritual wisdom. Upon reaching adulthood, while living in hiding at a shepherd's house, he married an honest girl in accordance with the divine word he received. It was there that his baptism of wisdom occurred.

[GV4:P0561] India is the birthplace of numerous great souls. Consequently, the *Varnashrama Dharma* and the *Trimurti* system are, in reality, unnecessary for India. The Prophet had received revelations. However, it was also stated that it would be conveyed only when requested. The prayer conducted at Santhigiri has been revealed from the Supreme Light. When that prayer was practiced, since 1973, everything began to be fulfilled for us. It is the girls who have received the immense fortune to perform this. Through this, we have also been able to eradicate the corruption that caused the degradation of women.

[GV4:P0562] Because they were able to believe and act upon what the Prophet proclaimed 1500 years ago, it has become a reality today. Similarly, even if the present generation does not comprehend what is being stated today, God has a specific purpose in making us pray and act at present. Everything revealed here has been meticulously preserved here. It cannot be disclosed now. It can only be revealed after this generation.

[GV4:P0563] The foundational nature of all the affairs of our ashram has been derived through prayer. A situation will emerge in the future where the world will understand the purpose behind our prayers. An action named 'Completion' was performed here 34 times. Those completions were in the nature of the 27 constellations. In 1973, 27 of them were completed. It was on the day the 27th was completed that the revelation was received: "The matters I had desired across eons have been fulfilled."

[GV4:P0564] This atmosphere is filled with the germs of perfection. Men and women handle things very carefully here. Their every word, every look and every expression will be absorbed into this atmosphere and linger. It will never fade from their lives. This is the stage where Dayananda Saraswathi, Rishikesham Sivanandan, Sankarachariyar – everyone has failed. If you can use your ability and energy for this, there is no greater fortune.

[GV4:P0565] It is your work that I love, not money. This idea is the result of a great sacrifice and I need the determination and pain to sacrifice anything to honor it. Humility, and along with humility, a care in speech, Appa! I do many things, I make many things happen; you must also maintain a pleading prayer that you should always make me do according to your will. This will only be correct if there is a dedication to offer one's life for this. Those who work today, even if they are a child, if they carry this forward without mistake, there is no doubt that their names will be etched in the pages of history. It may perhaps take one or two generations for that.

[GV4:P0566] This fortune is something your ancestors did not get. This fortune is one that will never be subjugated to anything or anyone. The great sinful power of killing the Prophet's children and seizing power is the reason why murder and killing happen wherever Muslims take power. Therefore, your life and the mischief in life must be untied and resolved here.

[GV4:P0567] The experience here is like getting a new earth. Before getting it, one does not know what it is. Earth here refers to the body. Many things are stored in the godown of the heart. It should be kept without spoiling. No matter how hard it is, one must be able to complete it. A state should be reached where we do not need both sin and merit. If merit is earned, then one has to be born again to experience its fruit. If you strengthen your mind, no one can defeat you. You cry when pain comes. Even through that crying, you must pray that you can do His will.

[GV4:P0568] We do not need Siddhi. Siddhi is a feature of a time. It is enough if Siddhi works as a feature of that time. Siddhi is not needed for this time. Sree Krishna showed the complete nature of Siddhi and stopped. Hereafter, Siddhi is not allowed. God is leading us to the Satya Yuga. For that, one must do there and take here. You do not have to do anything for God. You have to do it with a broken heart and take the fruit of that pain. Do not act and repeatedly let the mind go into mischief. If you have done even an inch, you should never go back. Everyone's good qualities should be modeled. There is something to learn even from a small creature. By learning from everything, you must have the determination that at least one person should become good through my action.

[GV4:P0569] The greatest Guru of a Manu lineage will get ten male and ten female disciples. That depends on the Guru's luck. Among these, three will be excellent, seven will be mediocre, and the rest will be those who reach only up to God-light. They will not merge in Brahma-light. However many others were in that Manu lineage, in the next birth they will attain salvation only as members or servants of this Guru lineage. There is another group, those who have vision, rise a little and then fall without doing anything. Another group are family people. They will carry everything in moderation, lead a family life and eventually attain salvation. Or they will join the Guru. Neither of these two groups should have doubts about the Guru. If any doubt arises like that at any time, one can attain salvation by confessing to the Guru that a doubt arose about the Guru at such a time, and seeking a remedy. Even householders can reach the state of the Trinity if they do not make mistakes. Or if a mistake is made, depending on the magnitude of the mistake, they will be born many times and at some time accept the discipleship of an elevated Guru of this Guru lineage and attain salvation through that. People who come to the group of this Guru or Guru lineage and stay for some time and then reject and leave, it is difficult to get a human birth itself in subsequent births. Even if a human birth is obtained, there will be absolutely no knowledge. Later, by praying to get knowledge, experiencing through many births in some other lineage, they will merge in the position of the Trinity. Another group stands close to the Guru and the lineage, rises quite high on their own, and after reaching a state in that rise where generally no one can find fault, makes a mistake due to jealousy or some other defect in action. The physical condition given to such people will be such that they will not be able to work in any way for the attainment of God. It is also possible that they will have complete devotion and humility in some birth. From that, by giving many births, seeing many Gurus, in a birth where the mind is tired and grieving, God will show mercy and give a healthy birth again and give salvation through it. After searching for it, getting tired and helpless, it will be obtained only through severe sacrifice. There is still another group. Being born through many births, wandering and suffering by worshiping in Shaktheya, Saiva, and Vaishnava traditions for ages, in the final birth they will be among Gurus in two thousand, three thousand years, and then they will achieve elevation according to the arrival of those Gurus. This is only a brief description of the very detailed vision side.

[GV4:P0572] The Path of Dharma Dictated by God

[GV4:P0573] Whatever we do, there will invariably be some shortcomings and injustices within us. What should be the aspects we share collectively to rectify these deficiencies? There are two pathways for this. First, through the meritorious rights (*punyavakasam*) we have acquired by fulfilling the dutiful actions (*karmadharma*) mandated by our householder duties (*grihadharma*). Second, the action that liberates one from the cycle of actions—having traversed the stages of the ascetic (*yogi*), the wise (*jnani*), the dutiful (*karmi*), and the devotee (*bhakta*)—must also emerge from the foundation of the actions you perform. It should not stem from our independent intellect. Instead, each of you serves as the foundational stone to cultivate that fervent thought known as divine will or *Brahmanischayam* within yourselves, and impart it to your young children or the great souls yet to be born. In this, there is no distinction of male or female, young or old. There is no caste, religion, or class.

[GV4:P0574] Today, a situation exists wherein a *Shudra* can access and function in any sphere. However, despite attaining full *Shudra* rights, without comprehending the true essence of a *Shudra*, they continue to gaze upwards, thereby rendering the *Shudra* devoid of true knowledge. Instead of wisdom, mischief, base emotions, and pervasive casteism were imparted to them, and these have now proliferated to an extent where they can never be eradicated. To resolve this predicament, the divine will itself is essential. To become a participant in this divine will, one must inevitably embrace a *Gurumargam* (the path of the Guru).

[GV4:P0575] A pathway for this is precisely what has been revealed to Santhigiri. This path is paramount. The world has never received such a pathway until now, nor will it receive one hereafter. Such a profound ideology has been bestowed upon us as the divine entity itself. It is this very ideology that all preceptors and prophets, residing as indwelling spirits (*antaryamis*), are continuously safeguarding for us. The framework of this action (*karma*) is designed in a manner to procure such protection from those spiritual powers. Henceforth, the requisite discipline, order, and systematic procedure for this must be attained through your traditional adherence to the path. A specific way of life must be formulated to proceed in accordance with this system.

[GV4:P0576] This is not a lifestyle dictated by any particular religion or caste. However, it will serve as a corrective measure to the existing ways of life. Regardless of whether one is a Hindu, Christian, Muslim, Buddhist, Jain, or anyone else, a situation will emerge in the future where they will accept directives from this way of life. This is being offered to the world as our magnificent contribution. For this, you must possess a fundamental understanding.

[GV4:P0577] How can that knowledge be acquired?

[GV4:P0578] This land is fortunate to be conducive to this action (*karma*). If asked how this land attained such fortune, that is an entirely different subject. At some stage in the history of this land, those who lived here must have possessed a certain inherent goodness. Be that as it may, a great fortune has befallen this land. If people, knowingly or unknowingly, deny it, it is not their fault. In the future, this fortune will at least serve them to impart it to their descendants.

[GV4:P0579] Today, quite a considerable number of people visit Santhigiri. Devoid of caste, religion, or class distinctions, what is being shared here with all of them is the complete manifestation of a relentless endeavor aimed at creating a traditional lineage, eradicating the detrimental aspects of actions accumulated over countless lifetimes, and cultivating love, glory, faith, devotion, and dutiful action as a heritage. No matter how much effort you exert to share this, it is never excessive. It possesses a nectar-like glory that remains inexhaustible no matter how long one acts upon it. In order for you all to have the strength to act in this manner, I am conveying this as a declaration.

[GV4:P0580] All of you must unite and embrace this *Brahmanischayam*, without any distinction of male or female, young or old. As the ignorant *Shudra* class, we must undertake it and facilitate others to undertake it to the best of our abilities. Rather than limiting it to the *Brahmin*, *Kshatriya*, and *Vaishya*, we must effect a transformation in all living beings and rightfully claim it for the dawn of the *Satyayuga*. *Kaliyuga* is the era born for us to earn the right to attain liberation in the *Satyayuga*. You must collectively embrace this by reciting a solemn pledge (*satyavakku*).

[GV4:P0581] Solemn Pledge (*Satyavakku*):

[GV4:P0582] Correcting the errors that have occurred to us and our lineage thus far, and turning towards the righteous path—the path divinely granted to us through the Guru lineage—we solemnly vow before the ultimate truth of the Guru that we shall comprehend and introduce that *Brahmanischayam*, which accords with the divine will, to the best of our knowledge, embracing it and handling it appropriately.

[GV4:P0585] The Pathway to Purify the Guru Lineages

[GV4:P0586] The primary objective of Santhigiri is to bestow peace and tranquility upon the world. The action we perform for this is akin to dragging a mountain tied with a flimsy thread. If it succeeds, it is a colossal mountain that is moved; if it fails, only a fragile thread is lost. We must cultivate a nature of love imbued with such profound caution. Only after we reciprocally experience and realize the love of that action will we attain true goodness.

[GV4:P0587] No matter how chaotic people may be when they arrive, they become serene once they reach here. The reason for this is the profound glory that has permeated this atmosphere through our prayers. Previously, individuals came here seeking healing for illnesses. Gradually, knowledgeable persons and those inquisitive about spiritual matters began to arrive. That, too, is the fruition of our prayers. The Almighty will grant us double the results of what we undertake. Even the most highly educated person who visits will bow before us. Once, a sage (*sanyasi*) came and remarked that the sublime quality of the air he breathed upon entering these gates was beyond words. The sage also stated that he had never experienced such a deeply pristine atmosphere in any other ashram. That, again, is the powerful result of our prayers.

[GV4:P0588] Because the atmosphere of our ashram is pure, no one with undesirable character traits can simply walk in. There exists a subtle spiritual environment here wherein such individuals cannot sustain their presence. You only need to contemplate on what to do with the time you receive here and how to utilize it properly; the corresponding results will naturally follow. The influx may be minimal, but the divine prosperity (*aiswarya*) is immense.

[GV4:P0589] The chaotic spectacles witnessed in the world today must be obliterated. That is our aim. Even if merely a few among you step out into the society and act, all these turbulences will perish, and both material and spiritual abundance will gain strength in the land. Therein lies God's compassion towards us. While engaging in any action, your resolve must be this: this ideology must endure, bringing eternal peace and tranquility to the world. While working, there should be no egoistic feeling that 'I am the one who did all this or brought this about.' Such an attitude will be detrimental. Whether someone sees it or not, 'I am doing this out of love for God, not to show off to anyone'—this is how you should think. If you think with good intellect and act mindfully, goodness will naturally manifest in your actions without your knowledge. Through your actions, this atmosphere must remain serene, now and always. It must be full of glory. Regardless of who among you does what work or from where, everyone must collectively pray for it to come to the forefront. Those working inside the ashram and those working outside must understand each other and share love. That is genuine love, the true merit.

[GV4:P0590] When one state fades and the capacity for action transitions into another more robust state, numerous obstacles will arise. At that juncture, if you perform dedicated actions completely devoid of arrogance, it will lead to the ultimate goal. There must always be a continuous prayer: "Oh God, may the actions, big or small, that I perform be fruitful; whatever I offer, may it be effective." There will sometimes be moments when devotion swells, the mind becomes full, and resolutions emerge as if catching fire. If you act vigorously at that exact time, all negativities will be severed. Everyone must pray for those who act and those possessing true vision to come forward. That is highly essential for the elevation of this lineage. Through the lineage to the nation, and then to the entire world—this is the expansive nature of this ideology.

[GV4:P0591] Our thought must be how to impart the love of God to these blinded people. Before that, we should also think about what the consequence will be if we worship God and if the love of God arises. We have a misconception that worshipping God will bring complete happiness. Do not assume so. This body itself is the cause of sorrow. For those who worship God, sorrows may come linked like a chain. This is because the latent tendencies (vasanas) residing in us over ages through countless births are being untied one by one. Intermittently, happiness will also come. Weight must be given to that happiness. That is indestructible happiness. However, there are those who live according to what they see without paying attention to any of this, who consider themselves knowledgeable and are considered so by others. We can see them going to places like London and Paris for their own happiness and to bring happiness to others. Only by going there do they find happiness! At the same time, if their own mother is lying sick nearby, they do not even get the time to go and see her. If the father and mother have money, they will find time to inquire about them.

[GV4:P0592] Coming here is not like going to a market, hospital, temple, or to hear a political speech. There is a love here that transcends all of that. Everyone participating in the unbroken chanting of the holy name (Akhanda Namajapam) here attains a sense of peace, knowingly or unknowingly. Those who come here somehow blend in with the practices here. A peace is attained from this atmosphere and from certain individuals standing here. It is an experience that even if it does not translate into action, a sense of peace is attained. The reason for that is God bringing our actions to fruition. You must carefully preserve that compassion. In the future, another goodness will emerge from this atmosphere. That has been accumulated here a long time ago. It is the foundation required for this lineage (Parampara).

[GV4:P0593] What is the nature of this era? It has become corrupted by the spread of demonic nature (Asuratvam). During my childhood, there was a time when producing an unnecessary sound or word was considered a mistake. Today, it is the exact opposite. Today has become an era ruled by the demonic (Paisachikam). God has a determination to change this. To change it, many pains will have to be endured. That pain is first experienced by the renunciate (Sanyasi). He will not get any favorable help, facility, or circumstance for this. The surroundings will be adverse to him in every way. Not only will no one obey him, but the exact opposite will occur forcefully. If he possesses a spiritual side, all demonic forces will accumulate and torment him inexpressibly. However, there is no difficulty where an oracle (Komaram) dances after sacrificing a rooster. Those with the nature of an oracle will not be able to stand here if they come. But there are some Sanyasis who seem to have reached the perfection of renunciation. They are the ones in whom devotion and humility stand strengthened. Such people will unknowingly stay here. The reason for this is that there is not even a trace of the demonic here.

[GV4:P0594] To completely eliminate the demonic, we established a ritual here some time ago. God revealed it as 'Completion' (Poortheekaranam). We have been shown altogether two thousand four hundred and forty-four Gurus and their lineage. Among them, the first seven Gurus in the highest tier have ten thousand crore followers each. The rest have four thousand crore each. We have eradicated all the demonic elements in these Guru lineages. We have also united the Gurus and their lineages in the divine light. It took four and a half years to purify these Guru lineages that stood corrupted in the atmosphere. Even after that, many completions took place. Finally, in 1973, an intimation was received from the Supreme Brahman that what I had desired for aeons was fulfilled. With this, the disciple lineage of these Gurus (from 1973) has been taking birth all over the world. Children higher than them will come and be born in this lineage. All the prayers and intentions taking place here are for that purpose.

[GV4:P0595] Guruvani

[GV4:P0596] Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Dedication Edition 2002

[GV4:P0597] Yati Pooja

[GV4:P0598] Sanyasi Pooja Models to be Practiced by the Santhigiri Lineage

[GV4:P0599] Letters should be sent to invite the Sanyasis to the place where they reside, wherever that may be. A money order must be sent for the Sanyasis' round-trip travel expenses. One should go and receive the Sanyasis wherever they arrive, be it the railway station, bus stand, or airport. If they are being escorted to an ashram, they must be given adequate hospitality and accommodated within the ashram itself until the day of the Yati Pooja. On the day of the Yati Pooja, after preparing the Guru Pooja and all kinds of food items, the Sanyasis should be seated on spread plantain leaves or pristine white cloths. First, a garland should be placed around their necks, and flowers must be offered on their heads. Offering flowers means making a coiled ring-like shape with a flower garland on the head and showering flowers over it. Garlanding and offering flowers must be done by the inmates of the ashram themselves. Along with the Dakshina (offering), betel leaves, flowers, and clothes must be given. The Dakshina should be given starting from one end. At that time, mantras from the Gita, Guru Gita, Upanishads, etc., must be chanted. The Ashram President or Secretary must sit with the Sanyasis. Afterwards, food items should be served. If there is remaining space, the pavilion (pandal) can be filled with people and food can be served.

[GV4:P0600] During the time of Yati Pooja, Guru Pooja will be performed for three days in some ashrams and for five to seven days in other ashrams. Clothes will also be provided to the Yatis on those days.

[GV4:P0601] If the Yati Pooja is conducted in a home, the Sanyasis must be received with as much celebration as possible right at the place where they alight and escorted to the house; their hands and feet should be washed, and all members of the household should welcome them together by offering prostrations. After receiving and seating them, something may first be given to quench their thirst. Subsequently, as mentioned above, clothes, Dakshina, food, and travel expenses to return to their place should be given before sending them off.

[GV4:P0602] Meritorious benefits (Punyamsangal) that accrue to the household conducting the Yati Pooja and to that land:

[GV4:P0603] 1. The ancestors (Pithrukkal) of those conducting the Yati Pooja will watch all this and rejoice. Ancestors are of two or three types. Those ancestors who have departed as Yogis, Karmis, and Jnanis. They are the ones who rejoice more. Even the ancestors who know nothing and have merged into the atmosphere like primitive humans will attain the eligibility to acquire merit (Punya).

[GV4:P0604] 2. The merit obtained is in accordance with the qualification of the guests arriving as Yatis. Yatis start from a certain rank (state). There are Yatis who have reached up to the state of the Trinity (Trimurthi). They are elevated up to a maximum of 5 to 7 states. If the Yatis are those belonging to the timeless Gurus (Kalanthara Gurukkanmar), their ritual will be one that qualifies even for liberation (Mukti). Ten or twenty families among the households belonging to the Guru lineage can also join together to conduct the Yati Pooja.

[GV4:P0605] 3. There are those who believe that building bhajan halls, temples, etc., is a meritorious act. Building ten temples will yield the result of building one Samadhi Mandir. If one performs the Yati Pooja understanding its glory and with the purity of its ritual, one will attain the result of building not just one, but three temples. Along with that, ancestors who stand elevated to the zodiac (Rashi) attainable by the Yatis will reach those positions; some will attain liberation and some will take birth. A progeny will be born from the position reached by the life force of any of these Yatis, bringing goodness to the family, the land, and the country itself. These are things that happen over seven generations. If every child in the household worshipping the Yatis does not understand this concept to its full extent, not only will it be impossible to put this into practice, but their lineage of offspring will also travel on the wrong path, becoming the cause for their own and their family's destruction.

[GV4:P0606] Abundant evidence for this can be seen in Kerala itself. The Brahmins who lived in Kalady, where Sri Sankara was born, not only became alienated, but today they are poor in Kerala and, more specifically, in India. Except for those who adopted the dress and language of the Westerners, who were judged as *mlechchas* (outcasts), and engaged in jobs ranging from clerks to bank managers, a few other high-ranking officials, and judges, all the rest are at a very low level today. If this is the condition of the people in Kerala or India who rejected the ideology of Sri Sankara, it can be seen that the experience is no different if one observes people like Kumbalathu Sankupillai, who was foremost among the householders who are said to have respected and revered Chattampi Swami, and who had earned a name and fame in intellect and practical work. Even if one examines the history of the families who loved Narayana Guru, learned and taught by serving him, and the numerous families who first built huts for the Guru in many places and later expanded them, one can see that there are many histories of them being ruined due to the same experiences and many other mistakes. However, it can be seen that those who went and met him once or ten times a month, received the necessary advice and instructions, and humbly obeyed them, prospered and later grew by trying to adapt to that ideology. Thus, numerous families, even without spiritual realization in that path, are indeed great ones who acquired education, wealth, and lordship. Similarly, the land where Jesus was born and the land where Jesus went, grew, and earned respect can be observed by everyone.

[GV4:P0607] Those participating in the *Yathipooja* should chant the *Gurugeetha* mantras and the *Akhandanama* for ten minutes, followed by the *Anukampadasakam* and *Gurukeerthanam*, and finally conclude by chanting the *Santhipadam*.

[GV4:P0608] The Method to Receive and Usher the *Yathis*

[GV4:P0609] At the very front, frankincense (*kuminchan*) should be smoked and carried. Behind that, the lamp and the ornamental umbrella (*muthukkuda*). Following that, the Sanyasins and devotees should be ushered in that order, along with prayers (in a low voice). A bloomed lotus flower should be given into the hands of each Sanyasin.

[GV4:P0610] Guruvani

[GV4:P0611] Santhigiri Birthday Poojitha Dedication Edition 2002

[GV4:P0612] Imparting of Knowledge in the Form of Guru and Disciple

[GV4:P0613] The word 'experience' has a very vast magnitude of meaning. We have the knowledge of experience ranging from installing *Madan* (a local deity) and calling him Lord. If *Madan* or any other such deities are assigned the position of a god and called Lord, those who do so will never reach the position of God. Moreover, those who intensely perform *poojas* and worship by swaying and shaking like demons might attain certain direct experiences and some special mystic powers capable of bewildering people and leading them into blindness, but their souls will become more degraded than that of an unbeliever who considers saying they have no faith as a matter of prestige. I have been able to see this as the greatest evidence in my belief. There are people with another kind of devotion. They are the group who make vows and offerings, perform frantic dances, buy elephants and offer them to the temple, conduct *kuthirayeduppu* (horse effigy procession), and organize *Padakam*, *Harikatha*, and *Kathaprasangam* (storytelling performances) for wealth and the accomplishment of other matters. Then there is another group of devotees who, out of extreme devotion, get some minor visions which then increase, and when a *Yogeeswaran*, *Manthramoorthi*, or *Bhadrakali* lying dead and suppressed in the family stands strong, they do something or the other until their death to make people believe. The family members then turn him into a favorite deity or a favorite *Yogeeswaran* and make him the family deity. Due to such practices, that family itself will wander and become bankrupt after one or two generations. Moreover, they will be subjected to a great sin.

[GV4:P0614] There is a reason for writing and revealing this. Among the many thousands of such families who come to me, I am only able to eradicate the sinful power of ninety-nine percent. The reason why the sinful power of some remaining cases could not be eradicated is that they suffer from the greatest of major diseases or have gone mad with an incurable manic nature. It is incurable and hereditary in the family.

[GV4:P0615] If we examine it this way, we might wonder if there is anything real. Yes, there is God who transcends the magnitude of what was mentioned earlier. A God who cannot be confined in a temple or within the limits of *nirmalya* rituals. In some families, there are some ancestors (*Pitrus*) like sacrificing great souls who have maintained honesty throughout their lives and managed to reach at least the position of a *Brahmarakshas*. In later times, some children will be born in that family in the zodiac sign where such ancestors reside. Even if that child does not become spiritually realized, they will be mature enough to perform good deeds without caring about the aforementioned artificial practices and liberate those ancestors. If it is a girl, there will be a lot of goodness. If it is a girl, she only needs to be helped in the act of granting liberation. Ancestors who attain liberation in this way can show some visionary paths to a woman or a man and make them a good devotee or a wise person. Otherwise, they will at least make them a fallen yogi or a wealthy person.

[GV4:P0616] The most superior path than all of this is to find a wise Guru. If a Guru is found, one will be able to attain spiritual merit (*Atmasukrutham*) at least to the extent of the fortune of their soul. All these things mentioned might perhaps seem negative to those who are not spiritually realized. Therefore, I desire that the idea for a good path becomes clear to the people. In a state filled with ignorance born out of the lack of love, not just of our land but of the world itself, and some barbaric idiocies of enjoying making money through savagery, even if you do not read such things, you should try to seek a good path that helps to bring firmness in virtue and the fortune acquired through karma.

[GV4:P0617] Disciple: Guru! If you summarize this subject like this, we who are ignorant do not know how to take it. We also do not know how to grasp it through the words of a wise person.

[GV4:P0618] Guru: The antiquity of the soul itself is necessary to grasp this subject through the words of a wise person.

[GV4:P0619] Disciple: I have felt in many ways and situations that the antiquity of the soul is necessary. Still, we have an intense desire to know. Therefore, we wish to know it in detail.

[GV4:P0620] Guru: Everything said earlier was about the antiquity of the soul itself. If doubt arises even now, what is to be done? Now, let me speak about what is meant by the antiquity of the soul.

[GV4:P0621] Biology itself represents the evolutionary principle, consolidated and manifested completely in the macrocosm and atomically in the microcosm. The Hindu doctrine holds this as the eternal principle. This is the very foundation of the Puranas and epics. However, whether experienced or not, some scholars harbor doubts regarding certain illogical aspects of this doctrine. Therefore, they claim that what the sage Badarayana has written, what the four Vedas, the six Shastras, and the eighteen Puranas have unequivocally praised, and furthermore, the merit of the scholars' own research studies, are authoritative. They also employ a highly logical language for this purpose. Such scholars, who think solely through their own logic, will fail to recognize the truth in biology. At that point, they seek refuge in *Mayavada* (the doctrine of illusion). Yet, when *Mayavada* is subjected to logic, it essentially states that there is only one, not two (non-duality). Subsequently, clinging firmly to the truth that there is only one and not two, they introduce dialectics (*Tarkashastra*). Their peculiar logic is such that they can study and teach such dialectics for any length of time. Using ordinary Puranas and logical words, they illustrate this with the inference of mistaking a rope for a snake. If the one who gives this illustration sees a snake (let us assume it is a King Cobra) right in front of him, even if he dares to chase it away with courage and arrogance without fear, the snake will inevitably turn and bite if driven into a corner. The truth is that one cannot escape that snakebite without medicine, imagination, or knowledge. If he firmly clings to *Mayavada* with the force of his erudition and logic, will he remain unaffected by the venom? If there were a snake instead of a rope, and if one adopts some method to step aside without getting bitten or to destroy it, doesn't *Mayavada* become a hollow concept? The one who has studied dialectics, the scholar, and the ignoramus are all equal in this regard. However, a Sannyasin possesses certain esoteric techniques by which venom does not affect the body, regardless of which venomous snakes bite, let alone a King Cobra.

[GV4:P0622] Question: What is it that you refer to as a technique (Vidya)? Doesn't the Sannyasin possess true wisdom (Jnana)?

[GV4:P0623] Guru: What the Sannyasin possesses is indeed true wisdom (Jnana). That wisdom does not have a method of destroying or otherwise eliminating what is ordained by divine will. The wise one (Jnani) anticipates such matters in advance and adopts a path to escape from that event.

[GV4:P0624] Question: There is history of massive snakes serving as an umbrella for Sannyasins, as well as history of them being companions to certain Sannyasins, is there not?

[GV4:P0625] Guru: There is some truth to that as well. The reason for this is that most Sannyasins adopt disciplines belonging to the path of propitiation (*Upasana*). For instance, they are those who have attained occult powers (*Siddhis*) through actions—in thought, word, and deed—along the *Upasana* paths of Shaivism, Shaktism, and Vaishnavism, thereby acquiring the eightfold sovereign powers (*Ashtaishwarya Siddhi*) as a manifestly attainable state. Others do not do this; they adopt the path of *Kalpaseva*. This is a discipline that involves the consumption of substances, starting from various leaves up to the seeds of the Strychnine tree (*Kanjiram*). Furthermore, there is another discipline that involves the consumption of the nine poisons (*Navapashana*) prepared in various ways. During the period of such consumption, they reside inside a specially constructed cave with nine entrances. While consuming the medicine, this individual will be unable to stand or walk. Even the excretion of feces and urine will cease. There is a specific calculation that one must face a particular entrance during a particular watch (*Yama*). The accompanying disciples shift their position to face the respective entrances. The disciples would have been taught beforehand about the care to be administered during that time. By the time they attain the eight *Siddhis*, their body will return to its former state. Once this regulated regimen is applied to the body, it will no longer be afflicted by old age and graying hair. There is also a principle that even death will occur only when they desire it. Serpents can recognize those who have attained two or four of the eight *Siddhis*. Serpents possessing such recognition will immediately turn back upon seeing them without staying. Or, even if bitten by snakes belonging to an ignorant, wicked path, the venom will rebound upon the snake, merely resulting in the snake's death. All of this is not achieved in a single lifetime, but rather through paths adopted across multiple lifetimes in accordance with inherent tendencies (*Vasanas*). Upon attaining *Siddhis* in this manner, they exhibit various miraculous feats. Such *Siddhas* are often mistakenly perceived as truly wise (*Jnanis*).

[GV4:P0626] Haven't you heard people asking whether a certain person is a *Siddha*? There are behavioral tendencies wherein people take pleasure in recounting various tales and anecdotes about Sannyasins who attain *Siddhis* in this manner. Such stories are particularly heard in southern Travancore. One such story goes like this:

[GV4:P0627] In a certain place, there were two brothers. One was educated and a scholar. The other was uneducated and a fool. Both took turns guarding the banana plantation. One day, the uneducated one went to guard. Hearing hymns being chanted here and there, the elder brother approached and asked the younger brother how he had learned this. He replied that someone gave him two bananas, and the hymns dawned upon him when he ate them. The elder brother, who picked up and ate the banana peels from the base of the banana plant, also became a poet. There are people who believe even this. One has heard claims of seeing a Swami observed at one location simultaneously at another location. These are all illusions manifested through the application of *Gaunamani*, *Sthambhanamani*, and *Rasamani*. These are anomalies that occur in action when all of this is misinterpreted as true wisdom (*Jnana*). These are the paths we adopt.

[GV4:P0628] Haven't you seen some people playing with snakes draped around their necks? If he has not extracted the fangs or kept medicine in hand, he has indeed plunged into a fatal error. There was an instance in Koorkanchery, Thrissur, where a person known as Pampu Swami used to walk around with a snake around his neck. None of this should be mistaken for true wisdom (*Jnana*). A true *Jnani* will not exhibit specialized *Siddhis*. Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa has stated that *Siddhis* should be discarded like dog excrement.

[GV4:P0629] Thus, through the prolonged habit of being born and dying over many eras, that soul's inherent tendency (*Vasana*) becomes exactly that. Consequently, whatever course of action and course of duty was practiced by the soul residing within the body composed of the five elements, that soul can only return, fall back into it, and become the possessor of a life that exhibits various distortions. None of this constitutes true wisdom (*Jnana*).

[GV4:P0630] Question: Then, are you also advocating the theory of evolution?

[GV4:P0631] Guru: Yes, this is indeed evolution. We must remember that if the convergence of the lights of the earth, the sun, and the moon does not occur, not only animals, reptiles, termites, and other living beings, but also the marvels of creation—ranging from the aforementioned *Navapashana* to medicinal paths that cannot be categorized by name or number—would be unable to exist or survive in their respective forms and efficacies. Even electricity, which claims to stand at the zenith of growth and progress, is significantly affected by the changes in nature. Therefore, the only desire here is that one should not become the master of actions that seek to intimidate humanity by further chasing after such *Siddhis*, esoteric techniques, and theories of action like *Mayavada*.

[GV4:P0632] Question: Having said all this, how will the people learn about our path and the duties that must be performed, or will they not learn?

[GV4:P0633] Guru: People with faith, that is, those who believe and pray with faith in a lineage of Gurus (*Guru Parampara*), do indeed attain fruition, do they not?

[GV4:P0634] Question: Fruition is attained by those who believe in other paths as well. Then why single out and specify our path in particular?

[GV4:P0635] Guru: Our path has not emerged from reading about or following the footsteps of any categorized path such as Yoga, Bhakti, Karma, or Jnana. This is my own direct experience. I have clearly realized through experience that everything mentioned by name truly exists and that nothing is non-existent.

[GV4:P0636] Question: But it is said that others have also realized it through experience, is it not?

[GV4:P0637] Guru: What we call our experience has been shown in the philosophical aspect regarding the greatness of the Manvantaras, the great souls, the origin of the Trimurti system, and its efficacy in the Treta Yuga and Dvapara Yuga. The Treta Yuga and Dvapara Yuga are periods when one could reach as far as possible by worshiping, praying, and practicing Yoga in the Deva system. However, in Kali Yuga, not only is that system ineffective, but those who follow that system will not attain liberation in Kali Yuga either. That is why it is said that they have reached and stand in that path. The path advised by Shiva to Parvati in the Skanda Purana confirms this experiential truth - the Guru Gita.

[GV4:P0638] In this Gita, Parvati asks Shiva, even though you exist as the life of all living beings and are the greatest ascetic and the most supreme among the Trimurtis, whom are you meditating upon? The subject matter discussed in the Guru Gita is Shiva's response to this question from Parvati in the form of advice. The Guru Gita discusses the subjects that even the Trimurtis do not have liberation, how the karma and knowledge of that Supreme Being are attained, how the disciple understands it, and how it helps in liberation.

[GV4:P0639] All human souls have been caught up in the karmas of the Trimurti system or the Manu lineage for a long time. It has been proven beyond doubt that no matter which karma one is involved in, one's karma will not go to anything else beyond what one does. It is believed that this belongs to the original path of Manu.

[GV4:P0640] The human souls have been believing in any one of these paths like the path of Devas, path of Acharyas, or path of Prophets till today. We have been shown all these paths, and the karmas that have come according to the order of gross, subtle, and causal in everything, the balance of good and evil existing in each, the deviations that caused the errors, and the corrections for them. Having experienced the meaning of what has been called chanting of names from time to time, and taking the matter which is its gross, subtle, and causal, Deva, Acharya, Prophet, Sage, Ascetic ٹ. Thus, whatever exists in the form of noun, and its karma, and the karmas that are gross, subtle, and causal which connect those karmas, our path is to correct the disciple in the field of experience and action.

[GV4:P0641] There are few paths that correct as far as the gross, subtle, causal, and effect. That is our path. Our path is the Guru's path which corrects without error the method by which the gurus and wise men who have come so far correct our mistakes from their compassionate greatness. Here, some may see and hear certain things in the states of waking (Jagrat), dream (Svapna), and deep sleep (Sushupti). The Guru-disciple relationship here, or the greatness known as the Guru's compassion, is to elevate the disciple to the heights of a wise man by distinguishing and convincing them of what it is when the waking-deep sleep occurs in the two states of Turiya and Turiyatita.

[GV4:P0642] Kali Yuga is the time when liberation is equally ordained for the Shudra, who does not grasp the meaning of the distinction of true Varnashrama Dharma but is entitled to complete self-knowledge in Kali Yuga, the Brahmin, the Kshatriya, and the Vaishya, who always wishes to be a merchant and a wealthy worker. That is why even the sages prayed, "O Lord, give me birth and let me see the Kali Yuga once." And the birth should be in India itself. India is the fertile land of knowledge of all types of sage lineages. The path of knowledge mentioned in texts like the Guru Gita should be acquired by man through karma.

[GV4:P0643] This Guru's greatness has come as evidence revealed through the words of the perceptive sages that man can reach much higher levels from the knowledge that has come so far. That is why our path is delivered in the form of Guru-disciple dialogue through knowledge by thought, word, and deed without any web of magical powers. I pray to that treasure of compassion who has shown and told this lineage as a way to untie the knots of karma and dharma that have been entangled in life for lifetimes through the acquired karmas that are the gross, subtle, causal, and effects of the entire human lineage, not just this lineage, and to guide them to liberation, and to complete the dharma of the next yuga by coming in this yuga, so that it may be bestowed upon the human world to put an end to births and deaths forever.

[GV4:P0644] Guru Vani

[GV4:P0645] Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Samarppanappathippu 2002

[GV4:P0646] The Divine Will Vested in Santhigiri

[GV4:P0647] In the world, the influence of human history is upon Asia, and especially upon India. It is India that gives the complete account of the four Yugas and the Manvantaras. It still exists today in a way that cannot go wrong.

[GV4:P0648] The duration of the *Yuga* system is determined by five visionary Gurus. There is a transitional period (*Sandhikal*) between the end of one *Yuga* and the beginning of the next. This transitional period acts as both an end and a beginning. It is impossible to determine the exact duration of this transitional phase when entering one *Yuga* from another. However, the *Manusmriti* states: the duration of the transitional period between the *Krita Yuga* and the beginning of the *Treta Yuga* is equal to the length of the *Krita Yuga* itself. Similarly, the durations of other *Yuga* transitions have also been specified. A *Chaturyuga*, comprising all four *Yugas*, is said to last for twelve thousand divine years. This calculation originates from the lineage of Manu. Yet, this calculation does not account for the transitional periods. The transitional period is of special significance as it is an era when countless great souls manifest and act. In a single *Yuga*, there are visionary Gurus whose foresight spans from five hundred to five thousand or even ten thousand years. When considering the total calculation of a lineage, it extends to ten thousand years and beyond; certain religious doctrines, establishing rules both old and new, even span from twenty thousand to two hundred thousand years.

[GV4:P0649] According to the Hindu calculation of the fourteen *Manvantaras*, the combined duration of these fourteen *Manvantaras* is depicted as a single day of Brahma. Once that day concludes, the deluge (*Pralaya*) follows. The duration of the deluge is also equal to fourteen *Manvantaras*. However, it is also stated that somewhere in between, an obstacle arose and the action of the four-faced entity (*Nanmukhan*) went awry. In the works of certain artists who navigated through the Puranas, the concept of the four-faced entity was altered and instead depicted as the faces of Brahma. Through an alternative narrative route, various limbs of Brahma were similarly portrayed. The fictional tale of Brahma thus emerged to complete the *Trimurti* system. Lord Subrahmanya, who represents the path of wisdom, is known by the name *Arumukhan* (the six-faced one). When *Arumukhan* engaged in conversation with the faces of Brahma, the Brahma-conceived tale of the four-faced entity completely dissolved! When imagination and poetic fancies intertwined, leading to errors in the *Yuga Dharma* and the *Trimurti* system, the face of wisdom (*Jñānamukham*) ceased to speak. In the history of the four-faced entity, which became entangled in poetic imagination or Puranic lapses, it was depicted that Subrahmanya, in a fit of anger, pinched off the fourth face, the face of wisdom. Subsequently, when the depiction was restricted to the *Trimurtis*, the face of wisdom vanished entirely. The conceptual deities of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva were thus established by depicting them over these fundamental errors.

[GV4:P0650] Proceeding along that path, the concept of the *Saptarshis* and the history of the lineage of Manu were lost. Returning to the present, wherever the Vedas were codified into four, the Shastras into six, and the Puranas into eighteen, they established the boundaries of rivers and artificially created oceans of knowledge. Even one who merely marked the boundaries of a lake or a stream attempted to articulate it with the profundity of oceanic wisdom. Thus, scholars sitting in royal assemblies crafted narratives favored by scholarly councils, thereby creating an ocean of wisdom. They brought it to completion by adding sounds, vowels, and consonants to impart meaning. When every meaning was formalized according to the scholar's rhetoric, an ocean-like knowledge seemed to emerge. This is essentially the poetic stage of historical scholars.

[GV4:P0651] But this alone is insufficient for us. When human dharma, which ought to have provided light and righteousness to the eras, faltered, historians attempted to gloss over it by attributing it to the Stone Age and the like. All these efforts turned out to be like trying to straighten a tangled thread that had been thrown into the sea and had begun to rot and unravel.

[GV4:P0652] Be that as it may, can we utilize the opportunity we have been given? If so, how? The given time refers to the era of the incarnation of great souls. That is, as mentioned earlier, from the great visionaries who foresaw five hundred years ahead, to Moses who came after Sri Krishna and his accompanying lineage, and subsequently the Buddha who appeared in India (Gautama Buddha, among the numerous Buddhas mentioned) - all offer specific calculations. Furthermore, the principles of *Siddhi* that emerged during certain intervals, and the various systems transmitted through them such as *Yoga Nyaya*—*Karma Yoga*, *Hatha Yoga*, *Chandrika Yoga*, and *Hamsa Yoga*—also created distortions, performing deeds that generated various miracles. When Dr. Somervell traveled through the outskirts of the Himalayas, he happened to see a person sitting like a skeleton. Upon approaching, this figure asked: "Is Henry IV currently ruling England?" Thus, through practices like *Kayakalpha* therapies, surviving for centuries and fulfilling actions described as miraculous penance exist here. The ascetic action that dictates the qualifications of an ascetic has been reduced to mere completion of rituals. This is not true penance; it is a form of yogic *Siddhi*.

[GV4:P0653] Will human consciousness towards wisdom be awakened by recounting such miracles? Alternatively, if one fulfills the aphoristic points of Patanjali's Yoga and completes the ritualistic aspects of Yogic science, will it serve human dharma? The story of Ramanuja's disciple, Kabir Das, speaks of a Gorakshan (Gorakh) possessing miraculous powers. However, not only was he unable to defeat Kabir Das, but history also records that he eventually vanished. Then, what is the actual benefit of such miracles?

[GV4:P0654] Now, let me narrate what was imparted at Santhigiri. It has been experienced as a truth that whatever must occur according to the divine will (*Brahmanishchaya*) exists in the *Trimurti* system exactly as it should. But upon deeper elaboration, dharma only persists where these three faces are mentioned. The face of wisdom is conspicuously absent there. There is no way to describe the course of events that unfold when visionaries arrive in those realms. We must understand one thing. Studying Sri Krishna, the architect of the Gita, will clarify a few aspects. History proves that Sri Krishna was deliberately brought forth by divine will. The sorrow Sri Krishna endured during his final days is beyond description. Subsequently, numerous great souls arrived bearing various doctrines. They all met the same fate that befell Krishna. This was the exact experience of Moses who followed Krishna, of the Buddha in India, and of countless other great souls who came, with or without the confines of caste and religion.

[GV4:P0655] If we consider around twenty-five historical figures, the Prophet is one such great soul. The Prophet, who arrived through the very same path as Jesus, encountered the exact same destiny. What can anyone say bypassing this truth? The Prophet did not speak for any specific caste or religion. He spoke for the entirety of mankind. It was the Prophet, attaining Samadhi in the seventh state, who proclaimed: "Oh Lord, what is this that you have done to me, who believed that there is nothing but You, and that God and Truth are one? It is the *Jinn*s who rule the world." Did he speak a lie, or did he state this for the sake of the world? Other than worshipping these *Jinn*s, what else have we been able to accomplish to this day? Each religion, in its own language, worships a god, a goddess, a yogi, a rishi, an ascetic, or a sage; however, in reality, what we worship are the *Jinn*s. Even after that, we have seen so many great souls who have remained unacknowledged to this day. Radha Swami is one among them. However, there is no Guru-disciple relationship in that system.

[GV4:P0656] What is the Guru-disciple relationship?

[GV4:P0657] The guru-disciple relationship corrects the changes in states in various ways by elevating the states of waking (jagrat), dreaming (swapna), and vision (darshana) to the transcendent state of turiya. For one state, there are seven thousand four hundred and forty-four visions. He who completes the seven states in this manner is the one who has fully realized the presence of God. Then comes the realization of God, the realization of Brahman, and the realization of the Supreme Brahman. It is because there exists a particular state about which nothing can be explained that the sorrow of these great souls cannot be resolved. First, they must be liberated. After that, their lineage must be liberated. However, only a Guru who comes with the permission of Brahman to liberate them can recognize whether the aforementioned ethereal voice is true or not, without utilizing sleight of hand, mystical powers, or acquired knowledge. Those who dismiss both knowledge and ignorance, who speak of duality and non-duality and then settle into a comfortable state, do not realize this. Only a soul that is born having inherently completed the eighth state, having taken crores of births and thirsted solely for wisdom, can actualize the word of Brahman.

[GV4:P0658] Another thing to be done for this is to show in a vision who all these aforementioned great souls were and how they came, and thereby realize who stands where in the changed states of those times. It is our destined duty to discover the self-sacrifice each of such great souls has made for our sake, and to knock and open those doors. Duty is not a buffoonery of arguing and winning by debating whether something exists or not.

[GV4:P0659] Vision (darshana) is the harmonious uniting of the ascetic and the wise one who have led the soul to a virtuous path, showing and correcting the mistakes and good deeds that have occurred. The transition of states (avasthantara) is the categorization of the stream of light by seven, seven thousand, and seven thousand four hundred and forty-four, upon reaching the state where the soul makes an offering of the soul.

[GV4:P0660] Believing without a doubt that we all are indebted to the divine decree that proved this to be true, one should pronounce as Guru the one who reaches the soul-vision of 'Jagrat swapna sushuptinam sakshipoorthi namonamah' (Salutations to the complete witness of the waking, dreaming, and deep sleep states) and makes corrections. This should not be fulfilled merely through the words of an eminent scholar. This is the measure of the stream of light completed through self-realization. For this, the language of the Vedic scholar is as follows:

[GV4:P0661] The inner light, the outer light,

[GV4:P0662] The inward light, the Supreme Beyond,

[GV4:P0663] The light of lights, the self-effulgent light,

[GV4:P0664] The light of the self, I am Shiva.

[GV4:P0665] This is the Tantric aspect. However, none of this is our sorrow. Let us begin to study at least from the time of Sri Krishna. Honoring the words of the great souls who had the wisdom to humbly prostrate and express their sorrow to that great power that sent them to act upon this, before finally leaving their bodies after working within the systems of Hindu knowledge that have existed from then until today, we must highlight the Dharma of Kali (Kalidharma) that has passed until yesterday and which exists today.

[GV4:P0666] What is written down stating that Kali is acceptable and not acceptable? It would be a pitiful sight to see scholars, who logically assign meanings even to vowels and consonants, rotting and falling here. The cycle of time to recognize this Dharma of Kali, imparted by that divine decree so as to be passed on to at least the coming generations, has caught up with us. That is, by presenting to our grandchildren or the future generation the truth that has shown us, along with cause and effect, the Dharma that came, or has come, or is yet to come to implement the divinely ordained action denoted by the four epochs, complete the duty of a householder.

[GV4:P0667] If one can present the sacrifice, love, and respect of the wise and the learned, each person becomes a special manifestation of Dharma that reveals the truth. The wheel of time is returning to us the brilliant sacrifices of the selfless, so that seekers of all kinds of knowledge can study and verify each truth through experience. The intention here is to give our little ones the opportunity to open and examine that brilliantly colorful sacrifice that has passed, is present, and is yet to come. Kali is the unique cycle of time that the divine decree has opened up for us for this purpose. This Kali is a special Dharma that can be experienced by the people of the world and all living beings.

[GV4:P0668] I am informing you repeatedly—of all epochs, Kali is the good one. Our life's goal should be to fulfill the path of Dharma, defined as gross, subtle, causal, and effect, by transcribing into the atom and the infinite the brilliant sacrifice of the great prophets who shared a noble life or passed away sacrificing their lives grappling with body and soul, and of the eminent sages who shared their lives for us.

[GV4:P0669] Let us share forever the pain of revealing the truth through the epoch and the life of Dharma, and the pure blessedness that has been fully experienced. The divine purpose is to show us the revered life of the Guru and disciple, which is our nectar of pure consciousness and is of an absorptive nature. This is the path of salvation of Santhigiri, ordained by the Divine. This is the truth of truths, the source of blessedness, and pure, brilliant genius!

[GV4:P0670] Guruvani

GURUVANIKAL · October 2002 · Volume 4
Malayalam source paragraphs GV4:P0671 to GV4:P0691

[GV4:P0671] October 2002

[GV4:P0672] In what all ways have our ancestors provided guidance for our sake, or for the sake of this worldly knowledge, or in the financial and knowledge-related fields of the world! They have shown us by finding and applying every matter suitable for guidance. One of the most important among them is Ayurveda. It is the Veda that holds the secret of life.

[GV4:P0673] According to the topography of our land, harsh administration of medicines should not be done. Ingredients like mercury, sulphur, and arsenic should not be applied as they are. However, they can be processed, brought to the practice called Gurukalpa, and used in the Gurukalpa Seva system. But the Western method of application is not like that. Today, there is a speed there akin to boiling rice in five minutes. The medicines given to us are those prepared using ashes (bhasmas) and various other such materials. They quickly affect the body. This will harm the body.

[GV4:P0674] There are reasons why the way Westerners produce and apply medicine is different from ours. One is the difference in topography. Another is the lack of availability of medicinal plants. It is difficult to get plant varieties there. But we do not have that difficulty. Any kind of plant that grows in our forests is medicinal. However, there are also difficulties in utilizing these medicinal plants. Our ancestors have also shown us the ways to overcome those difficulties. The same systems that have existed since very ancient times are still in existence today. But today, that is not enough. Why?

[GV4:P0675] Let us assume that someone manifested a god, someone manifested a goddess—or rather, that they even manifested and fulfilled the great sage Dhanvantari himself, who is considered the most complete figure in medical science. They might have prescribed two or four medicines to this worshipper. Taking the medicine obtained in this way, considering it together with his ascetic power and the theory he has been following, he will apply it to some people. And the disease will be cured. Does that mean we should assume that the diseases of the entire world are cured?

[GV4:P0676] The disease will be cured. All those are truthful aspects. But this is not enough. What we need is a precept to act by seeing and knowing in the action that is changing momentarily. Kali is the best epoch suited to create such a thing. This is God-given. If we continue to burn and distill as was done in past times, the Dharma of this Kali will not be fulfilled. Everything that exists is true. But for which time is this to be applied? We must think about this time. That is Kali. Kali is the time we have been given to be born.

[GV4:P0677] It is said that even some gods have wished to be born as at least a blade of grass in Kali. Why? That desire is because if they were born as at least a blade of grass in this Bharata, they could fulfill this karma in the growth and glory of this nature. But we have suffered some kind of loss to the extent that we are unable to be born and grow in that Bharata and honor the Dharma that has imparted vigilance and truth.

[GV4:P0678] During the time of Sree Rama, Bharadwaja brought forth the science of aeronautics (Vimana Shastra). His Guru had told Bharadwaja that such a science was not needed for that era. If the flying machine (Vimana) was built, it would lead to everyone's destruction. But Bharadwaja did not obey. He went to Kubera's kingdom and had the king there build it. The war occurred because that flying machine was used to come here and abduct Sita. We all presume this to be a war between Rama and Ravana. But it was entirely a struggle between a Guru and his disciple. Consequently, the kingdom itself was destroyed. The calamities resulting from not doing what is necessary at the appropriate time have still not left us today. After that, we have never been able to regain the sanctity of that Guru-disciple relationship.

[GV4:P0679] Let someone else make the goods. We will get them too. But that is not equal to the Dharma (duty/nature) of our life (Jeeva). Our birth is meant for thinking and making others think about the Dharma of life. Our soul is confined within an instinctual origin (Vasanas), having seen, heard, known, and acted upon good and bad across many births. We must absolutely possess a state of mind capable of contemplating what system is required to understand that soul.

[GV4:P0680] If a scholar sees a poor man doing something, he will only treat it with contempt. The scholar has the attitude that he knows everything. But what is this poor man doing? He takes a fallen man onto his lap, nurses him, and speaks to him about good and bad. But the scholar does not know how to do this. He [the poor man] does not have the scholar's attire or education. Without these two, what else can be done!

[GV4:P0681] What is this nursing? It is a task that depletes one's merit (Punya). At the same time, the other person's merit increases. There is a Karma (action) that can reclaim this lost merit. What is that dedicated work? You will not attain it by simply setting out somewhere. For that, one goes and knocks on the doors of a deity whose eyes remain closed, crying, "Oh Lord, didn't you see, haven't I been calling and doing all this for so long?" But the Lord will open His eyes. There is a way for that. That path can only be known while your soul is still residing within its cage (the body).

[GV4:P0682] If we have an educated scholar, an officer, and a doctor who knows the body by dissecting it—thus various kinds of people—in our house, the children of that house will walk around with quite a bit of arrogance. Does carrying this arrogance mean that they know about their home, their land, and their country just because they have all this? By instilling this arrogance, this ego, into these children, they have become spoiled to the extent that they cannot distinguish between wealth, capability, and the actions through which these are applied. This is our situation today. By composing, fabricating, or studying Puranas, how much knowledge can we really gain to change this situation?

[GV4:P0683] There lies a Karma here, taken up through immense effort over a long period, grown logically, discovered, honored with love, humbled, struggled, and sacrificed for. We have not seen the doctrine of this Karma. We have not acquired that knowledge. Without knowing whether that knowledge exists or not, what else are we doing other than amusing ourselves by arguing back and forth that it exists or it does not? What exists is not going to vanish, and what does not exist is not going to materialize. This is a matter from my own experience.

[GV4:P0684] Now, regarding ghosts (Pishacha). If asked whether ghosts exist, the answer is yes. If anyone says they don't, I ask them, then why do people perform sorcery, tantric rituals, mantra worship, and death rituals invoking ghosts? Can those who perform these actions abandon the ghost? It is easy to say it does not exist, and it is easy to say it does. It was the former Acharyas who stated that everything from ghosts to the realm of vampires (Vethala Nagaram) is agony. They spoke after seeing it. It is only when one reaches the realm of vampires that one understands the special nature of the sorrow there. Beyond that, when one reaches the actions of Shaktheyam, Shaivam, and Vaishnavam, one will see the positions where gods, goddesses, sages, and ascetics stand. Even if seen, to bring it into one's experience, there must be a Guru to instruct, saying, "Do only this in this specific way," or "Manifest it thus"—"Do not do that, do this instead"; he imparts it by making it part of your experience and your fortune.

[GV4:P0685] In the truth of life that comes according to our Karma and Dharma, everyone is equal. There is no other justification in this. However, if there are five children in a family, all five will have slight differences in their course of Karma. They are all indeed the children of the same father and mother. But one will not be like the other. One might have more compassion for the poor. One might want to marry from a poor family. People end up poor due to the lack of merit (Punya) in their soul. Not everyone can take that upon themselves. It will only increase the pain of the soul.

[GV4:P0686] When we say 'Sadhukkal' (the gentle/poor), it should not be understood as the poor. It means 'Sathukkal' (the virtuous). Do not try to remove these flaws using your logic and intellect. What you need is a life that examines the flaws of the soul and transforms them. There is no point in showing off other justifications and arrogance. Whatever weight (arrogance) we have is ours alone. No one can steal it. Similarly, our good and bad are right in our own hands. Our children are the ones who transform it by suffering little by little, imbibing Dharma through the experience of that pain, and realizing merit. There is no point in preaching Vedanta for this. There is also no point in trying to correct children by scolding them. Without knowing the purpose for which you are getting married, what will the children born from such a marriage become? What is the Karma that correctly sustains the affairs of a household? How should our virtues be situated in that Karma, and how should this virtuous Karma be given to the land and the home? Without contemplating any of this, have we been able to show our children any action that provides satisfaction, other than bragging and recounting the magnitude of education, the magnitude of properties and possessions, and the magnitude of prosperity? This is our shortcoming.

[GV4:P0687] You do not need to teach children Vedanta. It is enough to see children as children. If you find children with natural aptitudes (Vasanas), you should guide them along that path. There is no point in applying aptitude in unwanted ways; it must be applied in the right direction. This approach is needed for every one of our homes. You should not distance yourselves from believing, loving, knowing, and letting others know about this. This should be the goal of each one of you. The goal of an ascetic, a wise person, a worker, and a devotee. The path of Santhigiri is the one that unites all these paths. It is a path capable of discovering what the union of life (Jeeva) and the soul (Atma) is. This path will absolutely help you to move forward by understanding what the agony of the vampire realm (Vethala Nagaram) is.

[GV4:P0688] In our habit of thinking categorized into Shaivism, Shaktism, and Vaishnavism, or in the realms of gods, goddesses, sages, ascetics, the wise, and devotees who have fulfilled the course of karma brought about by their compassionate nature, where should we position our ancestors? This must be our goal. If you cannot achieve this, at least your children must be able to. You have the absolute authority to reflect upon who you are within that karma. You should not go seeking anyone's blessings (*anugraha*) or wrath (*nigraha*). People come to me here as well, asking for blessings. The knowledge of these poor souls is an ignorance that does not comprehend what this blessing or curse truly means. It is not blessings or wrath that you should seek. Then what should you seek? The affliction in your life—in that course of karma experienced by the body and mind, what is the *vasana* (inherent tendency) of the karmic course residing deep within the mind, and how shall we eradicate this *vasana*? That *vasana* remains rooted in dharma. As long as the *vasana* remains active, you will unknowingly usurp various things. Everyone usurps in different ways; that is all. Some like their father, some like their mother, some like their elder sister, some like their elder brother—this liking itself is a form of usurpation. What is the point of criticizing our neighbours while holding on to this theft ourselves? "That girl ruined my son; otherwise, my son would have been well-behaved." What a falsehood is being uttered here? What justice will the future generations learn from the absolute form of this injustice that is practiced by speaking in such a manner?

[GV4:P0689] No one ruins anyone else. That origin, which is replete with *vasana*, has manifested on its own. We lack the karmic consciousness to instill good *vasanas* in them from childhood in order to transform that innate nature. Instead, we have reached a stage of action where we curse ourselves, claiming that we are inherently bad. What is the use of such people like us finding fault with those around us?

[GV4:P0690] It might be true that the girl or boy in the neighboring house has flaws. What should we do about that? Should we wish that they somehow perish in those flaws? That is a course of karma acquired from birth. We should attempt to transform that karmic course in a way known to us. What is the action that helps shift them from that mindset and bring them into another mindset? They can be transformed through that action. I received a reward for bringing about such a transformation. I shall tell you about it.

[GV4:P0691] Guruvani

GURUVANIKAL · November 2002 · Volume 4
Malayalam source paragraphs GV4:P0692 to GV4:P0715
