Based on this present state, which has been imprinted over many periods, and the karma that is going to unfold in relation to the past and the future, where do we stand? We should only think about how we must handle this henceforth. In this regard, God has given us sufficient evidence to understand it concisely and to gain immense knowledge from that brevity.

[GV4:P1013] That is to say, our ancestors have been performing certain acts for ages; they did so with good intentions, but we suffer from the misfortune of not being able to distinguish whether it is good or bad. This is because we, as well as our ancestors, have been unable to investigate and discover where we stand today, having unconsciously deviated by doing many things in the name of worship, driven by the catastrophe of worship that has been practiced and propagated until now. With this sorrowful realization, will we receive an ordained karma regarding how to accomplish this or not? If we do, we cannot look back at the myriad ages of past errors that we must traditionally preserve and correct. Then what is needed? Even among those who know something—such as palmistry or the various aspects associated with our horoscopes—there are countless people who remain ignorant of this. What is known is little, and when we look at what is known, we are standing at ground zero. Why?

[GV4:P1014] Our ancestors have departed and are wandering in the karma of worship we have been practicing. It is not just us; when we say our ancestors, it is not enough to mention two or four generations. Having seen a great light of countless bygone eras, and witnessing what destructions have been sown as seeds within this light, how will we uproot and remove them? That is our concern. It is not enough for us or our country; we are entirely heading towards a karma that strengthens evil thoughts, having grown and spread to all parts of the world, standing firmly and powerfully poised for this battle. Seeing this, do we or our children have the time for anything other than challenging it or taking a form of retaliation against it?

[GV4:P1015] We do not have time to look after our own affairs. Therefore, we must move away from this karmic dosha where cause and effect have become entangled. There is only one way for us to do this. As mentioned earlier, if we proceed by discussing Yoga, Karma, Jnana, and Bhakti, our lifespan is insufficient even to reach that stage. Or else, what can be achieved through our lives? It is not that either, then what is it? Our children must step into the karma of untying the imprint that nature stamps upon them—an imprint that has remained fixed for ages, coming to them as a result of the karma we undertake throughout our lifetimes and its consequences. Instead of questioning how to untie it or whether to untie it, you should not become exhausted by overthinking it.

[GV4:P1016] Why? This is not something that can be resolved by mere thought. As long as we remain in complete ignorance regarding all this, we cannot comprehend it through thinking. But we can do one thing. Give priority to our children, proceeding with the determination, love, and respect that at least our children should be able to perfectly fulfill what God has ordained for each of us. Giving that priority means acknowledging that God has given us the knowledge to alter the karma performed by our ancestors. You are more or less aware of this. If any of our children reaches this state—existing within this interplanetary realm—think of the sphere of influence of countless planets under which our Earth, Moon, or Sun operates together in a karmic process! Only if we have conviction in this karma can we realize the harmful thoughts we have harbored because of it and understand that we must change from it. Unless we prepare a background of good knowledge regarding what this change is—a process that involves feeling pain and causing pain—we need capable children who can take on whatever comes to us or to this era, be it destruction or good, bad or evil. We cannot fully take it on ourselves. Nor can we completely reject it; we have acquired an incapacity that renders us unable to do anything.

[GV4:P1019] This was not given by God for our desires. We must strive to embrace a dharma where we have been made instruments to execute the divine will. For this dharma, you, your children, or our contemporaries alone are not enough. We need the application of progeny endowed with the intellect to remove the errors that have occurred over aeons. We have also been shown how to do this. There is no need to waste time idly talking just because it has been revealed to us. Let us always remain vigilant. That vigilance must become a truth preserved for the sake of our lineage. So, what shall we do with this truth? How shall we receive it? How should it be transmitted to this land and country through us? Should we revert to the karma of calling upon God while divided by caste, religion, and race? Or should we realize that this is a reality ordained by God for all of us? Rather than wasting time overthinking how we can reach the karma that we analyze, we should proceed by applying only the knowledge we have been given.

[GV4:P1020] What is it? If we are to move away from the karma that we usually refer to as that of yogis and karmis—or even the ones where astrologers satisfy us with offerings by telling the tales of deities—we have been granted a karma by God where we are immediately told what our ruin is, what caused our ignorance, and where we stand in this ignorance. However, because we do not realize that we are receiving such a great fortune, if we stand aside with our very petty minds and fight, where will we reach? We will not be able to achieve anything.

[GV4:P1021] Therefore, it is not just about our life; we should not be absorbing the heat of the departed souls from wherever they exist. We are the ones who must think about the temperature of those souls. Nothing can be done about it. Thus, it is the mistake that has occurred in the light of numerous eras passed across Manvantaras, whether through the prophetic paths, the system of goddesses and gods, or the system of the Trinity, which came about within and outside these modes of worship. This is being revealed to us. This is our greatness. What is being revealed? We have arrived at a very magnificent karma that gave us the opportunity to be born in a time ordained by God for this revelation, and for our soul to separate from our body at that very time. This is not just for us, but it should completely become an understanding for all kinds of people and even all living beings, and the merit acquired from this understanding should be passed on to our children; we must instill in our children the determination to stand firmly in the good deeds we do today. Through them, we should give that love to the world. That should be the goal of our life.

[GV4:P1022] So, regarding this goal, people might say that it is Vedanta being spoken, or that such things exist in the realm of knowledge. In this special karma, permitted to impart to us the aspect of knowledge from the divine presence, the experience each of us acquires should flow through our children, passing on to us, our ancestors, and the future generations; since we are in a karma that has been extremely delayed in adopting such an experience, we must not have any other resolve except the singular determination that we will perform our karma with God at the forefront, to the best of our understanding. That is all we have to do. By fulfilling that, we are clearing the path for the coming children to act, thereby eradicating the prolonged miseries of our souls. You must not drift away from this karma. Although this has been reiterated many times, it is understood that most people find it difficult to grasp. Therefore, it is impossible for you to grasp it if it is explained to you point by point. What is it? Let me say it in brief.

[GV4:P1023] Through the permission granted by God, we are able to see the karmic flaws that occurred across these Manvantaras, and we must observe the miseries of the great souls who acted as the greatest scholars and the most perfected sages there. For one, it is enough to look at our recent times. Going further back would be very difficult for us. Finally, before the beginning of this Kali Yuga, it was Sri Krishna who was born for us and demonstrated it for the welfare of this world. However, since we are nothing in that realm of knowledge, the scholars later rewrote it as well. We are witnessing the play of the narrative hidden behind the miracle, told as a story that created wonders through incarnation and birth once again. This is not what we need.

The transmission of the karma that we perform entirely with a sense of dedication will reclaim this atmosphere. It stands in the dharma of mind, word, and action. If you just justify it in some way, it will not be correct. You will realize that there is a wave that is beyond thought, fully imparted in these three states. It is impossible to explain what it is like. It is beyond thought, beyond intellect too. A karma that has reached such a state is a gift bestowed by God upon you and your lineage. No matter how much each of you grieves over it, it will not increase. This is not a subject introduced for individual worship or for any religious doctrine. Each of you who has received the fortune to acknowledge, see, speak, act upon, and donate to the world what those dharmic actions of the great souls who have come until today are, is great. For this, you should desire and pray that God makes you eternally good. There is no other side to this. Therefore, once you reject the time destined for you by God, you must not resort to actions or karma ready to make someone else reject it. It is a great karmic principle that does the smallest possible karma and cultivates and highlights a great merit. Do not lose the opportunity God has given you so that none of you ever act forgetting this.

[GV4:P1037] Experiencer: It has only been two years since I became a believer in the Guru. Five to eight years prior to that, I owned thirty cents of land in Cherthala. There was no place I had not visited in order to sell that property. From everywhere I went, I would be sent back with a promised date. When visiting temples, they would say it would happen after forty-one days. Thus, I visited numerous temples. Thereafter, when I came to have the *darshan* of the Guru for the first time, I told the Guru right away that I had a thirty-cent plot in Cherthala, and that despite going to many places, I had not been able to sell it. The very first thing the Guru told me was, "Dear one, you just pray." I went home and spent my time in prayer. My mother and I came here together. After arriving, I explained the situation to the Guru in detail. I mentioned that there was a serpent grove and thick vegetation there, and therefore, everyone who came to inspect the land turned back. No one would buy it upon seeing it. That was the condition of the land. Then the Guru said, "Let all that remain there. It can be removed when the time comes." After that, when I returned home, people started coming in large numbers for the land. At that time, it was a person from Vaikom itself who came and paid an advance to buy the property. The agreement was for a period of six months. Even after six months, there was no sign of them preparing to register the property. The reason was that they were a party who bought and resold real estate, and after they entered into an agreement for this land, even their other properties were not being sold. They came to me and said, "Brother, after taking this land, none of our other trades are moving." They had a suspicion; they did not know if it was because they took this land. You must certainly believe this: it was precisely because they took it that their other land was not selling. It was a land with such severe afflictions. It was due to the presence of these worshipped deities. They were worshipped deities such as Nagaraja and Nagayakshi. That was revealed in the astrological consultation. The Guru had already told me about it. The people who bought the land and I together went to an astrologer. The astrologer then stated that entities like Nagaraja, Nagayakshi, Arukola, and Yakshi were present there. The astrologer stated that it would only change if a major *homam* (fire ritual) was conducted. I told the person who came to buy the land, "I am a believer of this path. Therefore, I will do it only after asking the Guru." Knowing this, the astrologer said, "Then, you pray." I held onto my Guru and prayed. After that, he first said that the serpent had moved away. The astrologer was saying that what remained after that was even more powerful. I said, "You check it. How can you say without checking?" Then he laid out the cowries a second time. Upon checking, he saw a pattern where all of these were completely removed. Then how would they know it was changed? I said, "Let me go to my Guru and return; let me tell the Guru." I came here and told all these things to the Guru. Only my mother and I were present. The Guru called the *Janani* (Mother) and had it checked. Then, He explained the manner in which it had been removed, and instructed us to pray earnestly. After all that, when I went there, they immediately came running to me. It was to go to the astrologer again. The three of us went to the astrologer again. I had taken permission from the Guru. He had told me to go and check whenever I wished. On that day, Saturday was not an issue at all. There were many other people waiting to conduct astrological consultations that day. Thus, the astrologer checked. Upon checking, all these entities had been completely removed from there. It had been previously stated that the house had no divine grace. Now, upon checking, the very same astrologer said that complete divine grace was seen there. My Guru had completely removed all of that. They too believed it. I told them that it is a method of removal through mere divine resolve (*sankalpa*), without offering even a single flower. I possess that experience. All of them are now ready to come to the ashram. Subsequently, on that very day, immediately after the astrological consultation, they said that the *chitrakoodam* (serpent abode) should be removed from there. There were groves in two locations. I asked the Guru about that as well, asking what I should do. The Guru said, "You can boldly remove it." He added that if I wanted, I could call some believers from there to join me. The three of us who went initially went together. Internalizing the Guru's words, we went there, sprinkled some *theertha* (holy water), and prayed. After praying to the Guru earnestly, and with the Guru's permission, we removed it from there. Now, the very people who bought the land say that there is a special illumination there. Previously, they were hesitant to even come there. This is my experience.

[GV4:P1043] Become the masters of the karma that strives for the soul.

[GV4:P1044] The deity, or as we now call them, the rishi, the ascetic, the practitioner, the wise one, the devotee. This has its own unique capability. If we are to transcend that capability, we need someone to guide us. Simply guiding us minimally and instructing us to chant the Moola Mantra or the Jnana Mantra will not serve the purpose. That is, they are performing an action that he begged for on that day. They are asking, "O Father! We do not know what this is that is seen." Then they are praying from there. Supplicatory prayer. That is what they mean when they bow on their knees and perform the Namaz, saying it must be recited like this. They have proceeded in this manner. He is a prophet who came at the very end. Should we or should we not understand the fact that even though so many of these masters came to India, they did not understand this in any way? Once that is understood, if we debate who said the greater thing and who said the lesser thing, where will we end up? It is quite clear that we have such a flaw. (To change this) This is called the Trimurti system among Hindus. Shaivism, Shaktism, and Vaishnavism. One says the Vaishnava is greater. Another says the Shaiva is greater. Yet another says no, the Shakta is greater. To whom should we go to know what is lesser and what is greater? What is being said here is a practice that follows our path of mantras. No one can say that it does not exist. Who will we go and ask about who is greater and who is lesser in this? Is everyone great, or is one of them great, or are they all bad? Then they will just keep holding on to the branch they caught. Should we or should we not know that our predecessors have placed such a predicament before us? Upon seeing this knowledge, should we or should we not know how to discard it or how to adopt it? Only a person capable of discarding all three of these, namely the aforementioned Shaktism, Shaivism, and Vaishnavism, can do this. Only then can they guide you well. If this is what happened to Islam, which proclaimed that there is nothing other than You, then what is the meaning of the words of Jesus, who said instead let the rocks split, when he asked, "Father! Have you forsaken me?" Is this right or wrong? How are the followers of Narayana Guru Swami, who said that caste should not be asked, spoken of, or thought about, acting? "This too is our Swami!" Right? Thus, in each case, the rabbit they caught has horns. Proceeding in this state, things have become ruined across our generations. To change this, we must mutually understand what this apostle says, or what this saint says, or what this Sri Shankara says, or what even Narayana Guru has said today. Shouldn't we? Then we must act towards it. Otherwise, it will be detrimental to us. Otherwise, we will not seek anything in this. Everything we do will become a disaster for our future generations. Then we will not be able to do anything. What I am saying here is my own understanding. It is not simply stated in a commercial language. If you ask what caused me to say so—even if you ask, I will tell you. But I am telling you this because I have studied it that way. In that context where our mothers and sisters or our grandchildren are supposed to grow, if we hold on to all this and praise it as God, we must see where we will end up after death. Or does life end once we die? Then it will go and stay somewhere. Isn't there an acquaintance shaped by so many of our ancestors worshipping? What is the use of holding it here without granting it liberation too; won't it cause harm from there? You should understand it this way. Other matters come later. Then, didn't you ask if you couldn't go to this temple? You can. You must go to the temple. But how? Some of you who come here are often heard saying something like this. The fact is that other than coming and going, they haven't understood this. That is, when you come like this, they come saying they have some illness, some trouble, or that their boy is not well-behaved, or their girl is not well-behaved. When they are asked and made to understand if they are convinced that there is a specific flaw in this, "Yes, everything is clear, now what should be done? It must be removed. How to remove it? Just remove it for us." And then? Then we will do what is necessary. How? By going to that Madan shrine—understood? This is what going to do what is necessary means. I said, you don't need to come here for that; I will change it for you. There is no karma for this. There is no justice. There is no justification. I will change it. You must do such and such. You, as parents and children, must be like this. Only then will my doing this bear fruit. Otherwise, you yourself will go and invite it back, do unnecessary things, and render this effort of mine vain. I am doing this for you by expending this karma of mine accumulated over eras. If you do it, do it after understanding that. They will fold their hands and say they will do it. But apart from these words, if anything happens, they will go and sit at the nearest family temple and the nearest some major temple. Then, is there any use because of what was done? This must be changed first. That does not mean tearing it all down and throwing it away. Let all that remain there. Demolishing stones and bricks will not make it go away. So, feeling that let it stay there for you, you should embrace an action capable of teaching our children what to do about it. Or will you tell them to get out when they grow up? I am not speaking of karma in this manner. It is to acquaint you with transforming this that I have come here. You have an obligation to ask why I happened to come here when I do. This is the reason for telling you not to go to the temple. If I change this for you and tell you not to do this, and that we must do such-and-such from now on, you should not handle it unless you have understood it. Otherwise, it will only bring us further harm. It is dangerous if one does not learn to do it properly. We do not know where our ancestors and our parents go and stand after death. Then what are the characteristics of this soul? What must be done with it? Where should it be stationed? What I am telling you is the path to grant it rebirth or liberation. Is it possible not to say this? You are the authorities meant to show what you are to your coming generations, once you have understood this. Should this benefit our home, our land, and our nation, or is it enough if it benefits only our home? We should not act for the sake of our caste or for other superficial affiliations. It is not enough that only you understand this. If everyone you call father, mother, children, husband, and wife are not together in this, there is a defect. Do you know why? Suppose it was done out of your preference. When you go home, your mother will ask what was said earlier. Then, will you fail there or not? You will fail. When everyone fails like that, it's over. Make them understand first. We must speak to them only after making them understand it initially. Thus, a practice that benefits our father and mother, and if necessary, our land, home, and nation, must come into your hands. Otherwise, it will not go away just by showing off this pretension. Now, don't you want to hear about the temple? Do you know why I said this? I am saying this so that youths like you will ask. Only if asked can I speak. Otherwise, if told, one will just say, "Ah, fine, not bad," and leave. It is not that. Rather, by instilling in you an action subject to some resolution, you are becoming the owners of the karma striving for your souls. We all need this. Let us do it that way. By offering another excuse, it won't leave our homes. Else, is it possible to bring a rationalist and have it removed? Let us bring those who have everything. And ask them to remove all this. They won't be able to either. What I am stating here is not such a matter. This is not a karma I performed now, but rather some merit from past lives across immemorial time. For twenty-nine years, I have properly heard Pushpanjali for this duty passed on to me through words. What is this Pushpanjali? It means this scolding. About five thousand people have surrounded and yelled at me. But due to my Guru's grace, they did not beat me to death. That itself is a thing. A pinch from everyone together would have been enough to finish me. I could realize this only due to the maturation over twenty-nine years. I observed that by holding on to the arguments of this aforementioned deity, or goddess, or some other religion, or our own religion. After identifying what it was, when I looked for the action above it, I found Dharma. I have emerged from a lineage of Gurus who showed me that Dharma. I have not brought this in the manner that random people talk about. When you understand this, and when these young children grow up under your care, if we must do anything to improve these children, shouldn't our homes, lands, and country become good similarly, after entirely comprehending these matters? This is what I said earlier; didn't they teach not to invoke these devils? Who? The Prophet. They didn't leave him alone. They chased him away by beating him. That group drove him up one mountain and set fire to the other. But he survived by roasting and eating a dead animal and returned from there. Today our people go there, drag along these blocks of ice, travel to places where water is scarce, do all that tied work in that desert, and come back here showing off. They do not impart this understanding even to this home where they live with their children, husbands, and wives. "I have suffered this much, my daughter! Else, you should do only such and such. Children should do only such and such. I have suffered this much. I achieved all this by passing under this iron rod." They will impart nothing of this agony. This is a matter wrapped up merely to project the greatness of the father and the mother. Will we get anything good from their hands? Understanding it like this, what you need to know is what you should do so that something positive happens through you. Otherwise, what can we do if we quarrel over God or say, "My God is greater, take yours and throw it in the gutter!" But it is not that. If there is such a thing as God, it cannot be different things for different people. God will not become many, though interpretations might range higher or lower according to our understanding of God. Should we or should we not learn what such a divine contemplation should be and how it should exist? Learn this first. The rest can be learned later. Didn't I mention, did you observe that reality which rested upon the sufferings of the Prophet and Jesus? Similarly, it is said that the great saint known as our Sri Shankara leaped into a gorge. It is also said that Sri Rama went down into the water and attained Jalasamadhi. If asked why, there is no answer for that. The question is whether all this is needed among you youngsters or not. Learn like this. Then study how we should bring about whatever feels preferable to you, how... how it must be imparted to our wives, children, mothers, etc. First. Other things later. Do not discipline anyone to make them better. They will not improve like that anyway. If we do it this way, we will have to internally honor and understand what the karmic fate of our life is. That Dharma will pass to our children, our wives, and our mothers. It will reach wherever it can. Wherever the son arrives. It will reach them there too. Don't we need this one achievement? This is the matter.

[GV4:P1045] There are certain determinations of subjects recognized in ashrams or even in the very nature of temples. We are utilizing them based on our misunderstandings. What is that? Showing miracles. From that, utilizing great occult powers (Siddhis) to convince people that 'this is God's will'—such things have existed before and still exist among us today. But is all this God? Does God need this? We have never thought about this till today. Then, in another way, yoga, sleight of hand, and magical powers have transformed to make us believe that this spiritual nature is such a great thing. Among us today, if most people see a sanyasi (renunciate) or someone with any other kind of imitative nature, what pierces their minds are the miraculous tricks of these magical powers. If we rejoice in these tricks, what divine quality do we get? Is our God such a God? If so, isn't it enough just to practice and observe all that? But that is not what we need today. We have thousands of habits that we have worshipped for a long time, whether right or wrong. To say they don't exist might be right for that moment. But they won't simply cease to exist. If we feel this needs to be changed, how can it be changed? Who should change it, and what kind of person should they be? Because we lack information about all this, we have misunderstood many things. It's not like that; not only can all this be changed, but you must also live according to the dharma of this era (Yugadharma). This is the greatest fortune we have received today. It is a mere illusion to desire that we can get this fortune realized through brahmacharis (celibates) or sanyasis. Why? Sanyasis don't have children or anything. And not many can live their way. Then what to do? The householders (grihasthashramis) who live by doing karmas should see what the center of worship of our ancestors was, who acted in many guises and languages, and without simply changing it blindly, they should do what is necessary for it and then bring about the change. Simply changing it without purpose won't work. We can only achieve it if we have such karmic capacity. When we do this, we face a lot of difficulties and hardships. I can only speak about the information concerning me. Whatever else has happened elsewhere, must have happened. And it will be conducted. Regarding me, since my childhood, I had a thought: what is it that we need to attain, and how will we accept it? Whatever it is, there was divine grace for that. As a guide to that, if the people who get it and handle it don't become householders and their lineage, we are taking upon ourselves the greatest sin of destruction that can come upon the world. You must be able to change this. So, as far as I am concerned, everyone certainly knows that there is disease, difficulty, hardship, and suffering. But there is no need for this disease to come. At the same time, there is no need to suffer. People will bring whatever is needed for two, four, or ten people to survive. That will be enough. But that is not our goal. Seeing the right and wrong that have come in the tradition, we must pass it on to our children and whatever generations and lineages are yet to come. When we say lineages, it refers to the three types of worship orders among Hindus called Shaktheyam, Shaivam, and Vaishnavam. The path of our doctrine is to understand the karmic movements standing in this divine presence or star constellations beyond that, act upon it, and give it to our lineage. If this path is not clear to you, you won't be able to do it in any way. During the different transitional states of this, I have suffered some physical ailments. That can happen to anyone. But for others, it has usually led them to death. Except for the fact that death did not occur, all other pains have come. You had a perception before. We have a tradition behind us that has seen, heard, known, practiced, and observed the karmic systems of thousands of yogishwaras who practiced yoga, and some paths known through wisdom. There are certain special rules to know how to remove it and bring it before us, and through whom it should be brought forward. But I am not in a position to explain all that today. You will be told about all this. Since my physical condition today doesn't allow me to summarize and explain all this, someone among them will tell you about it. Because of passing through various states, the body has been damaged. Now, my soul has no damage, but the body is damaged. I cannot describe what it is right now. Therefore, please understand it at your own pace. Then, they will explain the reason and significance of this event called prayer now. Whatever it is, do it properly. Now, most people among us are not capable of making us understand in the way we need. However, it can be achieved through our effort and through karmas we undertake with repentance. What is it? If we do not regret past actions, we cannot take this up. You should be told about that too. There are several such subjects, many additional subjects. From them, we will listen briefly to one or two subjects and then go for prayer. If one person has come from our house, if it is not understood by everyone in that house and, if necessary, by the neighbors, and if it doesn't reach the people, it will become a great sin we commit against ourselves. We must understand the karma that if God has given us an opportunity and we do not accomplish it, there is a punishment for it.

[GV4:P1046] Guruvani

[GV4:P1047] Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Dedication Edition 2004

[GV4:P1048] He who speaks has not seen, he who has seen does not speak.

[GV4:P1049] The fourth face is a special manifestation of the imagination of knowledge. It cannot be corrected or modified. It is regarding such a face that the term 'Nanmukhan' (four-faced) is used. If this passes through the Trinity or the three faces, it will only be creative. A dissolutive special imagination that the disciple earns is also the essence of the Guru. In that path, the Guru-disciple relationship does not differentiate between male and female here. That itself is the Supreme Brahman. It is a truth that can only be repeated for the Guru and the disciple. It will seem like nothing on that path is learned or acquired. It will feel like in that Guru's life and growth, nothing is learned or acquired. Only the disciple will know that everything emanates from within himself without his conscious knowledge. Only the disciple can know the Guru. No one else can know. Such disciples are of thousands of types. Just as these seven notes are expanded into sixty-four musical notes, wherever the note ultimately settles, that is the Guru. The one who understands that is the disciple. That is why it is said that only the disciple speaks, and the Guru does not. When a scholar applied intellect to this and brought in their knowledge system, they wrote that the one who speaks has not seen, and the one who has seen does not speak. That is an act merely fit to be written by imitating the style of these vowels and consonants. How can one know the truth through this? The true word of the Guru is experienced by the disciple without it being spoken. Then one must come into the realization that the Guru and the disciple are one. There is no physical manifestation there. What can be said about the stupidity of writing a commentary just because Advaita was written down! They turn this very stupidity into their scholarship. And then, by speaking of it somewhere, they proclaim themselves as scholars. It means there is no experience. This is the stupidity of the scholar. All those who learned by hearing this repeat the same thing. Remaining here without male or female distinction, they named it Parashakti—simply because they had nothing else to say. Just like going to retrieve a coconut fallen in a mud pit, both the one who took it and the one who didn't got stuck there. Or like going to retrieve a seed fallen in a mud pit. They kept this hidden in the dark. But then, like the Englishman's tale, it sprouted inside. Pitch darkness, new moon. So, blackness. Complete blackness. It is a lid made of black. Inside it, a black cat. The cat understands that there is darkness only when it opens its eyes. This is a story of an Englishman. Will it open if covered with a story like this? It shouldn't be a story, it must become an experience. Now, our people who practice yoga, through asana demonstrations, assign it various other languages and narrate tales of an eight-span body. That will be correct according to their respective hand spans. Will it be correct for a little boy? If it is correct for him to that extent, it simply means it corresponds to whatever his size is. So, yoga is often discussed by incorporating such span measurements. Will things work if this is merely written or spoken about? This is not something that can be measured or written down like that. It is hastily spoken and hastily concluded. About this, Narayana Guru also says: 'One must fall, bow repeatedly, and recite'. When a scholar says this, the word 'repeatedly' loses its meaning. How can he fall repeatedly? Before one thing breaks, another bursts forth. Thus, it turned into an untrue trick constructed within the scholar's hidden strategy. Who can fulfill this? How can it be fulfilled? This is where it becomes a state where the disciple has nothing to share and the Guru has nothing to share, and the consciousness of changing states and differences disappears. It is a chain-like structure of non-existent disguises that teaches names like Dvaita and Advaita. It will seem like everything is there. But there is nothing there. That chain form is of karma. If that is gone, with what will you bind it? For this, saying Hatha Akasha, Hoda Akasha—thus citing Akasha in everything, ending up in a logician's language, speaking so hastily, and moving forward without caring for anything—how does one stand? For a person who goes without caring for anything, it is easy to speak about Advaita. When examining the karma and dharma paths of the commentator, it is like they built and built, made it dark, and closed their eyes. It is because they cannot explain the meaning of this 'repeatedly' that they close their eyes and create darkness. This love, respect, humility, and richness that grew in the light of time were all nurtured without a divisive intellect. The discrimination between the self and non-self mentioned by the author of the Gita, and the dedication of the self and non-self—whoever can do that is the Guru. The ability to say this, aside from the author of the Gita, has not been seen to this day. Or if it has been said, it is merely the iron fist of Vedanta's haste. It will not reveal the truth. Dvaita and Advaita are attained by climbing the steps of the Guru-disciple relationship in many ways. What is needed is not carefully explaining its meaning. Vowels and consonants are not required for this. In dissolutive love, glory, and truth, without the intrusion of disrespect, it becomes a merging of fortune and merit—the unadorned steps of the Guru-disciple relationship. This is the Guru-disciple bond. This is not something to be accomplished by pretending to be scholars or non-scholars using vowels and consonants. The result of people writing endlessly and posing as scholars in various ways is the gathering of literal meanings, thereby sowing the seeds of a difficult impasse. This is a crop that can never be harvested.

[GV4:P1050] Guruvani

[GV4:P1051] Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Dedication Issue 2004

[GV4:P1052] A Message for the Welfare of the People

[GV4:P1053] When we acquire a god, a goddess, and a lineage, it is spoken of highly. We have become incapable of knowing where the history of the *Nanmukhan* (four-faced Brahma) has gone, which was formulated by blending the positions of the Trinity (*Trimurti*) with the concepts of the Siddhars and the enlightened ones (*Jnanis*). It is said that many people asked Narayana Guru Swami about these matters. He gave no reply. It was Velutheri Kesavan Asan and Thirunelli Krishnan Vaidyar who posed this question. None of the learned scholars to date have been able to explain what the status of this Trinity and the status of the *Nanmukhan* actually entail. This represents the history of a specific era in India. It is also said that many have logically dismissed its core. Certain other aspects have reached us through individuals who tore pages from historical truth to rewrite them. The reason for this is that it is the lineage of Manu that interprets everything, encompassing all worldly nature. However, to those who have studied extensively, certain elements may appear correct while others seem erroneous. These concepts of right and wrong can be observed if one meticulously examines the history of our Supreme Lord Sree Krishna. But what we have come to know is a situation where poets and their fundamental nature fled in defeat, arrived, and vanished, merely to achieve historical milestones. When examining the timeframe of all our religious doctrines, what we observe is a minor detail. In your own life, you are born, you grow, and you die. Within this span, what is displayed is the extraordinary valor of great souls who went about fabricating tales when the scholar, the ignoramus, and the rogue fled in defeat. It has been written that an era wherein we fight among ourselves and somehow evaluate and reflect upon this is not one we are entitled to. This is what has been written and referred to as the *Manusmriti*. Through this, which foundation do we possess? Is it the foundation of the Trinity? Or is it the passage where Narayana Guru states that the lamp which illuminates upon the cessation of the triad (*Triputi*) cannot be attained by a hypocritical ascetic? Similarly, the Brahmins have also been deceived in numerous ways. When we speak of these Brahmins, what we have heard about is *Karma* (action). How much of this *Karma* can we possibly witness and write about while we are alive!

[GV4:P1054] If this is brought before a great scholar, they will merely read out the names of several books to those who approach them expressing their genuine sorrow. Every book elaborates upon miraculous powers, the disciplines of Yoga, and the protocols of *Karma*. Along with this, one is expected to assume the role of an ignorant believer or devotee. How can this possibly provide an elucidation concerning the *Dharma* of transitional epochs (*Yugantara Dharma*)?

[GV4:P1055] After Krishna, two thousand four hundred and forty-four followers of the Guru's path have appeared. The same applies to Christians. It is said that Islam burst forth from this. Be that as it may. Let us not argue over it. This is because a period of one thousand five hundred years has been attributed to its functioning here. If one clearly and affectionately asks them about this, they will have nothing to say. It involves all the gods, goddesses, and the visionaries who came and went during that interim. From their perspective, all of this is indeed the truth. Why is it proceeding in this manner? No one will be able to provide an answer to that. The reason is simply the ignorance regarding what the *Yuga Dharma* (the law of the epoch) truly is. Numerous branches, which such great men have investigated and stumbled upon, constitute the fundamental wealth of our nation. Multiple attempts have been made to make you understand this in the context of a Guru lineage (*Guru Parampara*). However, consider whether we have not inherited from our predecessors a *Karma* that has stumbled and collapsed under the weight of your intellectual prowess, familial prestige, and academic sophistry! I am telling you this merely to clarify it. You will not understand this easily—that there is an inability to guide your children onto that path. It is the knowledge of a mother who survives merely by straining her vocal cords that resides within the child. To whom, how, and in what manner will this knowledge be questioned? If you yourselves openly discuss these matters within your homes, there is no need to generate such a massive uproar about it. You may examine the calculations of the *Chaturyugas* that have come and gone over these twenty-five *Chaturyugas*—you will find it. It should not be sought through mere scholarly study. Where and how did your Guru act? In what manner were you a witness to that at the time? God has created a lineage to enable you to reclaim this. Men and women must not corrupt this by committing errors. It is not that the aspect of the Trinity and the *Manusmriti* do not exist. Similar is the lineage of the prophets. When they stand before a God brimming with compassion, possessing occult powers (*Siddhi*), abilities, and mastery over mantras, they will render all their capabilities entirely useless before departing. Do not question how we have received this now. Because foundational sciences divided epochs into four and prescribed them as Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra. How long do we think its duration might have been? Unless learned directly from the lips of a Guru, no one can explain these matters. Everyone knows that, as far as you are concerned, all these matters are true. How many great souls have appeared before us to live and learn for the sake of this truth!

[GV4:P1056] Similarly, demonic actions (*Paishachika Karma*) are described in numerous ways. If we keep completing all of these, across how many epochs have we been returning with destructive actions that lead to death and ruin! You have compiled and documented various pieces of evidence for this with the help of those who hold affection. I have also heard some people mentioning this to children. In all those times, I felt that what they were saying was indeed correct. Our governance system represents the acquisition of an ability for India to embrace such a fortune. If they and you contemplate and ask how this should be approached, asking them will yield no results. Consequently, the entire human world, having arrived at this demonic *Karma*, is incapable of discerning what the *Karma* of the father is, what the *Karma* of the mother is, or what the *Karma* of the child is. Therefore, do not proceed by squandering your time. Divine retribution is not merely limited to our nature; our ancestors have beautifully and with solid evidence documented world affairs and the global sphere. However, these scholars will not acknowledge it. When we speak of scholars, we have two types, do we not? If one attempts to resolve one, there is neither root nor branch to be found anywhere.

[GV4:P1057] The divine causality (*Ishwara Nidanam*) was first demonstrated here by the lineage of the Buddha. Although the truth was spoken, it could not be practically lived out. This is being stated so that all of you may comprehend. Here, one can travel by bus, by bicycle, by bullock cart, or on foot. Consider this as an analogy. This is not the primary subject. I shall elucidate all of that subsequently. Thus, everyone, all of you, must safeguard your lives in a manner that leads to true knowledge. It is for this very purpose that you performed *Gurupooja* (worship of the Guru). However, you have not grasped the true essence of *Gurupooja*. That will be explained later. If you do not fiercely protect it, it will transform into an affliction bestowed by God. Each aspect lies behind a truth that you can perceive in detail. Most people generally refuse to accept this.

[GV4:P1058] Guruvani

[GV4:P1059] March 2005. We must first examine the causes of our nation's degradation. It is here that we have committed our most significant errors. The primary mistake concerning our nation stems from initially adhering to certain ways of life—resulting either in its inherent deficiencies or in a form of governance tainted with wickedness. This has been our predicament. In the context of such governance and the ensuing wickedness, our ignorance has led to profound failures that are entirely unjustifiable. This phenomenon is not confined merely to our region or to India; it has occurred globally. However, regarding our capacity to rectify this, our developed critical thinking remains ambiguous. We lack clear guidance on what actions to take today or how to approach these issues, resulting in individuals merely acting according to their own limited understanding without achieving anything substantial. We can briefly examine the root of this failure. It is not minor, but rather profound, though expressing it thus might be difficult for you to accept. Sri Krishna was born prior to the *Kali Yuga*, or more precisely, at the juncture of the *Kali* and *Dwapara Yugas* (the conclusion of one and the commencement of another). In a sense, this represented a profound burden of sorrow, the magnitude of which we have yet to fully comprehend. However, by misinterpreting this, teaching it inappropriately, and attributing everything to the author of the *Gita*, both scholars and the laity fall into an innumerable series of traps. How can one even begin to quantify them? Therefore, this is not what we require today. What the author of the *Gita* stated is accurate. Have we truly accepted the author of the *Gita*? If so, in what manner? This is where our error lies. When asked if we have anything meaningful to say about the long history ordained by divine will across ages, the answer is negative. We consider the pedantic parsing of words to be the highest intellectual achievement, and we each hide behind this superficial cleverness. However, will such pedantic analysis bring any spiritual benefit to your soul, my soul, or any soul in this world? Such exercises merely serve as intellectual entertainment. You will find yourself incapable of performing actions that are genuinely beneficial to your life. Consequently, while existing in a state where you are told that the era of your birth is the *Kali Yuga*, and that *Kali* is detrimental, how can we possibly rectify our situation? You must realize that *Kali* is never inherently evil. That is the most profound truth. What does this mean? We stand in opposition to the divine will that provided the *Shudra* with the opportunity to attain the knowledge of *Brahman*. Sri Krishna serves as a prime example of this.

[GV4:P1060] The history of Kamsa demonstrates the anomalies that existed here even prior to the birth of Sri Krishna. We have been taught that Kamsa was inherently evil. This is fundamentally incorrect. Kamsa was a king. He fulfilled the duties incumbent upon a king (*Raja Dharma*). However, we have failed to comprehend the extent and manner in which this *Raja Dharma* should be executed, or our position within the conceptual framework of the *Yuga Dharma* (duties of the era). Consequently, what has happened to us? As the poet Asan noted, "the mistakes committed yesterday become the established doctrines of today," and so it has come to pass. We remain unaware that we are committing errors. Consider the profound sorrow of parents whose seven infants were ruthlessly killed prior to Sri Krishna's birth. Our historical understanding suggests that he killed all seven and spared the eighth solely because it evaded his grasp. If this account is accurate, what were the consequences of failing to cultivate knowledge about Sri Krishna or failing to generate any benefit or awareness for the subjects? Alternatively, in a region governed by numerous rulers—over six hundred provincial kings—the virtues of one king were absent in another. It is as if they were trapped in a vortex of conflict and conquest, or rather, languishing and suffering within it. Thus, we have merely wasted time observing the ignorance propagated by these kings day by day, or analyzing the achievements of our scholarly lineages, without ever truly understanding or acting upon this knowledge. We still remain incapable of doing so. The circumstances surrounding Sri Krishna's birth evolved in this manner. Yet, the populace of that time lacked the understanding necessary to protect Sri Krishna. Or perhaps, the kings lacked this understanding. Consequently, despite being shown the reality of this king, or the true nature of Kamsa's life, we failed to comprehend it. Kamsa was never an evil person. What then is the principle? It is '*Pratyakshavaham Dharmam*' (Dharma is that which is directly perceived or commanded).

[GV4:P1061] A king is one who listens to whoever explicitly reveals the truth to him. Thus, God stood manifest before him. Standing in that manifestation, what did God do? He dictated *Dharma* to him. Therefore, aside from the fact that he steadfastly acted upon that perceived *Dharma*, Kamsa committed no crime. He killed each infant in accordance with the command he received. The greatest tragedy, however, is that the contemporary kings, scholars, or the wise lacked the intellectual tradition to analyze why he acted in this manner, or to correct and guide him from a position of true knowledge. Why were they unable to offer this corrective guidance? That is another aspect. Our primary occupation consists of recalibrating the magnitude of our ritual offerings, operating under the framework of the currently popular *Trimurti* system, or the sectarian paths of *Shakta*, *Shaiva*, and *Vaishnava* traditions that we individually celebrate. We labor under the delusion that we have satisfied the divine through these means. We can never achieve this. Furthermore, a being thus appeased is not truly God. What then is the reality? There is something we must believe. Why? We construct a temple. Yet, we remain ignorant of what transpired through the lineage of that temple, the temporal scope of the actions of the ancestors who worshipped there, and our current existential position. We have not been instructed on the role of temple traditions within the *Dharma* of this *Kali Yuga*. Additionally, it is universally propagated that the *Treta Yuga* and *Dwapara Yuga* were the specific eras of this deity. Because of this inability to discern, its *Dharma* was executed in the *Satya Yuga*. Its *Dharma* was similarly executed in the *Treta* and *Dwapara Yugas*. However, we find it difficult to believe that this occurred within a Guru lineage. Why? We have before us the practices of even the sages (*Rishis*) who worshipped and adored this deity. But we have not acquired the knowledge to explain the underlying reasons for this. What is the cause? We lack detailed information concerning this *Manvantara*. Or rather, we are ignorant of several critical matters. A *Manvantara* refers to the epoch of a specific *Manu*. The duration of a *Manu's* epoch is said to be seventy-one *Chatur Yugas*. Within these seventy-one *Chatur Yugas*, this *Kali Yuga* represents the smallest measurable fraction.

[GV4:P1063] April 2005

[GV4:P1064] As epochs and centuries have passed, various states of existence have emerged. When we speak of these states of existence, everything from a demon (*pishacha*) to a deity (*deva*) represents a particular state of our being. In the context of this specific state, there are individuals who worship a deity and ultimately perish after attaining the state of that deity. Beneath this hierarchy are *yakshis* and malevolent spirits—are there not individuals in our regions who worship entities like Karinkuttichathan? Similarly, entities like Muthappan and various others have existed in diverse forms. Furthermore, there is a tradition of conceptualizing Subrahmanya in this manner. All of this is factual. It is not that these entities are non-existent; they do exist, and they were venerated by our ancestors. How can we transcend this? If we attempt to overcome it through *yoga*, the *yoga* referred to here is not what we contemporarily understand it to be. The *yoga* mentioned is *Rajayoga*. The others are classified as *Hatha Yoga*, *Hamsa Yoga*, *Chandrika Yoga*, and so forth. Those do not involve *pranayama*. In this *Rajayoga*, there is no *pranayama* either; there is no practice of restraining and holding the *prana* (life force). Having heard all these assertions and assuming them to be superior, we have placed our faith in those ritualistic actions (*karma*) demonstrated during an era like the *Treta Yuga*. That is the *Treta Yuga* and

[GV4:P1065] transferred through the *Dvapara Yuga*, and we are still practicing the very same things. This did not require any modification during the *Satya Yuga*. Back then, during the *Satya Yuga*, humans lived as truthfully as possible. Divided into these eras, we currently refer to the four epochs as the *Chaturyuga*. When speaking of these four eras, the shortest is the period of *Kali* (*Kali Yuga*). This consists of 432,000 years. Double of this is the *Dvapara Yuga*, and double of that is the *Treta Yuga*. Consequently, as we traverse through such vast expanses of time like the *Dvapara*, our practical realities and circumstances undergo complete transformation. Because of this, it is necessary for preceptors (*acharyas*) to emerge from time to time. Only they have the capacity to rectify these matters. This transformation does not rely upon a mere *yogi*, a ritualist (*karmi*), or the simplistic belief that a divine manifestation alone is sufficient. The manifestation of a deity, goddess, or sage is no longer adequate. Their respective eras have concluded. What, then, is the current situation? You must understand this. When such matters arise, unless you gradually inquire and learn, merely attending will yield no benefit for you. You will simply fail to comprehend it. Currently, we have attained the state of a demon, internalizing and worshipping it as part of our heritage. We are subjugated by this demonic entity. We have been worshipping it under the misconception that it is a deity. Over various epochs, we have venerated and empowered it. If we claim it does not exist, how can it simply vanish? Therefore, rather than habituating ourselves to deny its existence, we must acknowledge that it is present. However, to what extent, and in what manner? This is precisely what is termed as the differentiation of transitional states (*avasthantharabhedam*). Thus, when discussing these differences in states, what we must determine is how we completed a specific state or stage, and through what means? That constitutes one aspect of it. Accordingly, the *yogi*, the ritualist (*karmi*), the seeker of knowledge (*jnani*), and the devotee (*bhakta*)—it is through these four paths that one reaches a standstill. There was an era traversed by the *yogi*. That era should not be forcibly applied to the present. Why is that? That must be clearly understood. The era of the *yogi* evolved into the human, which transitioned into the deity, then into the sage (*rishi*), subsequently into the ascetic (*sannyasi*), and ultimately forms the path to liberation as a *jnani*. The deity is not at the forefront. Therefore, the human being itself embodies the deity, the sage, and the ascetic. Concerning our modes of worship, we possess a lineage characterized by the veneration of sacred serpent groves (*sarppakavu*) and similar localized deities. It cannot be stated that these do not exist; they are very much real. The question is, to what extent and in what manner should this existing reality be worshipped and brought to fulfillment? Achieving this requires a profound philosophical vision (*darshana*) of that specific state. We are entirely unaware of the forms or variations we have traversed within a single lifetime. Why, then, should we dwell on it? There are multitude of transitional states. How should one intellectualize and discard them? There are those who question the utility of contemplating such matters—namely, the proponents of Non-dualism (*Advaitins*). To speak as an *Advaitin*, one must have successfully transcended these transitional states. It is not a prerogative granted to everyone. Ignorant of this, individuals utilize merely human intellect, capabilities, and skills in their innate endeavors, celebrating material wealth and education, only to pass away without ever comprehending these transitional states. It is uncertain what has been understood from this. What have you grasped from all that has been said thus far? It is insufficient if we merely continue speaking. May you truly comprehend it. Only when you attain a level of understanding comparable to ours can we progress further. Let us simply impart what we know.

[GV4:P1066] The current epoch is indeed the *Kali Yuga*. There is no utility in regressing to the past; those eras have concluded. Upon entering the *dharma* of this *Kali Yuga*, the Divine itself has caused the manifestation of numerous preceptors and prophets within this realm. Therefore, our *dharma* in the *Kali Yuga* must be one that critically evaluates the rights and wrongs traversed across multitude of past lifetimes. That pertains to understanding the true nature of one's own life force (*jiva*). How can we comprehend this? You must understand it. We must experientially realize the evolutionary nature of the soul, which has taken births even in forms as lowly as a worm. What is the methodology for this? We cannot meticulously sift through and analyze all of that. That is not why this is being articulated to you. You need not contemplate it at all. Dwelling upon it will only cause you distress. However, it is also impossible to refrain from thinking about it. Why? The realization that 'I' am the evolutionary product of a soul that originated from such lower depths inherently characterizes human intellect. It is said that becoming truly human is in itself an arduous task. Thus, do we not commonly say, 'He behaves like a bull'? In such instances, the individual is exhibiting aggressive tendencies comparable to that of a bull. Yet, this is a birth taken in human form. It is the consequence of actions (*karma*) lived out akin to an animal. The entity exists as a human, but possesses only the external physical form of a human. It has incarnated in myriad forms. The differentiation of transitional states (*avasthantharabhedam*) is the process through which one incarnates as a human across multiple epochs, gradually progressing to a stage where human karmic potential can achieve liberation. Nevertheless, one has been born as a human. One might question whether all humans are not inherently human. True; in practical terms, all are humans. No soul exists completely devoid of that nature. Suppose we have taken a birth now. We engage in various acts of worship, perform malevolent deeds, benevolent deeds, unnecessary deeds, and eventually pass away. What becomes of this soul? It will go and merge. Consequently, the lineage of worship that began with demonic entities remains ingrained within us. Will not the latent tendencies (*vasanas*) of that soul manifest? The only tendency derived from birth is that of being human. The soul (*Atman*), however, remains immutable; it is one and the same. It is merely a process of undergoing transformation.

[GV4:P1081] We have received a new method. There are four eras namely Satya Yuga, Treta Yuga, Dvapara Yuga, and Kali Yuga, and each era has its own distinct nature. The invading Brahmins settled on the banks of the five rivers and studied our history. They were those who saw God through their intellect. What they found here was a group of honest people devoid of deceit. They were people who would sleep wherever they pleased. They arrived at a time when the era was undergoing a change. Because times had changed, they could not see God directly. Consequently, they went to the forests and seashores, gazed at the horizon, and performed penance in various ways. They saw different kinds of light and forms. They carved what they saw onto trees and stones. When they contemplated it in their minds, they received words from the light. They received mantras. Thus, the great sages discovered each of these things. They carved many of them on stones, giving them form and color. Westerners called it the mind. Bhakti Darshana, Yoga Darshana, Karma Darshana, Dharma Darshana—the misfortune of this path is that even through a god or goddess, or even by a propounder of Yuga Dharma, these cannot be identified or described. Now, we need to highlight the great souls. Since we do not know what the Karma Darshana according to Yuga Dharma is, it remains distant even to those called seers. It is like asking what happened during the time of Rama or Ravana. There is no point in softly stating that the multitude of humans, who lack the knowledge to even correct and describe the worldview of the many ages that passed before, will not understand anything. However, there is an easy way. We need to cite the great ones as examples to understand, overcome, and clear the grand step of Yuga Dharma, wherein we cannot comprehend how long Karma and Dharma have been flowing astray. This is done by examining the course of Karma from Swayambhuva Manu to Vaivasvata Manu, who obtained foresight across Manvantaras and Kalpas, and by analyzing what a god, sage, ascetic, wise person, and devotee truly are. Let us take the shortest period. Time, as we describe it, consists of Satya Yuga, Treta Yuga, Dvapara Yuga, and Kali Yuga. A Chatur Yuga is formed by these four periods, transformed into an act of Karma by wise ones or practitioners—how many thousands of years does a wise person's foresight span! The length of a Yuga is made up of how many such wise ones. Who corrects and writes the Dharma of that Yuga? Then, how immensely profound will be the pain one has to experience when entering the inner chambers of spirituality? Here, the heavy burdens of destined baseness caused by past karmas are being untied. In its place, we are infusing goodness into our lives through action. This must be accomplished flawlessly. Consequently, one will wander due to numerous difficulties. If one prays along with the household, the whole household will wander.

[GV4:P1095] Devotion has a tendency to become easily agitated. Once a person becomes thoroughly seasoned in Sattvic qualities, they will act with proper understanding. One who has not attained such maturity will get agitated like a fool. Such agitation leads to ruin. The character traits that are supposed to develop over many periods emerge all at once. Whatever good deed is done, a difficulty will always arise first.

[GV4:P1096] For the sake of punctuality, sit for five minutes and pray through your work. Then, constantly fix it in your mind. When this happens, we will be showered with abuses. Illness will also come. Similarly, along with the spiritual vision, sorrow will also arrive. Whoever we see, the sorrow they experienced will affect us as well. Visions should not be spoken aloud for everyone to hear.

[GV4:P1097] If a good deed is done, an opposition will arise against that good. When doing good, resistance will come. When taking steps to prevent the resistance, one becomes exhausted. Any kind of falsehood might be employed here. Considering this as the consequence of the service rendered, an opportunity should be given for correction. When unbearable pain arrives, instead of retreating from there, one must hold on with diplomacy. If one retreats, everything is lost. For example, how did R. Sankar fare among the community? How did Mannam fare? Mannam held on until the end. What was the reason he could hold on? He had a diplomatic approach among the common people. Sankar was not like that. He only thought about monumental things. He would not manage to get things done. He would not speak matters affectionately. Humility was significantly lacking in him. Because he lacked administrative diplomacy, Sankar employed statecraft. Statecraft alone cannot correct those at the grassroots level. Mannam was exactly the opposite.

[GV4:P1098] Ezhavas and Nairs share the same predicament. They do not endure pain in spiritual matters. Nairs are a bit lower in this regard. What is the reason for this? Because they stood under the Brahmins, they could not bring it to their own homes. An elderly woman in the house chanting 'Narayana' with a mark of holy ash. Peons, document writers, village officers, subordinates—all of them apply the holy ash mark. And a dot above it. The pretense is that they are devotees. With this kind of devotion, there will be no hardship. But they do not know how to call out to God with a pained heart. There was a time when things were achieved even by frightening God. These poor people think that God is tied up with the string of fear. The belief is that if the battle between Bhadrakali and Darika is enacted, evil spirits will not enter the house for sixteen years! A face crafted in silver, dotted with rice flour and charcoal, dressed in Bhadrakali's attire with headgear and a sword. Seeing this itself induces fear. We do not have any of that here. Furthermore, there are no tests or miraculous powers here at all. However, the difference is that ours is spiritual, while the other is material.

[GV4:P1099] All we have here is prayer. It is intended for the revival and sustenance of the world. To eradicate the impurities that have existed in our minds until today, and for the fruits of those actions to become ours, first pray, and then put it into practice. If you pray intensely, there will certainly be results. In some child born now, there will be the genesis that contributes to the revival of the world.

[GV4:P1102] The joyful operational capacity to convey the divine message

[GV4:P1104] I am telling you, do not throw it away like this, dear ones; this is an opportunity. None of us will attain this merely by praying nominally. Then why are you being made to do this? [GV4:P1105] Disciple: The Guru himself did not know it initially, nor did those who stood beside him. It was later accomplished through disciples endowed with vision. [GV4:P1162] The Path of the Guide Who Attained Divine Nature

[GV4:P1163] You cannot learn what kind of attention stands in that course of action (karma) where form and name are prepared. Then how do we do it? There is a way for us to learn it. There is no novelty in telling you about something that does not exist. We do not gain any knowledge from it. Although it is good to say that we have heard, known, and seen, we are in a helpless state where we cannot do anything about it. From the atom to how these five elements took form, from the time they became the five senses, there is a karma that has been known by tasting, touching, and smelling. We can speak of this only if we see how life has repeatedly fulfilled the evolutionary nature of that knowledge, which has come down to our present understanding since then. This is wisdom. So, through actions, we have seen some, taken some, and will take more. But nothing of this has really happened yet. We assume that everything is over. We haven't even reached halfway. What is yet to come will arrive suddenly and end. Therefore, before it arrives and ends, if we do not acquire this already existing knowledge, it will just pass before us without our knowing it. Therefore, the nature of knowing what we should do for this must come through our acquaintance and experience of knowing God purely as a human being. A Guru is one who speaks from seeing and knowing the karma where the structural variations of atoms stand transformed in all living beings—humans, God, deities, sages, and demons. Seeing and telling is not enough. In the experience of a disciple, what is made to be experienced by a person is seven and seventy experiences for one state. It transforms into seven hundred experiences. It also extends to seven thousand experiences. It is a single state.

[GV4:P1164] Thus, having passed through each state, we must see it with our eyes. We must see deeper than what is seen by taking a photograph. Then, what is it? Because knowledge comes to us from within, we speak, understand, and tell each other. Otherwise, if our child is dull, and we say, "It's my child, let him not be dull," will it happen? We must know this. So, in the knowledge that human evolution has acquired, one must see where this path of dharma has reached the imaginative specialness of the course of karma, traveling as merit and sin. If we and our ancestors have seen the subtle bodies standing there, then our children must also see them. Instead of misleading us and destroying us, showing us the path truthfully, you should be convinced that you are the truth in that karma. Without being convinced of this, none of you can do anything. How will one be convinced? As said earlier about sleep, a person who appears to be sleeping like this. That is "Thoongamal thoongi" (sleeping without sleeping). We would think he is sleeping. But he is seeing how far the measure of time goes. Having seen that, as it transforms into births, a minor visionary speaks of the measure of that birth. For as long as that visionary says, we must practice it. Some will believe it. Some will not. Some will do it. Some will not. Some will find it and change. This is the mistake we have made to this day. What is it? The knowledge that came through each religion, they spoke like that. Like changing customs and tying them, like changing clothes, we changed and wore many things, learning and teaching, and we learned it through various languages in the nature of languages and the knowledge of letters. Those who have not studied the grammar of one language cannot believe that there is another grammar. Similarly, only if you have an experience of at least one thing, say a demon, can you believe that it exists over there. Thus, passing the demon and reaching the nature of the vampire (vetala), past those cities, we are seeing the thinking stage of a guide going to reach the divine nature. That is the special imagination. In this special imagination, in the dharma called "sankalpa karma manasa," life has the nature of a machine that intently watches what the dharma of the mind reached by your imagination is. The knowledge that climbs back to us on how we should take the dharma in that karma, which was imagined in the evolutionary nature of that life, are these children, husband, wife, wealth, lordship, and education. First, we must know what this is. So, knowing this and reaching the part of the knowledge of the aforementioned visionaries is the karma we need to know and take. Wherever mistakes occur, we should be shown them, and told what is what. To whom? To whom will we ask, "Why did you see it like this?" To someone who has experience seeing it; now, even a person who finds the parts of a bicycle and fits them together is a worker. Thus, after everything that runs through this sky and earth, it is said that he must see a particularity of knowing in which era this originated. This is dharma. Otherwise, everyone can say whether this exists or not. Our subject is not to make someone say whether it exists or not. A destruction has occurred in the acquisition of knowledge we have passed through. Rejecting this destruction and certainly bringing it to our betterment, the evolutionary state of life comes to us itself. Jesus speaks about finding such evolutions and knocking to open. But that same person asks, "Father, have you forsaken me?" What can we say to this? If there are any words to say that he was not a sacrifice and that he traveled in a wrong state, it is purely a negative statement. Similarly, they do not even know the karma of making good what all the scholars, the ignorant, and the prophets who have come to this day have said, after calling it bad. So that is not what is being said. What they all said is the truth. The question then is, through what will that truth be seen. So, where we speak of the gross, the subtle, the cause, and the effect, your Guru must reach that course of karma which your mind sees as the karma attained by you, your Guru, and your lineage in what you have achieved standing there. It is the Guru who shows it from there. No one else can do anything about this. So, to know what such a Guru is, one does not walk backward and forward. He sees and questions it there. This is an evolutionary nature. So, we must understand the extent of the course of karma that life has reached to this day. Otherwise, the strength to say "no" will arise from our ignorance. It doesn't matter. Anyone can speak and win. Or defeat. Do many things. We are speaking for neither of these. How we can interact and stay closely, what is the way for that—that is what is called the greatness of the Guru.

[GV4:P1219] Service must be shared as God's own

[GV4:P1220] The people of this land know me. Especially, we started this hospital in a state where the people living in our ashram environment, or living around here—all the people who are alive—were unable to assess the purpose of our hospital. But it is a kind of, as people say, like a worm crawling and forming a letter, it is like that. None of you should assume that this was due to the foresight or contrivance of any of us. Moreover, from that day to this, there is a working capacity demonstrated by the men and women who have come to work in the hospital, knowingly or unknowingly. Those who come in the future must recognize this and progress at the pace of that understanding. That is why I am saying this. What is it? This was brought to fruition by making ignorant youths and people with no connection to medicine do it. But they were not only brought to get it done, they were also given the responsibility and made to do it. Therefore, every individual who has worked here since then knows that they can do and get anything done. This is the part called healthcare service. The healthcare service that we have heard of is not something we do in the manner of today's government service or with the character of a private hospital. We can do that too. But that is not it. Our service, the service rendered by the men and women here, must have God's approval. We should not do it with the arrogant attitude that we are serving someone. We are serving the people. By setting up an institution, taking it upon ourselves, and doing it ourselves, a complete dedication to the world must come through us; it must reach the whole world. This should be our goal. It should not turn into a competition for sharing money and wealth. There is one good thing here, two or three groups have told me. People who were our inmates came to the hospital for treatment. Not inmates, householder disciples. Then they asked these children, what kind of sweeper or super are you? They did not give any reply to that. Later a woman came and said, none of you are qualified to ask us this. Whoever said that, it is a great thing. Because, we are doing a service according to our knowledge and our experience. So there is no need for you to talk about sweepers and supers. Here no one is in the authority of a superintendent. If you are trying to destroy the freedom of us doing a service, then there is no point in your coming here. With that single word, he didn't want to hear anymore. The recognition of your service is what the people who come and experience the healthcare say through your actions. Rather than, as you say, some quacks putting things together—there are such times too. We don't need to explain and show any of that. As far as we are concerned, the service of an ashram means this, it is to show this. So even if not all of us have understood what ashram service means, I have tried to make those who listen to me do it as much as possible. There are people who have started showing that they don't want it, or that it is beneath their dignity, that they are not this and that. They have also learned it as such. But that is not what we need. As far as we are concerned, we have nothing to gain by fighting and winning like this. What we have to gain is to ensure our service reaches whoever it can reach. It doesn't matter if they are great or poor, or a beggar or a destitute. What does a destitute know? He doesn't know. What can a beggar do? But we must handle it without thinking about any of that.

[GV4:P1221] It is getting it done through you to the best of my ability. I have not called a single child here for anything else.
