[GV4:P1224] The Path of Perfect and Supreme Sacrifice

[GV4:P1225] Humanity as a whole lacks a sense of Dharma (righteousness). Let that be. Nothing can be said to these absolute fools masquerading as scholars who try to drag humanity into an idiocy incapable of even recognizing the flaws in Karma (action). There is no point in talking to them. They are merely destined to perish, be born, and die entirely. There is no use paying attention to them. We do not need to absorb them into our intellect. Nor should we look for good in them. Let them remain as they are. We should not even attempt to reform them. If we try to reform them, we too will become corrupted. So, what if you stand firm like that? You must be thoroughly vigilant in your actions, and when another person experiences it and behaves with humility towards us, it should be transmitted to the world through him. That is our goal. You must never act forsaking this goal. Boys and girls, similarly, are sent here and taught in this manner. You should not send children here thinking they can absorb something else. To absorb anything from here, doing what has just been said is sufficient. One cannot simply teach or dictate karmic capability. All of that is a karma situated in a lowly state that needs to grasp your fortune and divine favor. That karma cannot be imparted to others. Individuals must absorb it themselves. Therefore, this is exactly what every realization teaches us, instills dharma in us, sanctifies us, and leads us to good fortune. Everything says exactly this.

[GV4:P1226] So, understanding this, at least some of you have said that there is no one here to see the work you have done and questioned why you are doing this. You are all somewhat aware of this. But you must implement it. It took this much time after I said I would come to explain this karma. Therefore, if this karma is to be concluded only upon leaving the physical body, let it be so; I have no grievance regarding that. Every one of you must develop such courage. We must depart, leaving the virtue of this endeavor to our lineage. This is our objective and the path of absolute sacrifice that must be nurtured through attainment, love, and reverence. We shall transform into guides for that.

[GV4:P1228] Why was all this stated? Everyone must understand. We must believe that what all of us are collectively doing on that path is entirely for the benevolence of the world alone. It is not merely for our own good. This will spread into the world. How? How did the British enter here? If they arrived with an intent to harvest—whom are they harvesting? Us; but we are meant to offer that harvest to them in a different manner. To offer it as a service. They harmed us. We must defeat them through another aspect. These Mughals and the aforementioned British are the administrative regimes known to us in recent times. We must not commit any of the acts they did. We must serve them and whatever mischief lies beyond them; by serving them, we must lead them to God. It is not for us to attain merit by bringing it to ourselves. That is not the path of God. Let them reach God. Let them receive whatever they are meant to receive from there. This is our goal. Not even a child among you should act deviating from this goal. We do not require that. Because here, when some people bought pieces of cloth for the children, they refused them. You should not view that as a great credit. We are not permitted to do so. We do not desire that path. Otherwise, if something is to be done, all of us collectively do it in a way that benefits a common gathering. You should also contribute as a part of that. Apart from this, do not accept anything from them and make it our wealth. If we accept ten paise from them, we will incur a loss of eight paise. It is not needed. They need not come to offer us charity. Provide them with service and send them out. You came desiring a good life. But, you will know it. You also know how to act. Any trivial act could destroy it entirely. Do not do that. Do not do so through a word or by making a slight noise. Stating this while seating you here is because it is the karmic flaw of someone who has accompanied us. You must reform them by saying, 'Please do not do that, sir.' That is your responsibility. Otherwise, even upon death, it will not leave his soul. Because, isn't this life experience? It adheres to his soul, and even if this life perishes, it will not be destroyed. It will remain as a flaw.

[GV4:P1229] Where will the possessor of this malevolent mind reach, who upon seeing their service is unable to say, 'I must be able to do something in this, what should I do, you must ask if you need any of my assistance'? One must depart only after demonstrating it. You know where one will go. I have attempted many times to say a good word to you. I did not get the opportunity. Today, I am utilizing this as an opportunity. All of you must receive it with love, respect, and reverence, transform it into virtue, and offer it to others. Let them earn through that virtue, become fortunate, and let that fortune merge into whatever resides as the controller of this universe. This is my proposition. We do not require an administrative system of this kind or independent knowledge of this nature. Our independence is the ownership of a great karma that offers love and reverence to God and earns respect through devotion. All of you must be able to comprehend that. It is in the purity of life that our girls, the segment referred to as the women of ancient Bharat, have received the Kali Yuga as an era to shine most splendidly. However, it grew corrupt like a compass pointing West, and not knowing what to do, their task became wandering here and there with the array of papers they studied, delivering some speeches, and sitting like an MD with one leg crossed over the other. None of these practices should enter among us here. You must not desire to replicate the instinct for violence in the same manner. If desired, all the work we do will become like drawing on water. Therefore, this is not our necessity. Now, the girls who have come here, or the elders, are not permitted to do anything of this sort. Nor do they do so. I consider that a fortune.

[GV4:P1230] The karmic capability that functions as workers and as the wealthy must become entirely our own. It does not belong to anyone else. It is by attaining purity in actions aligned with divine justice and reaching the karma where purity must be demonstrated, that this karma transitions into virtue and is offered to God. It is not that you undertake and perform it by yourselves. Only if you have that understanding can this be executed. Otherwise, do you know what will happen to you? You will discard it and leave, claiming, 'I have done this much, I have seen it all.' That must not occur within you. The experience and capability to do this much have come to you. You must not cast it away and depart. If you leave, you will find no salvation. It was given to you by God—if you ever thought even once that it was given by me, it will not endure. It is not given by me. It was bestowed upon you by God Himself. You cannot go and acquire this opportunity anywhere else. It was God who gave it to you. It cannot be achieved if I give it to you, or if the emperor here sits in penance and grants it. That is not what I am telling you. Before you leave this body after practicing and working to the fullest extent on this glory bestowed by God, we should not even get an opportunity to think or speak a single word contrary to it. Before that, when our life departs from this body, we are the ones who must leave it as an inheritance in this world for those noble births as well. After departing in such a manner, if anyone is to arrive as rightful heirs to execute any truth in this world, it will be our soul.

[GV4:P1233] The Grihastha Dharma of Recognizing the Fortune Decreed by God

[GV4:P1234] The devotees of Narayana Guru must reflect upon their inherent worth. There is lamentation that not a single child is awakening spiritually. Consequently, it is observed that contemplating this now is insufficient—one ought to have considered raising five or six more children earlier. What purpose do they serve? These are words spoken in the final stages. They have not been permitted to accomplish anything. Today, they are all devotees of the Swami. When I state this, can any of you speak merely to appease me? This is what has been observed and learned. I have never desired any of this. I did not act out of a desire for this. My message to you is that you must not squander this time bestowed upon you by God. What does that entail? The phenomena we have hitherto only heard about—such as visions, apparitions, or disembodied voices—are now being actualized in the experiences of your children.

[GV4:P1235] I am not drawing you closer by displaying miracles. That is not my way; may such things never come to me. May God prevent them. That is my sole prayer. What we hold in our hands are the ancestral karmic actions that have striven to prevent householders (*Grihasthashramis*) from attaining this. That is, it has even been decreed that householders are forbidden from engaging in any of this. They have been made to believe that a householder does not need to know what an ascetic (*Sanyasi*), an active worker (*Karmi*), or a wise person (*Jnani*) is. This is the fallacy prevailing among you. On the contrary, being a householder signifies being an individual who perceives reality directly. You did not understand that, did you? That is, isn't the child seeing it now? Are they not your children? The children perceive it. Can you ask, "Why can't I see it?" His father asks, "Why can't I see it?" If you say, "You are uttering lies," what can I say? Similarly, if her husband and everyone else ask me, "What is this, am I not her husband, why can't I see it?" what shall I reply? If you ask, "Are we not the child's parents? Why do you say this is forbidden for us?" what should I say? This is not anyone's personal prowess. It is a fortune destined for you by God. You must become capable of receiving this fortune. It is insufficient if only I am capable. If I accomplish this for you, you must dedicate children to me who can preserve it until the end. Is it not so? Therefore, it is you, the children living as householders, who are needed. They must undertake this. Through their progeny, this imparts goodness to the ancestors, deities, sages, ascetics, and the souls claiming liberation, who have been faltering until now. If this goodness is imparted, it will be fully realized by our seventh generation. It will only be perfected by the seventh generation. Once you experience this, honoring and adopting it is your responsibility. It is not for me to do. Apart from the fact that God has granted me permission, I cannot tell you anything else. I can facilitate it for you. You are the ones qualified to receive it. I would not suggest anything that you cannot pay attention to, would I? Have I ever spoken thus? Did you hear? I will not say such things. Now, this did not occur because the child desired to become an ascetic, or because you desired it. In her life, she does not know if this is raw or ripe. A young child. She lacks even ordinary worldly intellect. She does not possess a crooked mind. She only possesses a straightforward mind. It is this child who has received this. Thus, in the exact same manner, the family members in the householder stage are receiving it. If you ask me about receiving this, I can provide an answer, but it is you who must realize it. Is that right or wrong? My task is merely to call upon you and state the truth; my work is not to mislead you along a path for invaluable wealth by making you believe that you will receive grand arrangements, great visions, or huge lumps of gold. I will not make such claims. This is something bestowed upon you by God. How should you receive it? You do not even know. Therefore, this is not something we can purchase with money. Your lineage of children does not comprehend what this is. What can I do? This cannot be preserved in your home.

[GV4:P1236] You have had the fortune to receive it! You must inquire into the reason for it, and even if we do not reach its full extent through association, each of you must possess the ability to preserve it as the truth. Must you not? Is it enough if I do it? This is my perspective. I am not drawing you closer by performing miracles. I will not exhibit such methods. Nor have I ever exhibited them. May God never grant me an opportunity for that. So, you are receiving all this. That is true. You can only perceive this through a person who has the rightful claim to it. A person with such a rightful claim is being revealed to you. You may accept that person according to your own understanding of how they should be received; this is not a matter confined to a story narrated by someone. If the ancestral purity of our forebears, or divine purity—the deity they worshipped—is not rectified and aligned, this will collapse midway. Do you remember it being said that the Shudra class will not understand this? That itself is the ignorance prevailing among our people, where arrogance is displayed and wealth is wasted merely to misinterpret and ruin this.

[GV4:P1237] We must evaluate this path of truth as something that imparts goodness to those born as humans like you, or even to all living creatures. The reason I constantly speak to you is for all of us to uniformly understand that this has never been transmitted through any caste, religion, or class thus far. Is it not your responsibility to implement this completely? Instead, no one should allow you to be led down a corrupt path by uttering trivial words. This is not something one can witness by merely walking through an entire lifetime. You must comprehend and practice this. Even if one listens for an entire lifetime, it is impossible to hear this completely. Is it possible? Many people come here and display their affection and respect in various ways. However, you must understand one thing. If a word is spoken incorrectly, you must rectify it immediately. Obey, act, and assimilate. Nothing else is required. Do not behave in a manner devoid of dignity. Do not speak excessively. Sometimes, we may not find the time. We must act by visualizing ten years ahead, contemplating and performing each action mentally, envisioning that it should manifest in a specific concept and specific manner. For those ten years, we are merely working. After ten years, it will reach our intended destination. Our conception then elevates further and further. When we achieve that, it will ascend to another level. This is how it functions. Human conception possesses such a capability.

[GV4:P1238] You must keep your word. There is a predicament in it that will not stop even if I attempt to obstruct it. That is why it was said that those who do not uphold their word truthfully should not undertake this. The word is truth. When we experience that truth, it becomes the Guru. When it is experienced yet again, it becomes God. What you are doing to me, the one who has guided each of you to this karmic duty, is the exact opposite. I cannot refrain from telling you this. Do not assume that this is being addressed to newcomers. But it is indeed to them. Because, if they are merely believing, coming, and going in this manner, it is sufficient that you believe after understanding the nature of the place you are visiting. Otherwise, there is no need to create a stench like someone pointlessly carrying fish tied to their shoulders. You must understand what needs to be done with this. I am expressing my agony to you. You are aware that there is no limit to the abuses I have endured thus far. I am telling you this after having heard and known such abuses over twenty-nine years.

[GV4:P1239] Have those who believed gone wrong? I do not see it as their fault either. What is it? We are the children born in that zodiac where we do not know whether it is a divine system that had a slight flaw in its mythological authorship in the past, or in which lineage it aligns. What can be done? This is why I tell you after having done it for you, do not do it again in return. I am truthfully telling you something that has come to my knowledge. You do not need to do anything else. Just be mindful of the words you speak. You must not do anything that would corrupt me, you, and the generations to come by participating in this. Because I have removed it. This is Gurupooja. It does not happen everywhere. So, we have managed to do it that way. But there is no one to take it back. What is the use of making me do this? You all believe that I know this. I have a sorrow that, in accordance with your knowledge that is so many years old, you could not come forward as children and children's children. Whom will I tell other than you? That is why, even though this body of mine is in such a bad condition and I am so unwell, I am speaking to you like this. The person speaking is someone who is unable to utter a word. But there is sorrow. There is pain.

[GV4:P1240] Please, those of you who are present and those who are yet to join, kindly believe that we are preparing our children to remove a part of a karma that we have been experiencing for so many Chaturyugas (four-age cycles). Otherwise, we cannot do anything. Because we have grown this much and reached this age. What will you do now? Not that. If the children to be born and the parents to be born do not live truthfully, what can I do? It will be exactly like washing it away in the water. Therefore, at least those of you who have performed this act called Gurupooja should tell each of your children to preserve it carefully. Otherwise, I cannot do anything. It is not something that will change just because you change it. I do not have the strength to believe until today that anyone else will change it. I am telling you this conclusively. You know that too.

[GV4:P1241] Guru Vani

[GV4:P1242] Birthday Revered Dedication Edition 2005

[GV4:P1243] The Evolution of Knowledge Beyond Thought

[GV4:P1244] If all our forms exist like this, how does it stand in the gross state, how does it stand in the gross, subtle, and causal states, how should we take back that karma—the one who teaches this is the Guru. You must ask only after seeing it; you should not question it by doing acrobatics with words. This is not that. Yesterday, or just like that, an ignorance came to me. I have my mind, I have my karma. Or rather, there is no deficiency in the body. But when it comes to consciousness, an ignorance has crept in. If asked "What is it?", the familiarity that explains it, its medium, has led us through various paths today. One loses consciousness, one becomes ignorant despite having consciousness, another speaks nonsense after expressing all consciousness. So, he knows this. Even if he is crazy, he blabbers about the special things he knows. So, the knowledge of what this crazy person is blabbering about is what we see as madness. What the knowledge that stands beyond that madness is, can be seen as worldly madness too. Or else, it can be seen as a worldly drama. In the karma that takes place within this drama of the world, who is each one of us? What obligation do we have? In the dharma that we must reach through our lives, from our little children onwards, we are born and we die—or say there is no birth and no death; such people have no authority to speak about visionaries. Why do they say that? Therefore, do not say both together. Say only one. You should only strive to explain the evolution of that one. There is no merit in saying it doesn't exist without knowing anything, or saying it does exist without knowing anything. This is the Guru. What kind of Guru is that? There should be a Guru who can take us at least up to the devil. What is it? Is he not human? Then why take us to the devil? If we do not know what that devil is, we will end up in actions celebrating that it does not exist. But when they progressed by knowing like us, they say "Vethala Nagaram Batha" (Alas, the city of ghouls). Climbing up from there, starting with the Trinity system and the Mother, and reaching the karma called Allah, after completing that dharma or Shaktheyam, Shaivam, Vaishnavam, what stands in the place of gross, subtle, cause, and effect—the one who teaches this course of karma is the Guru. Thus, being interpreted through letters that no such karma exists, or by following the path of eminent scholars who have come through ages of writing, studying, listening, and knowing, we end up discovering it in such a wonder-inducing karma. Then God is seen like that. Taking out things wonderfully from the sky and the earth like that. But nothing can be taken out that does not exist in this earth and sky. That is the truth of it. So, it exists. It is there somewhere. It can be taken from there. That is not a big deal. That is not what you should obey. We have it. Suppose we get a gold block the size of Kerala. What should we do? Will we just take it and swallow it? So, it is not like that. How has that gold undergone its evolutionary nature? Coming back like that and changing it into its tools, who are we as far as that karma is concerned? Thus, transformed into these five elements, disguised as the five senses, trapped in the knowledge of the five sheaths, in the karma discovered through those nine lights, combined with toxic and non-toxic goods and united through yoga, who is greater among them? This is our thought. So, this has taken a different path. It is said in the language of another scholar that he is the one who discovered the dharma of this world. What is it? Carpenter, bell-metal worker, blacksmith, goldsmith. Another knowledge we have is that they have been practicing it for that. Then they brought him, gave him a different knowledge, and did another job there too. They gave him a chanting thread too. Let it be there. But it is through the left side. The right side is for this intelligent one. How will we know the dharma of this karma where deceit, lies, and truth are mixed together? First, you must believe that all these exist—knowingly or unknowingly. No one needs to show this to us anymore. But now, moving towards the realm of knowledge that only tells us the mistakes and good deeds we have seen so far is what is called lightness and heaviness. The previously mentioned Guru must teach us the course of karma that takes such lightness. There is a state we see sitting with our eyes open and closed. Bringing us to this point, separating us from there, and telling us that you can achieve this state only if you combine these things—that Guru must teach this. So, it is not enough to do it for one or two. Going on and on like that, performing millions of courageous karmic acts, we just need to discover the greatness kept before us and work in alignment with that greatness. We don't need to go back anymore. All those things definitely exist. Now it is not difficult for us. We don't need to search elsewhere to learn the names of tools or things. God has also given us the intelligence to take them by blending love and respect in the respective spheres where we have seen, heard, known, and studied everything in our language and reached the position of knowledge. It is this love that we must discover. This is the Guru.

[GV4:P1245] Therefore, such Guru-hood must be imparted to you. Having imparted this, whatever be the Dharma mentioned—be it of a prophet or anything else. Or be it five thousand; that too is acceptable. But it is not like that. The Dharma of Kali, which is said to span 4,32,000 years, is a cycle of time that is completed by five Gurus. Beneath that, there are many thousands, hundreds of thousands of Mahatmas who attain the second, third, fourth, and fifth states. It is not that, because we only mention the names of twenty-seven stars. But it catches our very eyes—how many crores of stars do we see directly? Thus, if you think like this, it is not something you can easily grasp. Therefore, you should know about the Karma connected to these twenty-seven stars. Reaching up to that Karma, experiencing and learning it as gross, subtle, causal, and effective, is our human Dharma. Realizing that man is a symbol who becomes a Deva, a Rishi, a Sanyasi, a Jnani, and thus a prophet and everything else, respecting that greatness and trying to learn it is the truth called Darshana. This is Darshana. Not the Darshana written down by someone based on their whims. Therefore, in such a Darshana, one must recognize whether the subtle course of Karma seeks merit or involves deceit and betrayal leading to danger. Having realized this, it must be explained to you. This is its essence. Therefore, only after saying that much and seeing that much can one become a Guru. Otherwise, one cannot. He is not a Guru. He is neither the seed nor the flesh of a fruit. He is nothing. Therefore, if you believe that the evolutionary nature of life capable of grasping such greatness resides in each of you, I too have the interest to inquire, to know, and to make known. You also have the right to inquire into what I should do. Inquire and find that out. This is its aspect. You should not reach that Karma which destroys you by preaching non-existent things in the name of Vedanta, leading up to 'Swaha'. That would be swallowing the axe of utter foolishness. It is destruction. Do not do so. I can say this with absolute certainty. What is it, it is not acceptable to say that I am lying. There might be someone traveling on the same path as mine. Similarly, there must be someone who has experienced through me. Otherwise, there is no need for any of us to boast by talking about other things.

[GV4:P1246] Therefore, we should know about the Karma that is told to us by turning back after reaching up to the Lord of the Ganas. This is the subject. So, understanding this subject, we should impart it to our children only in this manner. We cannot attain this merely by studying the Shastras. You must also believe the truth that both men and women can achieve this. There is no point in making you believe by saying things that do not exist. Nor is there any point in stating something you cannot discover. It is not so. In our human Dharma, we who are born at the beginning of this Kali yuga are fully entitled to it. That is Kali. Stirring and clearing the rights and wrongs that have occurred to date—that is the Guru. By stirring and clearing it, showing 'Look, there is such a mistake here.' This is being taught. It does not matter whether one is male or female, young or old. There is no point in boasting about caste and religion for that. There is nothing in it other than the pure manifestation of a blunder. It will be like the Dharma of an unbeliever. He cannot attain it. Therefore, if we have any personality that tries to learn by saying it does not exist, reveling in a personality that does not tell the truth to us or to its own life, in the act of destroying a poor brainless donkey, then in each such Dharma, we are entirely discovering a truth of humanity. We gain nothing by saying that this man is bad, or that he is somewhat good. We must only have the fortune to achieve this. In such fortune, we are seeking a course of Karma that each of us can take with absolute humility. We must be able to do this. This must be achieved while remaining a human being. Otherwise, there is no point in talking big about a Karma attained in the afterlife; God has given us the knowledge to grasp it in the light of a truth that can be known and attained by us while we are still alive. We must not fall short in that knowledge which we share as individuals. That is the intent of the greatness we have spoken, heard, and known with each other to this day. If we cannot manage to grasp this, we can do nothing except talk about something. You must realize that this is a truth achievable by human beings. Therefore, it should be known in the aforementioned manner. That is known. We will all reach the realm of such knowledge at some point or another. Because it is achieved only in accordance with our evolution of knowledge. We cannot attain it by doing anything else. Thus, the evolution of that knowledge reaches a point beyond thought, and sees the reality that transcends thought, regarding the evolution of life. Witnessing such reality, what we see is the glory of the form of light where the humility of love and respect is imparted. Whoever shows us the Karma that imparts to us the intent of that greatness which teaches the sense of Dharma to discover it, that is the Guru. There is no point in making any other justifications. Therefore, this must become a matter of your interest. It does not have to happen immediately. But it can happen. You should not think that each of you was born yesterday and grew up today. Consider that you are as old as the vastness of this world. Only when you see your life across such a distance can you discover the evolutionary course of that life. Any greatness that takes the Dharma residing in the course of Karma, which exists both subtly and grossly, and imparts it to you—that is the accessible Guru. Having learned thus, may you gain the familiarity to respect and absorb it. This is what I have to say.

[GV4:P1247] Guruvani

[GV4:P1248] Janmadinapoojithasamarpana Edition 2005

[GV4:P1249] The aspect of Darshana which is the Dharma ritually obtained for the Karma ordained by God

[GV4:P1250] We were talking about the Swami who came from Bihar. He would feel like he was seeing gods and goddesses. He has been seeing this for a long time. Just three days after coming here, it started becoming clear. Once it became clear, he started seeing words and the places he had visited. This is for you to understand. Why did it become clear when he came here? You should understand that too. Many among those standing here have seen this. But there is a plight where you cannot understand it, which the Vaishya and Shudra have. What is that? They were turned into a group dedicated only to agriculture and trade. Later, those who made tools on this earth were set aside into the category of carpenters, brass-smiths, blacksmiths, and goldsmiths. They were also given separate gods. We have been defeated in this divine system that has evolved over a long time. It is when we look at what happened to us because of this that we understand the extent of the blunder we made. But how can we understand that? We certainly cannot. An example of this is the Trinity system mentioned to you, that is, Shaktheyam, Shaivam, Vaishnavam, or Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva—whatever you call itٹ In this, isn't Shaktheyam included? So, even if we study these four Vedas and six Shastras, we do not understand its nature at all. We also do not know why we cannot understand it. After that, many visionaries, saints, or apostles came like this, and we now hear the story of two people who came as visionaries like the many Thangals. But there is no way to say they are visionaries. Why? When looking at their history, what we see in the history that goes beyond two thousand years is different. They brought it as the Old Testament or New Testament, and Islam evolved from that. There is some truth in that Islam. But even though this truth arrived, our own people, unable to accept or respect it, converted and became Muslims, Jains, Buddhists, and Christians. After this happened, what should they do? When they changed over, they separated from us again and started fighting. They stand apart and fight over whose god is greater. Nothing else is needed. Now, Rama's story is a matter that happened about seventeen lakh years ago. You might think it happened yesterday or the day before. No. If the story of Rama is this long, where will we go in the timeline of its ancestors and the religion and religious philosophy that operated within its thought process? We don't know this either. So, a culture of India that raised us in a way where we do not know such a side has drifted away in a completely inadequate manner. It has gone far away from us.

[GV4:P1251] Our girls should not listen to the Vedas. Or they should not study the Vedas. Or they are not allowed to handle them in a good manner . It is from this mother that we get children. We raise them as little ones, and when they grow up a bit, we get them married off. What do we get from this? If needed, they turn around, go there, and along with their children and their family, there will be fights, quarrels, and disputes with the brother in this house . They say this has been happening since the time of Sree Krishna. In truth, it is not like that . It has existed for so much time before that. We don't even know this . There is a reason for it to exist since the time of Sree Krishna. Because Tretayuga and Dwapara are not capable of anyone doing anything , it is a time that is meant only for those Acharyas (teachers) . After that, when coming again to the side of Kali, it is the Dharma of Kali. If there are any mistakes in the past Tretayuga , Dwapara, and Satyayuga , completely and utterly resolving them and showing the way to go to Satyayuga from now on is the story called Yugadharma. None of us know this . Among us, we have perceived it as just a sight or an offering. Or we have a course of action imagining that if a god or goddess comes, everything is settled . It cannot be anything other than that . You are people who came believing like that. I am also someone who came like that . A complete ignorance has happened to us in this. What is that? A plight where there is no one to explain what Yugadharma is . Caught in that ignorance , all of us--these four groups have gone astray. Suppose our children learn one of the languages as much as possible now. In our native language, they wouldn't even call their father and mother by name . What to do? Is this father and mother, or Appan and Amma--is this good--or is calling them informally and disrespectfully good? They won't speak . To father Da ٹ dy, Da ٹ .d y--see! So this not only makes our children not call out in our language , but also , this child can only develop a completely strange curiosity. After imparting this tendency , if they get a degree or go for a job through some education, it has become a trend where it is enough to come and see the father and mother for one or two days a year . Then after that, if the job is outside, rarely they and their kids would come taking turns, and in about ten years it will fade away and end. Then they wouldn't have the need to come here . Or if they come, they will adopt the ways over there--to drop them somewhere and go. Like that, many people have come here and asked me. That's why I am saying, children please listen, when they grow old, you should take them somewhere and dump them, okay. Did you hear what was said? They have found a language for that. Shall I say that? Vayojana Kendram (Old age home) ! Just take them there and leave them. So in this way we became bad; pushing our children into that is the language the father and mother teach--Daddy, Mummy. So if this complete theory is what you are bringing about, you are unfit to be called father and mother, or neighbors . What is it? Such a good language . Like in India , giving such a high position to father and mother, such a destiny of karma hasn't happened anywhere else.

[GV4:P1252] Today, there is a great conflict among siblings and among others! The reason for all this is that when we were neither taught, nor did we study, nor did we understand what the aforementioned system of the Chaturyuga entails, we became ready today to imitate whatever foreign countries exhibit, to the extent that it has no connection to our own lives. By making our children adopt all these guises exhibited by foreign countries, the child grows up devoid of any affinity for their native land, leading to the greatest ruin through education; and then, once they reach college, there is another "good thing". What is it? I do not even know how to express it in their language. I will say what I have heard from you—ragging. What, isn't it good? So, this is what we educate and send our little ones for. After studying like this, what will these children do? Where will they end up? With whom do they have a connection? With whom will you connect them? Whenever you try to hand over any kind of administrative discipline to them, they will turn into governing machines looking up to some other country. It is a process of learning by looking somewhere else, in such a way that we cannot derive any action from them that is rooted in the inherent nature of this country. Today, even computers have arrived. In this scientific system, what is the point in taking another's language, attire, knowledge, and commerce into our hands and then claiming that we are not accepting them? Therefore, this does not mean that what was invented somewhere in this country is either unwanted or wanted. India had methods that discovered things far beyond all these. What is that? We have heard it before. The guru of Bharadwaja, who invented what is called the Pushpaka Vimana during the time of Sri Rama, said, "This is not needed." Why? Saying that it is not suitable for the present times. But what you have heard about this is completely an alien version. Why? When the guru told this to Bharadwaja, he felt, "He is saying this so that I do not get it executed." That is why he went to the land of Kubera, explained it to the king there, had it built, and returned here. We must see whether the guru's initial warning that it would cause destruction came true. Coming here, he abducted the wife of the king here. Isn't that the nature of conflict? Have you ever thought like that until now? But then, because they did not deviate from the truth, even though she was taken away, she was not destroyed. She was recovered. No matter what we get, it is of no use to us. Our people went and discovered it. Such an aircraft was transformed into so many types, and today there are numerous varieties of it. So, if we shoot it with a machine gun, the glass will not break if hit. That is its strength. So, we have not yet started inventing anything like that. We assume that everything has already been accomplished here, or that we previously had none of these in our hands. That is not correct. We had all these in our hands. Because our ignorance manifested inherently in this manner, someone from here took it outside in a way that could destroy our country, and it went into the world, falling into the hands of the British or the Germans, and changed in many ways. Today, America has become its owner and is making us tremble. You must understand this. You are sending your children along this path to wherever the mother is seated and the father is seated. Where is the father seated? In Russia, isn't it? Isn't the "Comrade" coming as the father? Isn't he the one cooperating with us? Then, would it suffice to call him anything other than "Comrade"? Are not the mother and father cooperating with us? So, how ugly is the misfortune of India, which is prepared to call and teach the little ones in this state! Therefore, apart from the fact that we have been suppressed and confined within a specific religious framework where everything is bound up in the Trimurti system, having brought upon ourselves such karma, introducing our children in a way that is useless to this land and country, turning them into progeny devoid of rightful duty, and causing confusion in the order of worship, what have we gained? These might be the words you are hearing for the first time. But as long as you do not understand that this is applicable to you, to me, and to wherever the world exists hereafter, to whom will you say this? How will you explain this to your children? After understanding it in this manner, I had to take my time. I was also someone who firmly believed in your logic. What is it? In the Trimurti system. The proposition of our epics and Puranas is that if all the gods appear, or even if just one god appears, it is sufficient. But there are many among us who have seen various deities. However, they have not gained anything so far.

[GV4:P1253] Haven't you seen a lot? And what came of it? You might think this is a lie. If you look in here, you can find around twenty-five such instances. Among those who have come here, there must be at least ten. Try asking them. But just because we have seen all this, it means nothing to us. That is why it was narrated like a story of the Bihar Swami. After he came here, on the third day, it became clear, and then it started showing in various ways. Finally, unable to stand it, there was great distress. Then I had told him, you will feel distressed when you see this. But the fact is that this is wrong. This will become clear. If it becomes clear, you do what is necessary. But once it became clear, unable to stand or sit, he was constantly filled with joy and kept jumping around. Unable to stand still on the ground, he was shivering with the joy of seeing all this. After a while, he would start crying in the same manner. He would start laughing in the same manner. He displayed many such things here. He is here. So, what have they convinced us by saying all this? That through the manifestation of a single deity, everything will be accomplished for us. Haven't we come to the point where we can see that whatever you have worshiped in that manner, all of it comes and even bows down to the Guru? Even then, it went wrong. What we need to understand is that we cannot say there is no flawed karma that occurred to us in some era. There is. How to change what is there, how we should lead our lives after changing it, what all will come in that life, what hardships and losses will occur. We should never take our own intellect and use it in that. Such an intellect should not arise. I will not allow you to bring in anything excessively under the assumption that everything will come to you now. That is how I am being careful. I have not convinced you of anything by talking and made you do it. Have I? I will not do it. For us, it is purely a time destined by God. That is what you must understand. What is it? His task is for the Vaishya and the Shudra to rise, and by pulling along the Brahmana and the Kshatriya, take them to where they need to reach. Our philosophical perspective is a dharma derived as a custom for this duty.

[GV4:P1255] January 2006

[GV4:P1256] Whether it is Hinduism or any other religion, we possess a traditional knowledge that we have worshipped and followed until today. Therefore, whether this knowledge is right or wrong, it is something we have continuously been repeating. We cannot attain a clear, confirmed understanding regarding this knowledge. Because the flaw lies in our own hands. What is it? A competitive spirit among the Shaiva, Shakta, and Vaishnava sects. Everyone holds a competitive spirit without even knowing what a Shaiva, a Shakta, or a Vaishnava truly is. Similarly, this exists in all religious doctrines. However, such an extensively varying doctrine as found among Hindus has never been seen elsewhere. This is not because none of us have thought about the reason for it. We have thought about it; we have thought about it many times. But we have not attained it as true knowledge. I realized that it hasn't been attained based on my own experience. We have heard things like this. "Isn't a single glimpse of the Lord enough? It is everything"—there is still no shortage of such teachings among us. But no matter who learns or teaches in this way, no god or goddess is capable of sufficiently giving us anything. Nowadays, it is not a big deal for you to become a god or a goddess too. Each of you can become one. But when moving in that direction, one must understand one thing. The course and tribulations of this life cannot be resolved by these gods and goddesses. Similarly, there is the mention of Rishis (sages). This Rishi exists both beneath the god and above the god. But those who are above never obeyed the god during the era of the gods. We do not know this fact either. There is also a reason why they do not obey the god. These three sects compete and say - 'We are the greatest, our god is the greatest?' - The people within these groups themselves became divided into lower castes and higher castes, and thus assigned a different god for each caste, keeping a lesser god for a lower caste. Then whose god is the greatest? This is a question we must ask ourselves. Apart from this, there is something we remain without obeying and without knowing today. We have assumed that it is the Sanyasis (ascetics) and someone else who should be handling this. Beyond that, we have materialistic thoughts. We also convince ourselves that this is all we need. Leaving aside the fact that this happens due to our ignorance, ask those who say this: does one emerge as a Sanyasi, a Brahmachari, or a good Vanaprastha from family life? Or do they come from Sanyasa itself? What do you think about it? Since you completely fail to understand that all these arise from family life, you have merely assumed what you heard from someone else. This is not the case; truly, it is through people leading a family life that children beneficial to this land, home, and country are born. Whatever our past visionaries have done for us, if there are any remaining shortcomings in their deeds, such visionaries must explain to us the ultimate truth contained within the doctrine.

[GV4:P1257] So, because we do not know who such seers are, we make many mistakes. Thus, seers will not come in all eras. In this yuga, if we speak of the dharma of another yuga, it will not work. At the beginning of this yuga, Sri Krishna's clan was given royal status. So, at the very place where it was stated that there is no Shudra rule or Veda recitation, they were given ruling authority right at the beginning. That is Kamsa. So, this authority of Kamsa could not be fully understood by him with an attitude of dedication. What is this attitude of dedication? Be it a god, a goddess, a guru, or God, one should handle it only with dedication. However, as far as he was concerned, he did no wrong. What we have heard is about the wicked Kamsa. No. A wicked person cannot hear a divine voice from the sky (Ashariri). He is not wicked. We could not understand this either. How can a wicked person hear an Ashariri? He might receive something from some demon or deity. But because he had the dedication of this manifestation in his mind, a mistake happened. The god and goddess who are seen manifested will bless everything as much as possible. My god blessed me, my god, my goddess ڊ there are millions of people who say this. Each of these people says this believing they are great in their own way. They do not say it thinking it is bad. If so many people speak about this religion, caste, or class in different ways, is God something to be shared among each of them like this? Let us ask ourselves, is such a God supposed to do good for us? We have no question about this either. Then, if someone says something logically, they speak the truth in their minds as well, and go into an action that destroys broad-mindedness. What is it? Rationalism, liberationism - there are only two arguments. But by constantly arguing like this, they will end up paralyzed in their final days. Other than this, what can they gain through arguments? What do they know? What do you know about predestination? Nothing. What has become God's will? Without any such knowledge, as far as we are concerned, apart from making up God by forcefully grasping, we absolutely do not know any karma that imparts goodness from it. The reason for that is we have been taught that the dharma of Kali is very bad. Kali is never bad. If we are among those who believe this, this is what is generally said. Now, if a boy at home commits a mistake, they say, 'Isn't that Kali?' Whether it's a girl or a boy. So what is the fault with Kali? That is not known either. What is it? If there is a yuga dharma set apart for these 4 yugas, we hear a saying that in Satya Yuga we are all the same. Let it be whatever. In Treta Yuga, the worship system changed like this, and it became a bit stronger in Dvapara Yuga, and Satya Yuga is the same for all of us. The dharma of this Kali is to churn and straighten out if any mistakes have occurred in these 3 yugas.

[GV4:P1260] After your time in this world is over, what thoughts can each of you possibly have? Or what can you pass on to your children? If you have a grandchild in your home, what will you—as a father and mother—tell them? You try to show them God by telling tales of miraculous creations. Is God someone who performs miracles? Tell me if any of you hold such a belief. Are these miracles God itself? These are nothing but some ignorant notions that have clouded the human intellect. As far as we are concerned, regarding human beings—when we say humans, do not segregate them by caste, religion, or class—everyone is equally human. Then what is it? There are disparities. Everyone, whether fortunate or unfortunate, has made their efforts. And that effort is right. What is meant by that 'right'? It is the Chaturvarnya—Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra—according to the Yuga Dharma. We all think that caste originated from this established system of Chaturvarnya. Do not assume so. That history is untrue. The nature of Chaturvarnya merely defines the Dharma of each Yuga. Therefore, out of our ignorance, each person interpreted it in their own different way, resulting in a mistake that came into being.

[GV4:P1261] For us to correct this mistake, it has been billions of years - not just one or two. ٹ What is it? Isn't it what you are learning and teaching now? Not two thousand, four thousand, five thousand, or at most not going beyond ten thousand, you are stating a historical truth. Is this all there is to the origin of this world? So many billions of years ago - now, this Kali Yuga itself, as far as we are concerned, how long is it said to be? It is said to be four hundred and thirty-two thousand years. This four hundred and thirty-two thousand years, only the Kali Yuga that came after Sri Krishna is here. So we don't even know about Sri Krishna. What is it? Such a great a person! But what did we turn him into? For one group of people, he is the author of the Gita; for another group, he is the one who stole the clothes of the Gopis; for another group, he is a true womanizer. What all this womanizer has done, we don't even have the knowledge to see, do not forget the truth of that. But none of this is Sri Krishna's deed that we must believe. Why? These sixteen thousand and eight families, when they were in jail, if he gave them a vision there, you have not observed what it means. These sixteen thousand and eight families, and the later generation of the poet who created it came, then it just became sixteen thousand and eight wives. What a negative deed this is! How can you accept this? At least something that aligns with logic a thing shouldn't be said! So, going after the poet's imagination, abandoning dharma and dancing like an oracle, on top of that knowledge, one is seeing God. How will you see this? In what way will you see God? Then you didn't feel a thing. When talking about this Shudra class, in our homes, there are Shudras, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and thus all the Chandalas gathered together people as well. There is a story told here about that. I don't know if you know it. I don't know if the people of this land know it. When Narayana Guru came here, a big rich man here said, it seems: caste and all will change. Okay. Saying this, he said a Chandala resides in you. This man immediately went and the Chandala who lived in his compound was pulled out and removed, it is said. I don't know if you have heard this. So he didn't understand it at all. Our ancestors and those revolving in the sphere of influence of rich people are like this. What are they passing on to us? But a householder shouldn't be like that.

[GV4:P1262] In reality, what constitutes the knowledge of a householder (*Grihasthashrami*)? Their true knowledge lies in preserving their educated intellect without letting it degrade, while possessing children, a spouse, wealth, and authority capable of serving this land, home, and nation. Instead of this, what is currently happening? Everyone is solely focused on becoming highly educated. More specifically, God has bestowed a particular blessing upon you. The very first college in Kerala was established here (Kannur). However, what was the outcome of this college's blessing? You simply became like a westward-looking machine. Whatever occurs there, you indiscriminately gather and bring here. Merely observing and accumulating from the West has become your primary task. As a consequence of such accumulation, what have the North Indians done now? They have reduced the South Indian to the status of a monkey. Consequently, they consider themselves perfectly beautiful and superior in every way, while depicting us as monkeys. Furthermore, they did another thing. They proclaimed that the Vaishnava tradition is supreme. And what of the Shaiva tradition? They designated that as Dakshinamurthy. What are we to understand from this? Shiva is considered a guru of the people of these southern regions, encompassing these four states. By labeling him as Dakshinamurthy and composing texts like the *Dakshinamurthy Stotram* to convince us, they made us fall for this narrative. What did they do next? Along with that, they introduced Shaivism. And alongside this Shaivism, they brought in Shaktism. By continuously associating and combining these concepts, what did this amalgamation result in? It resulted in a state where we gained absolutely no true knowledge. It is a fact that we fell into this trap, whether knowingly or unknowingly. Therefore, even if someone approaches us to explain the truth, we remain incapable of understanding. There is a prevailing belief that devotion to God is exclusively for ascetics (*sanyasis*), and that householders have absolutely no need for it. But what happens if your child or a loved one faces adversity? Or if some form of ruin befalls them? At that moment, they call out to a God. Which God is that? Ultimately, it is the mother—representing nature in accordance with this Shakteya and Shaiva knowledge—who cries out, "My God, please let nothing bad happen." Thus, they pray that nothing untoward happens to the children who are about to be delivered after completing the ten-month gestation period following the menstrual cycle. Consequently, they desire neither the good nor the bad. Our mothers constitute a large community speaking from such profound ignorance. Why have our mothers become this way? Or consider our fathers, who travel elsewhere to work, struggling immensely to support their children, wives, and others—though this might be slightly less prevalent in these parts, it still exists here. If you visit South Travancore, they refer to it in two ways. One is stating that the 'elder is arriving' (*Mooppil varunnu*). The other is 'Father Comrade' (*Achan Sakhavu*). They use these material terms. In this context, there is another group: the materialists (*padartha visheshakkar*). They are the ones who blindly consume concepts of logic and liberation.

[GV4:P1265] Therefore, apart from the consequence of having wayward children through these various paths, what else have we achieved? Furthermore, this is not a recent phenomenon. You might assume this began yesterday or the day before. No. This is a profound distortion that has been occurring for eons. The root cause is our profound ignorance regarding the path of action established by Manu and his lineage. Even now, there is a path of action that we acknowledge. It manifests as Hindus following the Trinity (*Trimurti*) system, others adhering to the prophetic system, and the presence of isolated spiritual teachers referred to as gurus or the practice of various yogic disciplines.

[GV4:P1268] April 2006

[GV4:P1269] This must originate from these householders. However, you have completely uprooted and discarded this, adopting instead a traditional knowledge scavenged by someone else—a knowledge which, collectively, does not extend beyond ten thousand years. How can you reconcile this knowledge with the aforementioned calculations? While the temporal span of Kali Yuga is stated to be four hundred and thirty-two thousand years, this knowledge is merely five thousand two hundred years old. Presently, our understanding of Kali is such that we expect it to end tomorrow. How can it end? If we are born in this Kali, and if it is assumed that all born within it are inherently worthless, then who is left to inherit this legacy? The truth is contrary to this. The opportunity to be born in Kali Yuga is significant for you. Why? We are born into a specific state of Kali that possesses a momentum suited to these times and the inherent dharma to learn, act, and practice accordingly. We have been entrusted with the task of aligning this specific state of Kali with dharma. This applies universally, irrespective of religion, caste, or class. Consequently, we remain unaware of the inherent virtues of this Kali. Therefore, regardless of religion or caste, one must reflect upon this. Kali represents the authoritative force of a karma that identifies the errors of the past and present, purifying them into truth. What can we achieve through a dharma that diminishes such a Kali, claiming absolute ignorance? Consequently, we failed to facilitate the transmission of this wisdom to our children or the youth in any manner. What, then, is currently being demonstrated? Imparting religious dogma and fostering mutual conflict through it. What is the purpose of this? To which deity is this being offered? No one reflects upon this. What can we achieve by engaging in such aggressive actions? Wherein lies the error that afflicts our children and ourselves today? If our ancestors or others engaged in action, what have we transformed that dharma into? What have we attained within that dharma? Even this remains unknown. Consequently, due to such ignorance, gods, goddesses, and even malevolent entities have been elevated to the status of the Supreme, and oblivious to the wheel of time, each of us children—the root cause being the parents' inability to impart wisdom to their offspring. There might not have been parents who endured hardships purely for the betterment of their children. Even if there were, let that be. But upon observing that this is how they have struggled to cultivate this lineage, what benefit is derived from it for themselves, this land, or this household? What is it that we believe in?

[GV4:P1270] It is not that one should deny the existence of prophetic religions. They do exist. What we must analyze is the underlying reason for their emergence. Rather than asserting that one event caused another in a circular fashion, we must ask: why did they emerge? The dharma of the Hindu was irrevocably packaged and marginalized, and as a consequence of adopting transgressive practices, mutual conflict ensued. The individual could not approach the Supreme Deity; their only recourse was to approach lesser deities. What, then, could they do? It is a fact that they gravitated towards a space where they found liberty. It is necessary to do so. Had they not, they would have been denied liberty, education, wealth, and authority. Consequently, the only karmic trajectory present within India is one that has deviated due to the deprivation of these fundamental elements. However, if anyone presumes that isolating oneself and engaging in conflict will rectify this, let them attempt it. Otherwise, whether one resides within India or any other nation, it is inhabited solely by human beings. God has not descended to physically reside there. Therefore, whatever human beings require, they will require regardless of location; we can only exist in harmony with nature. It is impossible to impart dharma to individuals who live as spouses and children acting devoid of rational discernment, failing to comprehend or transmit dharma, and unable to reclaim the inherent goodness of nature. When one or two generations pass in this manner, these children will remain ignorant of the profound concept of liberty. Their understanding of liberty is merely what they arbitrarily perceive it to be. This is the genesis of our rationalism and liberationism. If we accept the truth that none of these ideologies will reform us, what is the remedy? How do we define those we term visionaries? A visionary spanning two, three, or five millennia will prophesy only up to their respective epoch. From that point, to elevate it, refine it, and rectify historical errors, the succeeding generation must possess requisite knowledge. Otherwise, it resembles a tree germinated from a decaying stump. Such a tree possesses another characteristic: it will topple in a strong gale. Similarly, devoid of true knowledge, we are merely running along the karmic assumption that science will unilaterally progress. This is incorrect. I am sharing my empirical experience with you. I have not adopted the logic or impulsiveness of anyone else. Given the opportunity to be born designated as a Hindu, I once presumed that adhering to Hindu behavioral norms would be beneficial. There were times I harbored such assumptions. What does this entail? What our mothers instill in us is: 'Children, God will strike you down.' Can one then escape the fear of a wrathful deity? Fear is inevitable. As one matures, the concept of God morphs into something subjected to trials and observations, eventually leading to the conclusion that none of this represents God. Consequently, the subsequent iteration of God is merely the residue of frantic, oracle-like possessions and utterances. When such a concept is carried forward over ages under the guise of faith, love, and reverence, it becomes an entity unfit for true belief. Subsequently, under the mere pretexts of rationalism and liberationism, one is presented with a deity tailored to their intellect, and one ultimately becomes lost within it. Thus, every stage of human existence, male and female, is being misdirected in this manner. Within this karmic progression, originating from the householder stage, you categorize and invoke individuals by various titles such as yogi, karmi, jnani, bhakta, fakir, saint, or apostle.

[GV4:P1272] May 2006

[GV4:P1273] It is situated slightly below the Padmanabhapuram Palace, towards the northern side. Have you heard of Peerukannu Sahib? You certainly would know of him. Are you familiar with Thuckalay? Do you know the Thuckalay Mosque? Are you aware that a multitude of people visit this mosque? You must comprehend it in this context. The individual known as Peerukannu Sahib was an eminent scholar. He even authored a treatise on Vedanta in the Tamil language. His guru was Kattuva Sahib. One must be cognizant of all these historical details. It was there that this guru attained *Samadhi*. It was impossible to transport his physical remains back. To do so, one would have had to traverse the distant mountains. Standing there, one can observe a fort-like structure near the Padmanabhapuram Palace. The site is located to the northeast of that structure. What he did there was gather stones of significant size and place them over the remains, ensuring that the body would not be exhumed or carried away by animals. Should you visit the site today, it is visible; stones are amassed to the height of a person. It spans lengthwise in its entirety. Presently, devotees visit the site to prepare gruel and perform *Annadanam* (the sacred offering of food). This practice occurs on most days. If you visit and observe the site, you can witness this firsthand.

[GV4:P1274] Did you realize that all of this is an entanglement encountered on the path of searching for God? In the place where this person called Kattuva Sahib is worshipped or venerated, inside the aforementioned mosque, there is a *Manjanathi* (Morinda coreia) tree. Isn't it called *Manjanathi*? Do you know? Only the people of South Travancore would know the term *Manjanathi*. He attained *Samadhi* (spiritual liberation) resting at the base of this tree. They have buried him there. The said *Manjanathi* tree stands there. There are stones on all four of its sides. If we go there before dusk, individuals will offer at least ten to sixteen bananas each. Some will bring jaggery. Some will bring salt. Some will bring black pepper. These are simply scattered around. This is what occurs. What is being narrated here is merely a fraction of what we have witnessed upon visiting various places in this manner. All of this constitutes a path taken in the quest for God. How will you attain this?

[GV4:P1275] Now, Beemapally is a place where a mother and son attained *Samadhi*. This is a narrative unfolding in a context where Islam dictates that graves should not be worshipped. Similarly, Hindus are people who install deities wherever an *Alstonia* (Pala) tree sprouts. What can be done? Should we believe whether this is a right or a wrong practice that has emerged from our antiquity, or should we not? It could be wrong. It could be right. Should we or shouldn't we? How can we possibly eradicate this right and wrong? How is it possible?

[GV4:P1276] Disciple: It becomes possible through a Guru.

[GV4:P1277] Guru: That is correct. Must we not find such a Guru? What are you saying? This concept of a Guru is not merely what we have been taught to recite. You will not comprehend it in that manner. Who do you assume all these aforementioned great souls are? What kind of renunciates do you assume they are? Even now, I strive to redirect everyone who comes here away from this, to the best of my abilities. When I say I am trying to redirect them, it is not merely about walking away pointlessly. One does not simply leave by declaring "it does not exist." There are specific detriments in it; you must eliminate them and then step away. Otherwise, they will entangle your children in this. This is what I have to tell you. If you need your children, you must change this. Is there any utility in my wandering the land delivering speeches, instead of stating this to you—to the mother, the children, and the father? It is my personal experience. Currently, there is such an awareness within you. If asked how that awareness arose, would you be able to articulate it? That is the phenomenon. In this state, ignorance befalls us. The question is whether we should recognize it or not. Is it acceptable to merely state that we are ignorant? We cannot possibly tell our children that we lack knowledge, can we? Would that suffice? Therefore, a systemic action has been executed to crush and bury us within this. Similarly, back then, regarding a condition that defied treatment by any doctor, it was instructed to apply holy ash in a specific manner, and it was done. If you do not understand this and act appropriately in the required context, there is no point in claiming you have visited here and there. You approached regarding each of these for a specific purpose. Do not assume that everything concludes with that. What currently exists within these children, what resides within us, what all we have to accomplish, and what we must do—if a clear comprehension of these matters does not solidify within you, what will you gain despite my performing all these actions? If you fail to understand this, what can I achieve after you come here and articulate a few things? Nothing can be accomplished. I am neither a sorcerer, nor a physician, nor an astrologer. I am a believer. I can share the experience of that. I can explain how you may attain it. What is your understanding of the term '*Grihasthashrami*' (householder)? You should only speak if you are a *Grihasthashrami*. Otherwise, you should not speak. For a '*Grihasthashrami*', there are five principal duties (*Dharmas*): *Pithru Dharma* (duty to ancestors), *Deva Dharma* (duty to deities), *Athma Dharma* (duty to the self), *Dana Dharma* (duty of charity), and *Jnana Dharma* (duty of knowledge). How does one become the rightful authority for all these five *Dharmas*? I am not a person who will ask questions like whether you arrived in a particular car when you went there. I know nothing about cars, nor do I know anything else. I am not discussing matters like whether you came in a white car or a black car, or if a chicken jumped in front of you when you reached a certain place. Have these five *Dharmas* been prescribed for you or not? How will you obey and adopt these five *Dharmas*? Nothing more than this is required to elicit anger towards you.

[GV4:P1278] A '*Grihadharmi*' (practitioner of household duties) must fulfill all these five *Dharmas*. What we require is a lineage possessing the functional capability to perform this, to cause it to be performed by us, and to sustain it. Consequently, do we not need to acquire such a distinction of functional capability? Merely acquiring it is insufficient. We must actively adopt it. We will pay any price for that. In that regard, there is no discrimination based on whether one is male or female, young or old. *Grihasthashrama* is the *Dharma* of aligning with one's respective role to facilitate taking, to actively take, to give, and to receive all of that. It is not merely for idle amusement. If it is said that such a *Grihasthashrami* is incapable of this, what can be done? I am stating this to you in brief.

[GV4:P1281] Our ancestors have already lived through these three epochs. What remains is the great illusion (*Mahamaya*) and the illusion of the Supreme Lord. Thus, confined within the protective veil of illusion, one is placed under the dominion of the Supreme Lord. What else should I tell you other than this? Is it not true? If brought under this Supreme Lord, is the time of the Lord not over? What is time? These three epochs. The *Satyayuga* has passed. It just went by like that. Then, according to the dharma that 'the universe will follow the course of genesis and karma', who are we by birth, who are we by action, who are we by merit, who are we by fortune, and what is the karma to be fulfilled? You yourselves must perform these five tasks. Entrusting them to just anyone will not suffice. You can entrust them; but only to one who is capable. Otherwise, it will result in ruin. Do you understand? 'This is *Gurudharma*'. There is no point in speaking of any other dharma. We must observe what became of our ancestors, our preceptors, or the incarnations who came as upholders of the epochal dharma, in their actions according to the *Yugadharma* that has passed through our many lifetimes. This is *Yugadharma*. This is what must be understood by holding onto the 'Guru of the transition of time' (*Kalantara Guru*). When there is a transition in time, one must know what all that entails. Every epoch has a transition. Likewise, the four-epoch cycle (*Chaturyuga*) has a transition. In this manner, seventy-one *Chaturyugas* have transitions. The preceptors who appear in each of those transitions are the true masters of this. You must witness it yourselves and attain it yourselves. Instead, what use is it to you if the 'Guru has seen it'? Therefore, this is why you attain discipleship; not merely for a commercial transaction. So, starting from demons, or as you often recite out of vanity now—what is it you say?—'Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha, and Vamana'; after these ten incarnations, how many incarnations have there been now? If you include Buddha and the rest, how many incarnations would that make? What is the use if so many incarnation-like beings came, and you and I just played along? This is not what I am saying. Whether it concerns you, me, or the world, without realizing the downfall caused by this singular error, we are fully suffering like a fish fallen into a stream. You must understand this. However many deities, goddesses, sages, ascetics, wise men, or devotees have passed in our lineage, we must liberate those who need liberation, protect and sustain those who need it, and they must ascend through our dharma in a manner befitting their karma. There might also be those among them who need to be reborn in our children. They too must do good for this world. This is not something that chases after anything else. It has not touched a single thing. It has not been involved in anything whatsoever. I am seeing this among the youth and among many others in your homes. By correcting this, it is being contributed to the world through you. If you do not understand this and act accordingly, my doing this will be like washing it down the river. You should only come here if you are prepared for this. Otherwise, there is no point in coming here. What you all have assumed is that when near death, or when all the nerves fail to straighten, one should go and lie in a wayside inn. Is that not what you have learned? But this is not that. Absolutely, for your age, and for any young age, look, even children of that age are experiencing this here. You should not assume that this is a mystical power (*siddhi*) or the continuation of something else. This is the first application. This is the divine resolve (*Brahmanischaya*). You should come and participate only if you have faith in this. Otherwise, I do not wish for you to come. I will never wish to summon you either. Then, having brought you to such an awareness, you will be instructed. That is a matter that satiates both your hunger and mine. It is meant to be consumed in such a way that one never hungers again. You should only consume it if you are willing. Then, try consuming it. We can consume it slowly. So, did you understand what was said? Sorcery, medicine, astrology, demonic possessions, and even the practices of an ascetic (*avadhuta*) were mentioned. It is not about telling other secrets. All of this has fallen within our experience.
