[GV4:P1284] The Perversion of Various Forms of Worship

[GV4:P1285] The manner in which you have perceived things is different. We have possessed this traditional knowledge. You are aware that we have incurred certain deficiencies because we have engaged in highly uncultured forms of worship, which have permeated every religion, caste, and class nature. Because it has been passed down traditionally in this manner, we have not been able to recognize it, nor have we been able to comprehend how this occurred or the reasons behind its occurrence. Not just one, two, or four, but numerous exalted souls have come and practiced this for that purpose. If we observe the arrivals since the beginning of this *Kaliyuga*, it is traditionally passed down that there have been two thousand four hundred and forty-four preceptors. Sree Krishna came merely to demonstrate initially what karma entails within these five thousand or five thousand two hundred years. However, we did not understand any of that either. The stories written and taught to us for that purpose, and what we learned, have all led us down an erroneous path. Then, the only way to say there is no error in it is through that familial lineage. What is it? There is a familial lineage called *Yadava*. It emerged within the *Shudra* class. Having originated in a lower stratum, that community still possesses a familial instinct in Northern India and here, surviving alongside cattle and their lineage. But we have not understood any of this. We have not contemplated why kingly status was bestowed upon this *Shudra* class and brought about in this manner. The reason is that these *Yugadharmas* manifested as a completion of the errors that have occurred over myriad ages. Thus, without fulfilling this *Yugadharma*, no one can accomplish anything else. So, if asked how to fulfill this *Yugadharma*, we do not know that either. The greatest blunder we have committed due to this is the massive doctrine of not knowing what we must do in each epoch. Why? The *Satyayuga* is described here as an epoch that speaks everything truthfully, without mentioning caste, religion, or class. Its actions were also the same. But when the *Tretayuga* arrived, we were not taught what the nature of that *Tretayuga* should be. Nor were we taught about the *Dvaparayuga*. The tradition of the karma that humanity initially demonstrated in this *Tretayuga* still exists to a small extent among us. What is that? Retreating to the forest. You have been led to believe that *Sannyasa* means going and residing somewhere in a forest. This is not *Sannyasa*, and we should not perceive it as such. Moreover, it is impossible to do so in accordance with the present times.

[GV4:P1286] The *Yugadharma* is being transformed. However, it is said that when this *Yugadharma* is transformed, a quarter of that epoch will be spent on this transformation itself. Therefore, we lack knowledge regarding this *Yugadharma*. Or, if there is any, it is all attributed to the Supreme Lord. There is no knowledge to articulate anything beyond that. Otherwise, it is the same in other religions as well. There is another religion that believes a group is born into the homes of lowly people and yet must arrive like kings. Thus, we did not even possess the conviction that manifestations from the Divine could appear as kings, as mendicants, or as the uncultured. What happened to us because of this? It is absolute ignorance that has been handed down.

[GV4:P1287] Sri Krishna is one of those who were born in various places to change this ignorance. Before the beginning of Kali, that is, out of the thought that if Kali started, things would go out of order, it was made so. But that too was not successful. Nothing that came later was successful either. Thus, such an ignorance of Dharma exists among all of us, among all human beings. Now, Jesus himself came. Moses came—none of them came to create a caste or a religion. No one understood this. So what happened? When life was lost halfway, our nature of worship became a killing tree (the cross). Whatever they were hanged on, that gallows began to be worshipped. At the same time, some place a cross. But nothing else is placed. In this way, it initially transformed into eighteen types, and now sixty-four churches exist. Then, speaking of its smaller and smaller factions, it is said that there are over two hundred. So, if this has happened to a religious doctrine that emerged in just four thousand years, what else could not happen? It is a lack of original knowledge that has afflicted us. This original knowledge is supposed to be obtained entirely from God. Then one might ask, weren't they all born from God, then why is this? Or you may ask if it is because of their fault. It did not happen because of their fault. As they grow up, it takes time just to understand them. When they are understood, it takes time to disobey them. They are obeyed only after their time. Then, everything seen, heard, spoken, and known will begin to be celebrated as a science. In this manner, no matter whose history you take, the knowledge we have acquired to this day is like this. So, when a man is alive, what is it, or what could we grasp from the karma that a man living like that relied on and desired? We don't know that either. Having gone into the depths of a profound knowledge where we have absolutely no discernment, all this turned into knowledge and began to be spoken through miraculous powers. Thus, in whatever manner a person was born, about that person, in a very clear manner, webs of siddhis and mantric arts came along, and apart from that, the path of tantra as well. When this changed into mantra, tantra, and yantra, we became ignorant of what was in practice at its beginning, what should come in its middle, what the dharma of that Yugadharma is at this end, or how another begins later. What can we impart to our children?

[GV4:P1288] Now, you are all family people. Each of us has a course of karma that enables us to grow in accordance with the family and live in accordance with the land. Can these children live in the world by knowing what danger has befallen this land, family, and country? Apart from living with us according to the prevailing dharma, they get nothing else. Then, some so-called historians write and fill up whatever they can. When all that is written and filled—we don't even have the time to study it. Then what will we study? Thus, what can each of us do when we don't have the time to learn and teach about the respective eras? We fought by speaking of caste, religion, and class, bringing ourselves to a karma where children do not live together, being ignorant of the Yugadharma; what can we do about the denial of God that occurred by not knowing and following it? Think for a moment, if God exists in different ways for each caste, how can you say there is one God? If God is two different things for you and me, then it is nothing special. We all have God. If this God resides in different ways, how can we unite? Similarly, acting contrary to His karma, that contrary karma was diverted for the caste. Thus, karma was created through caste. Caste was created through karma. Thus, things contrary to each other are done. However, there have been some changes now—within these five thousand years. How is it? Now, everyone learns carpentry. The government has ordered to teach it like that. Similarly, the priesthood. It has been made to appear that whatever jobs exist in this world can be done by anyone. Just like this, education can be for everyone. If we see that education can be for all people, it means they are attaining a karma to be independent. So, because we lacked education, the ignorance of calling upon God while speaking of caste and religion often occurred. Believing it to be a karmic capability to manifest God, even the serpent dance (sarppam thullal) that originated in ancient times has become impossible to discard from our hands today. After that, by worshipping various kalari deities and displaying ferocity in various forms of worship, it is said that one attains the manifested power. How will our children understand this tradition acquired through dance, special rituals, and karma? Furthermore, do we have the time to study what our mothers or fathers tell us, or by sifting through the rights and wrongs that have come into our Vedic system? Or if we study, can we grasp anything? Because all kinds of shortcomings had come upon us like this, it took a long time just to follow the Yugadharma. So, when this Yugadharma begins, it will be something else entirely. It is seen through calculations that Kali is the shortest of eras. It has four hundred and thirty-two thousand years. So, can we call upon God only after this Kali era ends? It is said that Kali will not affect us. How did Kali not affect us? It is not like that. Kali is indeed good for all of us. What has been told to us and what our ancestors have taught us to this day is that Kali means destruction, isn't it? If our children themselves act improperly, attributing it entirely to the faults of Kali and explaining our own faults and virtues is the extent of our knowledge to this day. How can we find fulfillment in this knowledge? How can we act by knowing at least the dharma meant for us? It is a karma that we cannot accomplish in any way. However, by bringing forth these great souls here and there, no matter how they come before you, you must at least respect that the people sent by God have come to do that. Otherwise, you won't be able to accept it. For example, we could not understand Sri Krishna, who was born such a wise person. It was covered up with stories, turned into the most corrupted stories, changed into stories and plays, and became Kathakali. How much can we achieve in the karma of showing and informing that depicting all the evils in the land is our current intelligence?

[GV4:P1289] When examining each of these instances, we realize how long God has been working for us! However, we have completely failed to understand this. You may all ask: if God is everything as claimed, why can He not just change everything in a single stroke? That is incorrect. Consider the vast expanses of time, even the very calculation of a 'Kalpa' that you have heard of. It speaks of the history of a Kalpa—whether remaining inactive for that entire duration or functioning throughout it—that has encompassed countless 'Chaturyugas' or countless 'Manvantaras'. Can we proceed on the right path merely by studying all this? We cannot. What, then, should we do? If a prophet suited to the times, a preceptor (Acharya), or any such great soul (Mahatma) arrives, how will we recognize this person? We are utterly incapable of knowing. This is the same across everyone's history. Our shortest measure of time is this Chaturyuga. How so? Because Kali Yuga has only just begun. How can we, who cannot even fully comprehend a span of merely three epochs, grasp the extensive history of this Chaturyuga? Since we lack information regarding any of this, we have merely been reading the records written and preserved by whoever established the calculations, wherever they did so. How, then, could these historians formulate such an extensive historical account? They cannot. That is precisely why, no matter how clearly they stretch or condense the narrative, it remains a story that does not extend beyond ten thousand years. This is evident even if we examine the knowledge we currently possess. There is no need to look at anyone else's accounts. Since the birth of Sri Krishna up to the present day, the great souls who have incarnated have attempted to reform us by speaking in the simplest of terms, through their births and by causing births. Yet, no one understood this. Nor does anyone know who this is. Having reached that state, we have all fallen and decayed into a course of action where no one respects anything; we have drained its vital essence and instead gathered worthless refuse. Consequently, we have become thoroughly corrupted. How can we rectify this? It can only be achieved if a great soul instructs you. No ordinary individual is capable of imparting this. No one can correct you, except for that specific individual who has been granted the absolute authority for these times.

[GV4:P1292] The Path of Dharma Transcending the Stream of Thought

[GV4:P1293] Today, if an incident occurs anywhere in our known world, alternative mediums have emerged to present it before us instantly as news. That is a process that has evolved up to television, taking the place of true knowledge. Thus, you see this before you today. We live in an era where we lack the means to think and comprehend what this is or why it occurs in this manner. It does not readily yield to such thought. If we enter the stream of thought, what can we achieve other than pondering over various histories? We can achieve nothing. Therefore, we possess a trajectory of Dharma that inquires whether there is anything beyond this stream of thought. However, no community or nation has been able to grasp it. The familiarity we have with it today is constructed by intertwining all issues in a manner that merely incites us to fight among ourselves. Today, we are actively choosing the very place where the fortress of destruction—built by playing and manipulating the state machinery—has grown the largest. Every one of us is like that. What can those historical scholars who make these choices convincingly teach us about our true reality? Let each of you reflect upon this. Hence, if we, who are born and raised on a wretched path that is incapable of making us think, incapable of independent thought, and incapable of absorbing us into any real knowledge, try to figure out what we should become, it will prove futile. There is no point in invoking rationalism or theories of liberation (Mukti) for this purpose. If one speaks of the theory of Mukti, it cannot simply be taught. It is Mukti itself that is arguing. How can that be done? One who is bound to Mukti will have no time to tell you. If you hold any such understanding, please state it. You are all educated individuals. I am asking the educated. I possess no formal education. Therefore, you have the right to speak. Please do so. Thus, in this condition, it is not something that can be attained through mere study. Regarding that, as I mentioned earlier, the first university originated in our land; we claimed everything in its name. Is this not how we are taught? Are we not studying a history that claims when its scraps of paper were gathered and set ablaze, it burned for three months? What, then, are educated people like you going to serve here? What will you place into the hands of these children? You cannot offer anything. No historian can. No historical scholar can. Where do we currently stand regarding the actions we must undertake? Reflect on that as well. If we proceed without understanding that, we have no authority to articulate any justice concerning ourselves, our nation, or any part of the world. Let it be an educated or an uneducated person. Can we work and accomplish this to witness it as a reality within our lifetime? Is it an individual matter? No. What is required now? You tell me. What is it that we, who are alive today, need? Is it sufficient to merely patch together the remaining fragments of those stories taught by our parents and pass them on to our children? If so, that is enough. In that case, since the parents have already spoken it, does anyone else have anything further to say? When parents speak, they can only address other worldly matters. Take the easy route. If you can accomplish something in this manner, then do it. Otherwise, there is no use in corrupting yourselves by repeating this story. You possess an awareness of Dharma, prompting you to ask whether this can be accomplished or not, and how it might be undertaken. How will you grasp this Dharma? I can only suggest a minor task for this. When I say 'minor task', I mean an easy task. It is not actually a small endeavor. None of you should approach it under the illusion that it is a small task. We, who have not even had the opportunity to hear and understand it, possess no capacity to distinguish between good and bad, or small and great. We can only boast meaninglessly by uttering such hollow words. Therefore, relying on historical truth, this is entirely impossible for us.

[GV4:P1296] The Field of Action Imparting Ideals in Accordance with the Yugadharma

[GV4:P1297] We have learned our contemporary history itself in such a way that we cannot understand it properly. If you are educated, you cannot speak such nonsense. This is 'nonsense', in a way, isn't it? What a deception it is on his part to say it is 'philo-rubbish' in front of you educated people? That is why I said, if we wander behind those historians, we will get nothing. Through history, you will not get a single word about the path where your contemporary human beings acted and failed, or where our ancestors failed entirely. Then what should be done? People who are your contemporaries must see, know, speak, and practice this, and guide you onto that path. There is no other justification for this. If anyone claims there is, it is contrary to the truth. It will not happen. Because, all the knowledge we have discovered so far has been taught to us by the sorcerers among us, to fight and win against foreigners, or to hand it over to them, take money, and make a living for ourselves. Who else is there? In this history that has been cast so far away, what will you pass into the hands of your children who stand ready to ask, know, learn, and teach who each of us is? So what you need to understand from this is this: Look at whether the great men born in the history after the beginning of this Kali Yuga experienced happiness or sorrow. Gandhiji is a great man who was born as a mere materialist. Gandhiji had no spiritualism. You should not assume otherwise. Why? The Congress people portray him here as a spiritualist, do they not?

[GV4:P1298] Disciple: The demands are not gaining traction.

[GV4:P1299] Guru: If it is not working out, why carry it around? If it has no value, can't it just be discarded? Now we can say that it is good. What would be said in those days? We have come a bit further along. Nothing of the sort has happened. We did not study that history either. We could not grasp the magnitude of that sacrifice. We could not walk in the path of dharma either. Nor did we attain the aspect of virtue. This is the truth. [GV4:P1354] The Truth to be Cultivated in the World

Having heard, known, and learned all these words, why do you begin like this again? So, to praise whom are you doing this? Therefore, you cannot proceed in this manner. What should be done then? We need a direct perception (*pratyaksham*) of it. First, that must be attained within the waking, dreaming, and deep sleep states. Do not merely narrate tales. Thus, in your lifetime, most of you will not be able to witness this. However, a few among you have come as qualified individuals. Why is that? If it remains in your experience during the waking, dreaming, and deep sleep states, there are certain individuals you will perceive during those times.

[GV4:P1356] Therefore, what is being taught to us is who Krishna is and what Krishna did. Similarly, we are being taught about the Trimurtis, which speak of the antecedent state. Thus, when it is said that the entity who plucked off Brahma's head is present here, what does that action compel us to think? Who plucked off Brahma's head? Why does this Subramanya worship the one who plucked off the head of his guru and god? Consequently, this four-faced deity—whose head was plucked off along with the heads of fathers, mothers, gurus, and ancestors—now has only three faces. It is said that the other head was plucked off. Now, if each of you were to get angry, how many of your fathers' and mothers' heads would be lost? There are people here who have concocted and served such stories. This is not what I have told you. Thus, you can perceive it in this manner. *Pratyakshavaham Dharmam* means witnessing it manifested right before us. It involves elevating and demonstrating what Krishna is, what a Guru is, what God is, what Shiva is, and what Brahma is. This is *Pratyakshavaha Dharmam*. It is not merely claiming, "I saw Jesus," "I saw Krishna," "I saw them," or "I saw these people." Rather, it must lead to a path of action that demonstrates what Subramanya, the one who plucked the head, and the one who did not pluck the head, do together. This is the true vision. We are not speaking of an action that is merely settled through pretentious talk and judged by karma. We must not practice such a dharma. God has given us a profound opportunity to fully accomplish this. This is what I am telling you. Therefore, it is said that we can attain knowledge in this state. How can one attain knowledge in this state?

[GV4:P1357] Many great souls among our aforementioned ancestors, who have known and spoken the truth, must come before us. Upon their arrival, they must explain the historical truth of this matter. You must ask the Guru whether it is true. Only thus can this be known. If you wish to know it in that manner, can you go into asceticism (*sannyasa*) now? In this state, there is a duty you can demonstrate to your children. Both men and women. Having discovered this, you must find out whether there are countless such children in our country, or if we are being fed lies. To know this, you tell grand tales, do you not? How so? 'Gold must be tested on a touchstone.' What does that mean? The grinding stone is just lying there, isn't it? Can't we just grind it on that? Then why search for a touchstone? Therefore, it will only be correct if we rub it on the kind of stone where its purity can be ascertained. Otherwise, one will just keep grinding it on the regular grinding stone forever, without ever knowing its true value. This is what you need to understand. I am saying this after seeing both men and women; this is not a task done for a single caste, a single religion, a single region, or a single country. Therefore, you must learn it through such individuals. After knowing it, you must desire to serve it through your own efforts and your own love. This is what I have to tell you. I handled it this way to avoid speaking at excessive length about this. Both men and women must be able to boldly state that this is the truth. No other justifications should be offered. Statements like, 'She is a woman, she won't attain it; he is a man, he won't attain it; he is a scoundrel, therefore he has no God,' cannot be accepted here. If the scoundrel, the drummer, the mahout, and the farmer are all children of God, they must attain it. So, if they are to be children of God, they must reflect on what that entails. That is its true aspect. I did not do this to tell you, 'You will not get it, but you will get it if you just jump around.' It should be viewed in this manner: *Jagrat* (waking), *Swapna* (dreaming), and *Sushupti* (deep sleep). First, let you perceive it this way. You must not deviate from history or abandon the truth. Then, just as you perceive in the waking state, you must perceive in the dream and deep sleep states, and similarly in *Turiya* (the fourth state of consciousness); only after seeing it there should you undertake the journey towards *Turiyatita* (the state beyond the fourth). You have been blessed with the fortune to come to that duty. You must reflect on what you need to do to reclaim this fortune. By thinking, knowing, and acting upon this, even if we lose everything, what can we do with the consciousness of truth? That is your resolve, that is your duty, that is the truth you uphold. It is to prepare you for this truth that I speak. If Jesus could be beaten like this, people will come to beat and kill you too. No one who runs away saying 'I don't want to die' needs to come. At least if you are terrified like that, you won't come, right? So, all those who were searching for this were subtly tricked. But we have unraveled this trick. You must understand this. Therefore, you must attain the subtle body of these past ancestors. In which realm of the atmosphere does this subtle body exist, and from which realm does it control you? What is the structure of that realm, what all happens there, and how can you be guided into the narrative of what occurs there? Your Guru is the one who explains this to you. Seek and find it, and inquire wherever you need to inquire. Similarly, may this knowledge come to your children, and may those children become everything for the country. It should not remain confined to your home. That is not good. If it stays confined to your home, when you finish consuming all that you have amassed, he will die, you will die, and I will die. Right? Therefore, we must move completely towards a dimension of knowledge. This is your fundamental need today. I have stated that there is no harm even if your properties, house, or other belongings are sold to fulfill this need. Why is that? It is the very same word spoken by Jesus: that a wealthy man cannot easily pass through this path. Does that mean throw away all your money? It doesn't just mean that it is a word spoken by Jesus. If you hold onto the arrogance of wealth, we will not be able to progress. You do need money. I didn't say you don't need money. You don't need to argue that there is no God just because someone wrote a story elaborating on it and left. It doesn't mean that this applies to the rich, the beggar, and all the great sinners who are labeled as poor. The one called poor has merely swallowed his condition of poverty. What will he do now? This is the state of the 'poor.' So, if you set out to reform all these poor people in the land, the matter won't succeed. Therefore, do not prepare to dress up these poor people in this manner and invite criticism! Do not proceed to that destructive act of creating a situation where these poor people become even greater sinners and are forced to stretch out their hands before you, thereby destroying them. They are being driven to the brink of destruction. This is not how you uplift the impoverished. First, let him acquire the knowledge to earn and sustain himself. What is it? How does one earn and eat? People should offer it when they see you. That is what is meant by earning and eating. Let's do one thing. Let's make a man walk through here without a single thread of clothing. What happens? Will he get clothes? Similarly, if I sit down to eat saying I am hungry and go around barging in everywhere, won't they give us food? So, none of that is sufficient. Upon seeing you, clothing, wealth, capability, love, respect, and humility must all emanate through you; this must reach the country, and the children meant to implement this *dharma* must be creatively entrusted into your hands.

[GV4:P1360] Introduction to the Ashram and its Administration

[GV4:P1361] There is a certain conceptual knowledge we have held onto regarding the antiquity of the ashram. We do not know how that understanding of the ashram came to us. When we hear the word 'ashram', we solely assume it to be a place designated for asceticism (*sannyasa*). That is not the case. However, because we do not think in that direction, there is another complication as well. History states that children were taken to Kanva, Sandipani, and others to study there. For what purpose? Were they taken there to become ascetics? It is recorded that even Sri Krishna lived in the ashram of Sage Sandipani. For what purpose? Was he taken there to become an ascetic? There are even those among you who believe that one must not go to an ashram. And furthermore, women are strictly not allowed to enter an ashram. This is a certain perception you hold. Why did this ignorance take root in you? You do not reflect upon that. You failed to understand that this is merely the remnant of a historical practice that traditionally forbade you from possessing education, wealth, and authority—even forbidding you from wearing proper clothes or learning the alphabet. Consequently, what happened? Those who taught history taught it in this distorted manner. They taught that a *sannyasi* is someone who sits silently somewhere, doesn't even require food, or if they consume anything at all, it's merely raw water or a leaf. You acquired knowledge in this flawed state. Is there any historical truth in this? You haven't even investigated whether there is any validity to it or not. You lack the foundational knowledge to investigate in that direction. Because of this lack of knowledge, what have you become? Today's Brahmin is the one who possesses any knowledge about it. Even among them, it has not been properly investigated why one goes to an ashram like this. Thus, both the Brahmin and the Chandala end up standing in the exact same state of ignorance. What is to be done?

[GV4:P1362] It is said that for this system to be good, there must be the blessing of a Sadhu (sage). What is this Sadhu? You don't know that either. So, it is to improve the system and to learn about life that one is placed in this ashram. Not that it became a place for asceticism and the children were just dumped there--the ignorant injustice of saying such things still resides within you. What to do? What happened to you because of that? Whatever is done for you, you have no realization. You are unable to regain that knowledge. You, who have spoken and learned here so many times, were told a word that those who perform Gurupooja here must be careful. That is not just a single word. It was an obligation meant to be maintained until the end. But because you don't know this, you do not have the heartfelt determination to respect and understand it. What is the reason for that? You have been taught that after existing as this god and goddess, all souls are sitting under this god. What is the point of sitting under that god? You don't know that either. The reason is that none of you have paid attention to the knowledge called Manvantara. You don't know how long a Manvantara is, or how many Chaturyugas make up a Manvantara. So, we have swallowed a lot of such ignorance together. We cannot do anything about this. No matter how much is told to you, it doesn't enter your head. I see five or six new faces among you. I am not talking to them. Let them just listen. You who are called the old-timers don't pay attention to this at all. That is indeed a matter of great pain and sorrow. What is told to you as soon as you come? There is a karmic residue behind us, worshipped and made to be worshipped by our ancestors. It is coming and attacking us. We are the remnants of a corrupted karmic residue that manifests as disease, poverty, demonic children, various violent tendencies, and those who never fit in with the family. It would be a wonder only if we didn't have all this. How should we obey this? How to adapt to it? All this was explained to you before the Gurupooja was done. Or else, you don't have to do it. There are people here for two to four years who still haven't done Gurupooja. They are not allowed to do Gurupooja. What do you think that means? Let someone older here speak.

[GV4:P1363] Disciple: Does it mean it should be done only after gaining that maturity?

[GV4:P1364] Guru: You are not able to. For how long have I been teaching this. We have realized that the flaw of what was done is within us. Then why can't it be done? We say in a word that it is due to the lack of the meritorious aspect (punya) of the soul. That is true. But, are you gathering the strength to assume that you don't need this merit anymore? How will you understand that? The meritorious aspect is needed. How is that? Should God give the merit?

[GV4:P1365] Disciple: It is the fruit of karma that is being experienced.

[GV4:P1366] Guru: Then, where will the children born again be, when your karma is standing flawed like this? If you do not behave carefully regarding this, no one can do anything. I did many things and explained many things properly. But if only this matter is told to them, they will not obey. Because you do not act with knowledge, how many mistakes have occurred because when a karma is done and things get straightened out, you don't obey and the family doesn't maintain it? There are countless. There are so many people in here now! Should I do this and be ruined like this, or is it enough if you ruin yourselves, or should everyone be ruined together? You must give an answer to that.

[GV4:P1367] Disciple: No one should be ruined.

[GV4:P1368] Guru: Indeed. But, what is it like? Can it be achieved through your unnecessary actions? Your children were not born in that way. What is it? You are the type of people who offer vows and offerings to God to get things done. How lowly you are, trying to win God over by giving offerings. Why are you keeping quiet? I am asking, what is the special virtue residing inside that intellect which thinks it can gain things by giving vows and offerings to God?

[GV4:P1369] Disciple: Isn't that how parents have taught us?

[GV4:P1371] Disciple: We don't have the capability.

If there is any opportunity, you interject your intellect, insert something else into it, and from within it, you hold on to every embodiment of ignorance that revels there. Nothing can be done. You do not even desire a truthful life. What to do? Even if you have the desire, it is like this. You cannot do it. You don't know what it is. This itself is our flaw. Has this happened to one family, one caste, or one religion, or is it present in all human beings? Is this present only in our India right now? Do you believe that this exists and is taking effect in us?

[GV4:P1373] Disciple: Yes.

[GV4:P1374] Guru: It is not enough if only one person speaks. If any of you have any theories of rationalism or liberation, you should state them. After demonstrating liberation-theories, rationalism, and nonsense, and then when paralysis strikes, you just surrender to it. Is it not so? What have you assumed? In the realm of knowledge, you are getting nowhere. Whatever has come down to you from the state, all of that is a course of action that ruins you and this world. What is the state like in that regard? The state is an ignorance that twists the perspective of the nation for the sake of caste, for religion, and for temporary needs, only to stab the people in the back. Apart from further increasing this ignorance time and again, are you capable of doing anything else? You are all smart. If asked why you are smart, you would not know. To you, this seems like a new matter, and you keep shifting aimlessly without reaching anywhere. How are the greatest writers? How are the greatest thinkers? In all such ways. Likewise, whoever it is, every tramp out there has ended up like this. What do you have to say in response to this? Are not each of you the ignorance taught by a doctrine that has forgotten to be humble or to show respect with love? Or are we all standing apart from all that? So, each one of us is eagerly taking up the culmination of the lowest kind of life that has crept in through ignorance, lack of experience, and habit. None of you wants to improve. Or is it that you act with the assumption, "Let illness come to me, no matter what happens, I will only do this"? If anyone has anything to say about that, let them speak. As far as we are concerned, for every thinking creature, or anyone wishing to grow—not just humans, but for all—this is a great destruction scattered like a storm. What do you feel like saying? You speak. I have asked you in various ways many times. But you will not say it. Either keeping quiet like those who know, or keeping quiet like those who do not know, or engaging in karma that perishes after attaining intellect—I cannot understand what it is. If elderly people like that mother ask this, I do not answer. Why? Because if told, they have reached an age where they can neither grasp it, follow it, nor impart it. What do these elderly mothers tell us? "We have done everything we had to do. Now do as you please. If necessary, I will just walk out." Where to? To take up asceticism (*Sanyasa*). Then do one thing. Just let all the elderly people go. Let them go away from our houses. At least they will not trouble the house, right? They will go their own way. Then they are going to sing that they have nothing. How much ignorance is assumed when saying this. It is the ignorance that comes when asceticism and family life (*Grihasthashrama*) mature. There are our ancestors who matured in asceticism. What is to be done? So, what we have assumed is that asceticism is a weapon to be taken up when all strength is gone and the nerves refuse to straighten. How did such lowly desires come among us? That is it; if it is known that someone went to an ashram, it is a quarrel. What did you understand? Did you not understand that it is the remnant of bad progeny? Did you not realize that these children are the amassed personification of ignorance, unable to distinguish what an ashram is, what a *grihasthashrama* is, what a *brahmachari* is, what a *karmi* is, or what a *jnani* is? We are the mothers belonging to this category. Right? What can be gained from this mother? Even then, the stubbornness remains the same. Which is? Let people hear the mother say that the children are the ones who do not give her water. One meaning is like that. Another meaning is, "Just like so-and-so's mother and father walked out, I will also go away, listen." That is another remnant of this. So, look at how the knowledge formed by the culmination of ignorance in this state resides in us. And then, after hiding under some flag or banana tree or in the paddy for a few days without being caught by the police, escaping from their hands, polishing himself up and wearing a shirt, parading as a leader, and bringing the third generation coming after him into this nonsense—such are the parents of today. When I speak the truth of this, you should be able to say it as it is. Speak. It seems no one here has brought their tongue. Having lived and learned so badly like compasses pointing north and compasses pointing west just to raise these children so wretchedly, who can reform you? I can say whatever I want. That is why I am scrubbing and washing you like this. I am peeling you. Even so, if I see that your mind grasps it somewhere, that is good. Speak, they sit here without a tongue, nose, or head. For our mother and father to be in this state, we must understand what their ancestors had made them believe. Having raised them and transferred the incompetence of merely pampering the children, they have become mothers and fathers. Is it true? Even after aging like this skin, to protect these children, they possess an ignorance that overrides their intellect.

[GV4:P1377] What can be earned behind the interpretation of letters

[GV4:P1378] There is a karma I have been performing for so long. The pain is that not even a handful of households have realized and adopted this. It is not due to a lack of experience. Let them say that they are not obeying it because of a lack of experience. They are people without inclination or innate nature. This is the reason. You cannot buy this from a market. You can only handle this if you have the sense of dharma to imbibe it through your life. Otherwise, there is no point in you doing this. You will not gain anything either. I am saying this out of sorrow. In your home, where you speak of your wife, children, mother, and father, you live bearing the misfortune of being unable to impart it to them. Having understood this, you should do something; children, there is a karma that is shared with our lives—have this father, mother, or others been able to tell you what to do for it? [GV4:P1406] That which is known in the witness of Waking, Dreaming, and Deep Sleep

By understanding this, we must recognize the hardships, glory, respect, humility, wickedness, and righteousness inherent in our own lives. Isn't that so? It is there that one must truly understand what one's Guru is. You must definitively decide whether you want this or not. Therefore, if we are to draw closer to this essential realization we desire, do we not also require the experiential familiarity to observe where the snow transformed into rain, solidified into ice, melted back into water, and ultimately, where it reached?

[GV4:P1410] Where was it in the ancient times? Without anyone making it, this snow was present here. This is the brilliance of nature. Then it melted as snow, and to be cut away, it became hard enough and it melted and thus the water body rose. It rose through the water body and became water itself. Whatever it had to mix with, it mixed and there is a story where it submerged Dwarka. So it is about that state. Such a great man, that is why a Guru is needed. By denying the Guru, if any matters are spoken at any time, that matter is gone. Then it cannot be retrieved. If one thinks of getting it through that logic! The one who is sitting in the tragic state of not being able to recognize his own father, how can he analyze this logically? Only if I talk a lot of nonsense like this will you understand. Did the mother say it was the father, or did the father say it was the father? So couldn't this just be said normally? In this state, how else can I scold you? Right or wrong? This is what happens in my house. I don't know what happens in your house. So, because of the familiarity of such a pathetic acquaintance itself, we must believe that there is a lack of knowledge in us. Thus, maintaining this ignorance, and pointing out that it doesn't exist, the Guru brings us to that extent. At the time of our birth, we were not familiarized by being told about such matters. What we have heard and kept is what our father, mother, and ancestors have said--isn't a vision of God enough? It is on the outside of this specific ignorance that we stand. Not a hundred of these. Even if a thousand appear, we gain nothing. Even if a crore appear, nothing happens. The one who makes us capable of offering our soul through the soul is the true spiritual Guru. If you have any doubt, you can ask. You must know it. That is why I am saying this. Do not go with doubts. Now, didn't I see yesterday; I slept well yesterday, I felt very good last night, sleep; isn't there a lack of knowledge communicated in our hands like this? So now I told someone else that I slept well yesterday. If I say I didn't experience it, what will we do? Isn't it I who knows whether I slept or not? So the feeling of 'I' is there. That 'I' is what saw everything, existing in a form not different from oneself, with the nature of evolution, the dharma existing in this literal nature, the action of the form of this sound. Should we get back this humility or not? That is, this sound we hear mutually now, do you realize that it has merged into this atmosphere or not? Just like that, is there any doubt that this nature took a photo of all of us sitting and talking together? Just like this, our ancestors worshiped and made others worship, mixing the bad and the good, true worship and the untrue reality, shouldn't we realize this? A remnant of the life that acted mingled and forgotten, known and unknown for so long, is this life sticking to my body, shouldn't we know this? Or shouldn't we? So this knowledge can only be gained through the Guru. So whichever deity or whichever demon is seen, my Guru must be there. What is the doubt? You must ask about the part you have a doubt. Only then can I say. If I make you mature through my words and make you ask, what can I do? Shouldn't you be the one in need? So, if one says this is not it, this is not it--if a toddy seller is given the water from old gruel, will it become toddy? Its color will somewhat match. So milk is white, this is also white. And then there is a slight difference in their form changes. Shouldn't we distinguish this? So it is about this matter that needs to be known that we are asking. This cannot be known unless our house is right. If one becomes a Guru like this, who goes along with every rowdyism and every good thing by habit, how would it be? When I say this, you will think, alas, did he say that about the Guru? This is how the Guru is. A complete rogue. So whatever rogue behaviour is seen, I see my Guru along with it. Why does one say it should be seen like this? Thus, it is the path the Guru passed through that we are shown. When the Guru and that seen form dissolve together, as to what one becomes, fourthly if it is this one--take and place it. Then showing us an amorphous nature in this nature of what stands dissolved and undissolved, in this formless being, one must show us as true law what resides in it. The item without form. Through this formless being what was done? If we do not see this through the Guru too, how will you see it? It won't happen. For this, you need a Guru. What kind of Guru should it be? Only if good things are heard, will the Guru sit there. If bad things are heard, the Guru will leave. If bad things are seen or heard, the Guru will run away from there. Then who will separate the bad and the good from you? If there is any space for that, tell me. A formless power that knows and informs that your mind is not lost or corrupted and not bad in another way, shouldn't you see it as a form in yourself? He is formless. But he is formed. Through whatever that formed being went--this too is being shown to us. That is waking state, dream ṭ 'whatever was seen in the waking state' in dream and then in deep sleep, and after that the special quality of these form differences and name differences is what Turiya, Turiyaateetam show. Waking, dreaming, deep sleep, Turiya, Turiyaateetam; turning us around with these five parts, the skill in action is the Guru. During the time of the deity, what was the deity, what did the sage do there, that sage who is called the doer of action, yogi, knowledgeable one, devotee--turned in four ways who are these sages, what is the connection between this sage and my Guru? Or how do those good qualities of all the past deities reside in my Guru? Like saying this Shakteam, Shaivam, Vaishnavam, singing with a thousand hands and showing a role, we call it Bhadra. But shouldn't we see the true quality of Durga? Recognizing the qualities of this life without gender distinction is our Guru's acquaintance. If one says this is not it, I have nothing to say. I can go from here. What do you say? This must come into our experience. That is what I said, I am not training the children brought from my house for this. This is being trained on your children, your husband, and your wife. This is the love of trust in the Guru that flows through you to your children, and from those children to their children, to an enduring state, showing what was there and what wasn't, being poured into you. Say yes or no. But this is all I have to say. Everything stands strong in this nature at a formless place where one's Guru takes it and shows it. It is this Guru who characterizes what that constant power of the past era is, and by making us know it, goes forward again. This cannot be done by the deity. The deity will show some rolling and manipulation. This is not some manipulation and rolling. Shouldn't we know what the evolutionary theory of our life force is by seeing it and knowing through what all we have crawled and climbed up? Isn't it through your soul that you have to see it? So the soul sitting along with the life force in this body, the knowledge that is known by reflecting both, isn't it true knowledge? The question is whether you believe there is a soul and a life force in us itself. If we do not have in front of us an action path to retrieve it and show it in ourselves, we will wander bewildered anywhere. Understand this from experience. This <span200>is belief.</span200>

[GV4:P1411] Let us tell only the Guru, and no one else, about what we experience in the waking, dream, and deep sleep states. Why am I seeing so much bad? Why am I seeing so much good? How wayward am I? Why have I been placed in this seat of ignorance? — The Guru is the authority to ask such questions. Now, what is the doubt? Do you believe it or not?

[GV4:P1412] Disciple: I believe.

[GV4:P1413] Guru: Believe like that. Here it is, how did you feel after applying the sacred ash?

[GV4:P1414] Disciple: It was better.

[GV4:P1415] Guru: When we take some medicine, doesn't it aggravate in another way instead of subsiding? How did you feel when you applied this sacred ash? It subsided. So, who is the sorcerer here? It is our faith. Transcending all this, it is a self-offering that unites one's life and breath. Not to spout great Vedanta or say it was like this in the Kathopanishad; I am not talking nonsense. Is their experience what is written down? I did not say that to deny or interpret any of it. There is no need to interpret anything here. It is what it is. If it is not convenient for you, learn it from somewhere else, or take it, boil it, and eat it. That is all. When I say this, you will not like me. Why? I am an unlearned man, one who does nothing, and a great trickster. After explaining so much trickery, what a disgrace it is to call me an unlearned trickster. I am stating both together. 'Jagrat swapna sushuptinam sakshimurthy namonamah' — Guru is the karma sustained by our household, myself, and one's lineage, encompassing what we have worshipped as a witness in this, what we have failed to worship, the bad, the evil, the good, what we experienced knowingly or unknowingly, and what came by special destiny.

[GV4:P1416] Guruvani

[GV4:P1417] Birthday Tribute Edition - 2006

[GV4:P1418] The Guru speaking to the devotees from Palakkad.

[GV4:P1419] Take Palakkad for instance. The problem seen there is the result of what they have been worshipping, believing it to be a good path. The difficulty we might face by worshipping in such a way is that it will stagnate within our life. They will not respect anything. They will not step forward to do anything. Consequently, their children will grow up with wealth, riches, and enjoyment. But these children will fall into danger. They do not realize this. There are many such households. This problem exists in every house that shows off such arrogance. Aren't they flaunting their wealth and authority? It is present in all these houses. Nothing can be done about it. This is because of the mistakes that occurred in this outdated system of worship. Now we have faith. Can we avoid proceeding with that faith? We cannot change that fact. Then how should it be? We must investigate it like this. If we continue doing this for eight, ten, fifteen, or twenty years, the very course of this life will turn into that. Right? If it goes on like this, we will end up being ignorant of yoga, karma, devotion, or any other path of knowledge. One must understand this first. Otherwise, we will be in trouble. It is good. Everything is good. But then, if a little education, wealth, and authority come into our house, they will not respect anyone. They will simply lack a respectful nature. When will they eventually return? It will be in their old age, when they are entirely fed up with these children. Then they will start crying out, 'Oh God, Oh God, Oh God'. There will be no saving them. These children will scatter in different directions. This is the entire situation in Palakkad. Ah, did you see them? A nest of Ezhuthachans. Isn't there a community of people called Ezhuthachans there? Most of them suffer from mental deficiencies.

[GV4:P1420] Disciple: It is there in many families.

[GV4:P1421] Guru: Will the locals believe it if I say this now? This is not what I am saying. You remember what I told you when we came here that day. That innate tendency (vasana) will not enter their life. If the vasana does not manifest in life, we cannot grasp it. Consequently, many youths are simply wasting away on this path. When this happens among the youth, one group takes that trajectory. Suppose there are five members in our household. Three or four of them are on different paths. One is on a virtuous path. These four will dislike him. Whether male or female, they stubbornly stand their ground amidst this chaos. We cannot make them obedient in any circumstance. Humility is simply not imparted. Their inner selves remain rigidly blocked. Therefore, if a transformation is to occur, shouldn't an action that engenders humility arise within us? What shall we do if this humility does not emerge? If we attempt to induce it forcefully, it will merely push them to the brink of destruction. Ultimately, we can never save that family. Then there is a faction devoted to rationalism and spiritual liberationism. They pose as significant figures in both ideologies. This is the prevalent observation throughout the Palakkad region, starting from Ottapalam. Thus, upon understanding this, one realizes that this is entirely the residue of deep-rooted vasanas. How can we transform this entrenched vasana? Even if one desires to do so, it cannot be changed. You must understand it in that manner. Why is it said that it will not change? You are all artists, aren't you? This artistic vasana remains with them even if they face failure; they will not abandon it. There are numerous such individuals. Many have been lost. Individuals who deviated like this in a family are reborn in a state influenced by an ancestral spirit that perished elsewhere. They will never deviate from that path. Simultaneously, there is one's inherent vasana, which will frequently surge forth. For instance, just as I mentioned regarding Ezhuthachan, there are countless petty writers. They are always humming and wandering about. How many such individuals have truly prospered? They cannot; they will not improve. Thus, observing this, we fail to comprehend the trajectory of our karma. None of you should harbor the illusion that we can progress without exhausting this karma. It will not happen. Wealth, capabilities, and prosperity may grace a generation, and they might live a commendable life. However, within them, the contemplation of the Divine may be present in some, while entirely absent in others. For some, it is quite different; they aspire to become sheer brutes. It continues like this. Despite possessing intellect and ability, they veer off in this direction. I am asking you how this can be resolved. You should perceive what I am saying as reflecting the ignorance of your mind. Shouldn't I express it? It is inappropriate for me to conceal this truth. It is like chanting 'Narayana' only until crossing the bridge, and then reverting to the old ways. Such is the state of the mind. I am explaining this so that you do not have to suffer in the end due to a lack of understanding. If you approach me, I will speak only in this manner. I do not seek your affection. What do I require? I desire the magnificence of your spiritual growth. If you are to attain that greatness, you cannot proceed in this manner. I am merely explaining its nature. What is occurring now? Take the children of officers here; if there are four children, all four are sent for tuition! Why is that? If a single mark is lost, the mother's mind becomes agitated, akin to moss gathered and stuffed into a basket. If moss is packed tightly into a basket, it ferments and generates intense heat, doesn't it? Her mind burns similarly. This is improper. Some women come and lament, 'I have nine children, Swami. Seven of them are officers, both boys and girls. But two children—what can be done? One daughter failed a section and tried three times with no success.' Did they lie? No. 'No matter what the other child does, there is no progress.' What does this signify? There are wonderful children in this house. Many have secured employment. Yet, she is a mother incapable of teaching them the true essence of life, do you understand? She provides milk, serves food, washes their clothes, and refuses to let the children do any chores. When situations demand it, these children—some of whom are quite unruly—will wander down whatever path they please. Rather than letting them face consequences, the parents quickly cover it up, pamper them, and cater to their whims, don't they? I am pointing out the mischievous folly committed by such parents. What will be their state when they grow up? This represents the household. You will find yourselves utterly helpless. This is the consequence of pursuing various misguided forms of devotion. You are unaware of it. This phenomenon is quite evident from Ottapalam onwards. You can verify this in every household. Consider the Brahmin streets; if there are twenty houses clustered together, you will undoubtedly find two widows there. What can be done?

[GV4:P1422] Look at Ernakulam. The fundamental question is how we can comprehend all of this. Upon understanding it, regarding our ancestors—nobody deceived or destroyed anyone. It is an inherent misfortune residing within that soul. This soul will remain in such a state. You all assume, 'We are Grihasthashramis (householders); we are simply surviving somehow.' To be a true Grihasthashrami, unless they cultivate complete wisdom, prosperity, and competence, they will end up begging after one thing or another. What does this mean? What are your thoughts on this? This supplication should not exist. A Grihasthashrami implies a person who possesses the capability to lead their household and community in a pure and righteous manner. That is why it is said that society requires wealthy individuals, affluent people; otherwise, a place devoid of noble souls (sadhukkal) is considered desolate. What is meant by 'noble souls'?

[GV4:P1423] Disciple: Those who correct errors upon observing them.

[GV4:P1424] Guru: Exactly. If an error is spotted and corrected, shouldn't they rectify their course? What is the method for that?

[GV4:P1425] Disciple: Humility is essential.

[GV4:P1426] Guru: That humility is not present in his father, is it? Then what is he to do? Furthermore, our mothers have another trait. Speaking with great authority, they say, 'Narayana, God will take care of all that.' What is it? Haven't they entrusted it to God? Mother and father live like this in nature, living with all their character flaws and whatever else they have accumulated, and then for a few days, they will fervently call out to God. Then they will say, 'I have done whatever I needed to. If you want, you do it. I can't anymore.' Then there is a mother with even more knowledge than that. What is that? 'I gave birth to ten. I experienced such and such sorrows. You gave birth to one or two and became like this. What am I to do?' That is a kind of knowledge. You are getting the mother's knowledge in a solid form. Isn't that enough? When they became modernized, they won't even say that. See? The others would at least say that much. So, like that, the duty our mothers had to take up with humility was not given to them when they were little children. Did you understand what was said? Their mother and father raised them, got them married as best as they could, and they became children, children's children, husband and wife. Seeing this in many houses and seeing this English medium too, all of them got shaken and went another way. If you talk about a householder (Grihasthashrami), he is someone who should be an absolute model for this world. Otherwise, one should not wander like beggars and accept the householder stage. Then there is another thing shown, taking sannyasa (renunciation) at the time they are about to be destroyed and turned into ashes. They take the Bhagavatam and hum it, hum and study it for a few days, then they end up in a temple, then in a wayside inn. Now there are no wayside inns. That is a pity, isn't it? What is a wayside inn? In those days there were no vehicles or boats--if you go by boat, this thing won't work out. So they would pack their bags and set out. If they had to come to Thiruvananthapuram, they set out after packing their bags. They would sleep in these wayside inns and reach Thiruvananthapuram in ten days. So, we shouldn't just feel happy thinking about those times. It is all good for us. Now we don't need wayside inns. No roadside wells. No resting places for headloads. Do we? So we are born in a place where all these things are not needed. What did you understand? Life has become easy. So, I am telling you to look at that sorrow. If we had to deliver a thing to the town, look at the experience, difficulty, and trouble of those days. There is a hundred acres of land on the hill. Will you farm it and pick it up by hand? They do not understand the fact that things have become so easy now. You never even think like this. What to do? So, is the time we are born in better? Or is that better? The time we are born in is better. In the old days, if one house had education, the ten houses around it wouldn't have education. Do you know that? Suppose they get a letter in English. How will they read it? Then they have to walk somewhere for it. In the time of C. Kesavan and others, he was the 33rd B.A. holder in Travancore ٹ C. Kesavan and Sahodaran Ayyappan. We understood that it was only that much, didn't we? You can see that if you look at the Kochi souvenir.

[GV4:P1428] September 2006

[GV4:P1429] Right now, theology and all religious doctrines are being taught. Aren't there people who have studied this? Then why are you specifically teaching it now? Is it not because it cannot be put into practice here? How can it be attained by merely speaking of its valor? That is not possible. That great soul must come, grow, and grasp the history of that domain right from its beginning. After doing so, without giving that great soul their due, we cannot move forward. You do not understand this. We are taking responsibility for the errors that have crept into this prophetic religion. Thus, we are taking upon ourselves these two thousand four hundred and forty-four Gurus as well. After taking them, we must make them function. What did you understand from this? This is why seven generations have been mentioned, for them to come and act. Isn't that what I said when speaking about vision (darshan)? The time of all of them has passed. Whose time? That of all the successors. However, in this position, a few years of the Prophet (Nabi) still remain. I do not know if you have understood that. It has been one thousand five hundred years since he arrived. Only a few more days remain for that. The word spoken by that great soul must not be broken. Shouldn't they be capable of ensuring that word is not broken? But if the era of that great soul passes, then you will not be able to grasp it later. What is it? It must be grasped within this time frame itself. When we pray, we will connect with all the traditionally existing constellations of stars for that purpose. Different levels of importance are assigned to each one. After receiving this vision, it is being handed over to a Guru capable of bearing it. We must take it back ourselves. To practically implement it among the people through action, a distinct personality is required. Therefore, we must adopt the karma of this lineage of Gurus who have come and gone until now, right down to the 'Ustad'. Otherwise, if we go the other way, things will get complicated. It is the lack of time to grasp this that stands as a roadblock for Sri Krishna and the aforementioned Prophet. This is not something anyone can deny. It is a historical truth. This is not how the scholars put it. They are talking about some other convoluted theories. We must respect whoever has come and gone, wherever they may have been. We should not deny them. If we are not to deny them, we must embrace their karma. There is no other justification for it. We cannot proceed without clearing the path for them. That operates through the grace of God. So, if we attain a Guru or a guide, only when we reach that point and look from there can we see the rest. Therefore, it is like climbing a mountain. One must climb one, see its end, get down, and likewise climb up and down seven folds to accomplish the task. Narayana Guru gives many examples for this.

[GV4:P1430] 'There is medicine on the mountain, three snakes and

[GV4:P1431] tigers standing guard on both its sides,

[GV4:P1432] an outcaste took and consumed half of it,

[GV4:P1433] it still shines, oh mind, you too take it!'

[GV4:P1434] This is understood. But what to do? It did not come into this doctrine of karma. It is not enough to speak of the doctrine of dharma. The doctrine of karma must come. This is what is called experiential realization. When that realization later enters the realm of utilization, upon attaining it, we can only say that we have attained it. But it becomes true knowledge only when it is utilized for the people. Calling it a vision (darshan), they recite Vedantic hymns—their stance is that the vision is wrong. If this vision is wrong, why did the name 'darshan' even originate? Isn't darshan the dynamic course of action that distinguishes between what is and what is not! Who says it does not exist? What will happen if one speaks all sorts of nonsense, talks of literal knowledge, makes corrections using vowels and consonants, and merely performs intellectual gymnastics within the theory of Yoga? You will feel bad when I say this. It is a painful matter. I am speaking from my knowledge. Hindus have a limitation, Islam has a limitation, and similarly, all these mentioned visions have a limitation. It is when you go there that you see the predicament. No one will understand this even if they hear or see it. This is my experience. A system called fulfillment existed here. The word was received. Certain things must be done. They were done. It is not the Vedantic vision spoken of in logic. Is there any need to conduct mimamsa (critical investigation) here that eliminates dharma by bringing Vedanta into mere alphabetical knowledge? The result of that inner vision is, 'What is this, father, that you have shown me?' If these knowledgeable religious theorists fail to understand this, what can we do? Time is simply being wasted. It is about what needs to be done to prevent that from happening. That is the topic I must tell you along with the beginning of the Kali Yuga. Whether anyone asks or not, I will say this. The reason is that we lack the karma of imparting and absorbing love in the act of communicating face-to-face. Who are we telling this to? Who is being made to hear this? What is being said here? Aren't all these theorists speaking as if they came to praise and glorify a mistake? Do not adopt that theoretical approach. That is all I have to say to the people of this world. I have nothing else to say. Who am I to tell? I am merely conveying to you the sorrow that I have experienced.

[GV4:P1435] Disciple: We have only one religion. The religion of love. We cannot attain salvation through any other religion.

[GV4:P1436] Guru: It will never be possible. I have nothing to say to those who think it is possible. We have insulted the Gurus who showed us what that love is. Isn't this the truth? Now, if anyone has anything to say, let them say it. This is my experience that I am sharing. Then, God assigned a specific time period to each one. That is what we know now. Two thousand for one, five thousand for another, ten thousand for yet another—we do not receive any knowledge beyond what is said in this manner.

[GV4:P1438] October 2006

[GV4:P1439] It is the Yuga Dharma (the duty of the age) that we must understand. There is no point in presenting something without observing what must be observed in that particular era. Is this not our tradition? Have we not been born? Where will you go to correct yourselves now? We only have a very short lifespan. When looking at the grand vision of time, we do not exist even as a mere atom. What will we do here? This is where the truth lies. The knowledge of this doctrine, which pervades both the atomic and the infinite, must begin from the point it has reached. Otherwise, things will not be right. There is nothing to be gained by simply wandering here and there. That is just teaching people foolishness. It is not honesty. We have pushed out onto the veranda the standard of love established by our ancestors. This is the question the Prophet asked. They do not know this. None of us knows it either. All the Mahatmas who have come before and after have strayed from this Yuga Dharma and blocked the path. I do not know if one can study this deeply and say that fish and meat can be consumed together. You are all educated people. I am uneducated. Each of us is left out of the corridor of this sectarian trend, which makes us very sad. What will happen if we do not all feel that this is regrettable? If understanding that is our goal, love must be at the forefront. The respect for that love is required. You also need the wisdom to receive it with humility. Otherwise, it will not be Dharma; it will become Adharma. I respected that experience because, at one time, Mahatmas with all visions spoke of the greatness of scholars in that manner. However, scholars have also come. I am not saying they haven't. Within these five thousand years, many known Mahatmas have come. But the demonic vision they speak of is the remnant of the wicked deeds standing in their practical realm. Do not feel bad when I say this. It is a mistake that can happen to them. It is indeed a wicked deed. We understand this when these Mahatmas come one by one; I will not stand by my knowledge or acquaintance. This is where this calculation is told. We must see all these mentioned Mahatmas without exception. We must grasp that aspect of where they went wrong in their practical realm. Regardless, we cannot reject them and put something else in their place. How it is, we can speak in terms of the countless crores of people who believed and obeyed them, but a crore is not a magnitude here. If we do not accept their decadence, there is no other way. We cannot say it. We can say it, but we should not. You can only proceed by rejecting them. When we accept them, we are taking on that part. We have to experience it. That is one reason you asked. The youths who have come to me so far do not understand it at all.

[GV4:P1440] Among them, only this Pai spoke a truth. Dr. Pai. How many years ago? Eight years ago. This is not a disease worth mentioning. Then I will give you medicine. If I do not experience this, there is another flaw. You will not be able to move forward. You can discard it as unwanted. Shouldn't we see it in the practical action combined with blood, flesh, and marrow? It is not there. I haven't told any of this to anyone here until now. So, seeing what happened to that Mahatma, we should not intellectualize that action but explain it. Are we to intellectualize it and hand it over to the scientists? When I say this, it becomes too much. They cannot do it. The illustrative experience for that is the very science you speak of. Where science hits a dead end, there stands God. If I tell them all this now, won't they mock me? Since you have no way to proceed, I said this to clear a path. The most difficult thing in this world is the action that our ancestors worshipped and made others worship. There is also no knowledge to sustain it. So, it is for this reason that the words spoken are indicated. Seeing this in detail is why it was asked, 'What are you doing to me, man?'

[GV4:P1441] Disciple: The Prophet had to lament like that in the end.

[GV4:P1442] Guru: That is what we must take into account. It is exactly this. The question asked, 'Father, have you forsaken me?' Why did you throw me among these demons? That is the sorrow. If there is no solution to this sorrow, there will be no solution to anything. When I say this, some will like it. If they like it, let them. Anyway, things won't work out just because you like it. Because my lifetime is just a fraction of an atom, isn't it? If I discard even this atom and leave, where will I go? We cannot take anything with us without this. The ultimate truth of a human being is love. If that love is without respect, it is not love. This is where it was lost. We need a person to figure out the path of that love. That is what was said. That is, as far as we are concerned, we should be able to carry this forward. But we can show it to them. Everyone in every religion has said that it will happen. None of them said it merely for the literal meaning of the words. Then what is so special about saying they have said it? It was said after completely gathering all this. This is the benefit of working in this intellectual realm. What will we do here? Once you understand this, there is no need to worry about us at all. That is the only proof I can give you.

[GV4:P1443] Guruvani

[GV4:P1445] The author of the Gita has spoken of that special intellect to ponder how many eras have passed. We must respect that. All this running was done ultimately to fulfill that. Understood? Now, the path Jesus ran and the Prophet ran—didn't all these mentioned Mahatmas run? They ran to fulfill it. But they could not. Didn't we make it run from here? Where did it stop? Didn't it go and stop in another continent? Having gone there, wasn't this Dwaraka finished? Look at that Dwaraka even today, isn't it in the calculations? It is. That is one thing told to Arjuna. You take these children and women and save them. There is no other way now. So Sri Krishna, having told Arjuna what to do for this and having shown him, took him along. That is why the disciple was taken along; he was taken to repeatedly fulfill that disciple. What happened when they went there? It was an era where we could not identify the boundary of this action bridging the Yugas. So, Kali Yuga is this many years, Treta Yuga is this many years, Dvapara is this many years, and these three combined is Satya Yuga. Isn't this how we have been convinced? But what can be said about what lies in between this? Shouldn't it cross from one to another? How much time did that take? Is there such a condition? What should we do in this condition?

[GV4:P1446] Disciple: When that change happens, it will become a beneficial change.

[GV4:P1447] Guru: Yes. Is it enough if we just imagine it to be beneficial?

[GV4:P1448] Disciple: We must naturally accept it. Water will turn into steam in that temporary state at a hundred degrees.

[GV4:P1449] Guru: Yes. After becoming steam, won't it become water again? What is the recourse for that?

[GV4:P1450] Disciple: That is the transformation of energy.

[GV4:P1452] Disciple: It will become water.

[GV4:P1453] Guru: Where will it go? It will return. So that is it. That is exactly what was said. You give some parallel. I find nothing special in it. Is there such a thing or not? How can what exists be destroyed? Where will one go to destroy it?

[GV4:P1454] Disciple: What exists can neither be destroyed nor created.

[GV4:P1455] Guru: If we start speaking transcendently about such a state, where will we stand?

[GV4:P1457] Guru: When every religious doctrine, karma doctrine, and yoga doctrine were combined, the exact condition changed. What has been divided into four epochs has manifested as this Yoga, Karma, Jnana, and Bhakti. According to the capacity of the jiva (soul), one can ascend through them. However, without recognizing the level at which the jiva's capacity stands, one simply practiced yoga, performed karma, or practiced bhakti and departed. It is not his fault. That is what he is within the society. Isn't it? How would he know? By what means would he know? Thus, it was first declared, "Vāsanamayam jagat sarvam" (The entire universe is infused with latent tendencies). Not just our entirety, did you understand? It means not entrusting total liberation to just one entity. Assigning knowledge, fortune, and significance to different epochs was a mistake. Herein lies the Yugantara Dharma (the duty across epochs). Who is to state this, who is to see it, and who is to undertake it?

[GV4:P1458] Disciple: Isn't practicing the dharma of the respective epoch (yuga) the only thing that can be done?

[GV4:P1459] Guru: That is true, but about this epoch — one person says five thousand. Another says two lakhs, yet another claims it is even more. Another person asserts it is over four lakhs. Then another states it as eight thousand or nine thousand. It goes on like that, mentioning figures beyond four lakhs, nine lakhs, and sixteen lakhs. What can be done about this? Do we face such an entanglement before us?

[GV4:P1460] Disciple: Yes.

[GV4:P1462] Disciple: Yes.

[GV4:P1463] Guru: Then is there a God (Deva)? Is there a prophet?

[GV4:P1464] Disciple: Yes.

[GV4:P1465] Guru: Is there not a designated period for the Guru?

[GV4:P1466] Disciple: Yes.

[GV4:P1467] Guru: Then isn't there a Kala Dharma (duty of the times)?

[GV4:P1468] Disciple: Yes.

[GV4:P1469] Guru: What should be done here?

[GV4:P1470] Disciple: In each Kala Dharma, does not that jiva function in accordance with its individual nature?

[GV4:P1471] Guru: It can only function in that manner. Thus, we stand beneath the visionary who emerged through the beliefs or customs shaped by the jiva's past actions.

[GV4:P1472] Disciple: Is not one continuously born into the very state that one has attained?

[GV4:P1473] Guru: When you say being born... Didn't we say earlier that it will turn into water again?

[GV4:P1474] Disciple: If it becomes water, isn't it becoming water while waiting for completeness?

[GV4:P1475] Guru: Yes. What doubt is there about that?

Isn't it the evolutionary state of the jiva? Wasn't it said that it should cease to exist? We have not seen to what extent that goes. One should speak only if one has seen it. Then, which skies does this evolutionary state belong to? That is this Nalukettu (traditional four-part structure). There are also those who say, 'He who hasn't built ten is a pig'. Let him build it. When practicing all these yoga methods, I am speaking in your language. So there is this Nalukettu. Shouldn't we know what it was tied with and what broke it? So this is how we must understand it. The reason is that specific doctrines were brought and bound upon us without knowing the duration of the yuga dharmas. We have not received the correction regarding what the dharma is to retrieve what has come and gone. We must understand it. So, if we cross the four skies, we must articulate what the dharma is that crosses the seven realms (Bhumikas) that are mentioned. Would yogis disbelieve that?
